The period of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) passed like this, and when Hadhrat Umar (RA) became the Khalifah afterwards, he also used to summon these men. When Hadhrat Umar (RA) was the Khalifah, the task of issuing Fataawaa was entrusted to Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA), Hadhrat Ubay (RA) and Hadhrat Zaid (RA).
sources: Tabraani. Haythami Pg. 1 32) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Ubaydah reports that Uyayna bin Hisn and Aqra bin Haabis once approached Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) saying, "O successor of Rasulullaah ﷺ There is a barren piece of land in our area that bears no grass and is useless, if you see it fit, do make it over to us so that we may work on it and cultivate it." Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) decided to make it over to them and had the title deed written in their favour. He appointed Hadhrat Umar (RA) as witness to the deed, but because Hadhrat Umar (RA) was not present there, the two men had to take the deed to him so that he may be witness to it.

When Hadhrat Umar (RA) heard what the deed contained, he took it from the two men, spat on it and thereby erased what was written on it. The two men were infuriated and addressed him with harsh words. Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "Rasulullaah ﷺ used to appease you (by granting you properties) at a time when Islaam was weak. Allaah has now strengthened lslaam (and there is no need to appease you), so you may go and do whatever you can against me. May Allaah offer you no protection even if you ask for in" The two men stormed back to Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) in a fury and said, "By Allaah! We do not know whether the Khalifah is yourself or Umar!" Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) replied, "'In fact he could have been the Khalifah if he chose to."

Hadhrat Umar (RA) then arrived in a rage and when he stood before Hadhrat Abu Bakr. he asked, "Tell me about this land that you handed over to these two men. Does it belong to you or is it the public property of fhe Muslims?" Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) replied, "It is the public property of the Muslims." "Then why did you give it to these two men rather than anyone else from amongst the Muslims?" Hadhrat Umar (RA) demanded to know. Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) replied, "t had consulted with these people around me and they indicated that I do so." Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "Although you consulted with those around you, did you obtain the opinion and consent of every Muslim?" (Because it is not possible to seek the opinion of every person in every matter,) Hadhrat Abu Bakr (chose not to reply to Hadhrat Umar (RA) and rather) said, "J did tell you that you are more capable of Khilaafah than 1 am, but you overpowered me (and forced me to assume the task instead)."
sources: Ibn Abi Shayba, Bukhari in his Taareekii, Ibn Asaakir, Bayhaqi and Ya'qoob bin Sufyaan, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol, 2 Pg.189). The author of isaaba (Vol, 3 Pg.55) and (Vol.l Pg.59) has commented on the chain of narrators. Abdur Razzaaq has also reported the narration, as quoted in Kanzul ummaal Pg.80).' 88 (Vol 2) reply of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) was one that engendered unity), (" Consultation with the Sahabah (RA) in Battle Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr (RA) reports that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) once wrote to Hadhrat Amr bin Ai Aas (RA) saying, "Rasulullaah ﷺ used to consult in matters of war, so ensure that you do the same." A narration of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abi Awfa (RA) has already passed discussing the consultation of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) with men of knowledge before engaging the Romans in battle, ^ Hadhrat Umar (RA) Consults with Men of knowledge Hadhrat Umar (RA) Informs his Consultative Assembly about his Proposal to the Daughter of Hadhrat Ali (RA) Hadhrat Abu Ja'far narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) requested Hadhrat Ali (RA) for his daughter Ummu Kulthoom's hand in marriage. Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "I had intended to marry all my daughters only to the sons of Ja'far." To this, Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "O Ali! Marry her to me because I swear by Allaah that there is no other person on earth who anticipates as much as I do by treating her well (this he explains later)." Hadhrat Ali (RA) then agreed to let Hadhrat Umar (RA) marry his daughter, Hadhrat Umar (RA) then approached the gathering of Muhaajirecn who always sat in the Masjid between the grave of Rasulullaah ﷺ and the pulpit. They included Hadhrat Ali (RA), Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA), Hadhrat Zubayr (RA), Talha (RA) and Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA). whenever any matter presented itself to him from far off places, Hadhrat Umar (RA) would always inform the members of this gathering and then seek their opinions about the matter. This time he came to them and said, "Congratulate me on my new marriage!" They all congratulated him and then asked, "who did you marry, O Ameerul Mu'mineen?" "The daughter of Ali bin Abi Taalib," he replied. He then started lo explain, "Indeed Rasulullaah ﷺ said, 'Every connection and relation shall be severed on the day of Qiyaamah except my connections and my relations.1 I had been a companion of Rasulullaah ﷺ and now I wish to become his relative as well." (4)

paras: Hadhrat Atiyya bin Bilaal and Hadhrat Sahm bin Minjaab both narrate that Aqra and Zabarqaan approached Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) and said, "Hand over to us the Kharaaj from Bahrain and we shall give you the guarantee that no one from our tribe will ever leave Islaam." Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) acceded to the request and wrote a declaration to the effect. Amongst the witnesses appointed was Hadhrat Umar (RA). Since the agreement was facilitated by Hadhrat Talha bin Ubaydullaah, it was he who brought the written agreement to Hadhrat Umar. When Hadhrat Umar (RA) looked at it, he refused to be a witness and exclaimed, "There is no need to honour (appease) people anymore!" He then erased the content and tore it up. Hadhrat Talha (RA) became extremely angry and returned to Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA). saying, "Are you the Ameer or umar?" Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) replied, "He is the Ameer although it is me who has to be obeyed." upon hearing this, Hadhrat Talha (RA) was silent (because while his remark was such that it would have led to disunity, the

Hadhrat Ataa bin Yasaar reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) and Hadhrat uthmaan used to call for Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) and consult with him along with those Sahabah (RA) who participated in the Battle of Badr (the senior Sahabah (RA)). During the periods of Hadhrat Umar and Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA), Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) used to issue Fataawaa (rulings) and did so until he passed away. Hadhrat Ya'qoob bin Zaid narrates that Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab (RA) used to consult with Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) about every matter of importance and would say to him, "Dive into the matter, dear diver (because he was capable of reaching the essence of the problem at hand)," Hadhrat Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas (RA) said, "I have not seen any person as quick-witted, as intelligent, as knowledgeable and as tolerant as Abdullaah bin Abbaas. 1 have seen Umar summon him to solve intricate problems and say, 'An intricate problem has presented itself to you.' Umar would then do only what Abdullaah bin Abbaas proposed even though he was surrounded by Muhaajireen and Ansaar who had participated in the Battle of Hadhrat Ibn Shihaab reports that whenever an intricate problem presented itself before Hadhrat Umar (RA), he would summon some young men to consult and choose to act according to the sharpness of their intellect. Another narration states that Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab (RA) would engage in so much consultation that he would even consult women (when the need arose). In fact, there were several occasions when he liked the opinions that they expressed and acted on it.
sources: ibn Sa'd.

paras: Hadhrat Muhammad, ﷺ and Ziyaad all report that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once left Madinah and dismounted at an oasis called Siraar (3 miles from Madman) where he instructed that the army comes to a halt. The soldiers did not know whether he intended to camp there or proceed further. Whenever the Muslims intended to know something from Hadhrat. Umar (RA), they always sent either Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) or Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA), In fact, during the period of Hadhrat Umar (RA)'s Khilaafah, Hadhrat uthmaan (RA)

Haakim has also reported the narration claiming thai, it is authentic, but Dhahahi has commented on the chain of narrators. was known as "Radeef. According to' the Arabs, a "Radeef is a person who is regarded as the leader's second-in-command and the term is coined for the one whom the people popularly see as the leader's successor. However, whenever these two men were unable to extract from Hadhrat Umar (RA) the information the people required, they would then send Hadhrat Abbaas (RA). Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) then asked Hadhrat Umar (RA), "Has any intelligence reached you? What do you intend doing?" Hadhrat Umar (RA) then announced that the people should gather as they do for salaah and when they had assembled around him, he informed them of the latest intelligence. He then waited for their response. Majority of the people echoed that Hadhrat Umar (RA) should march ahead with them in tow. Hadhrat Umar (RA) commended this opinion for he did not like to disregard their opinion. He chose to rather dissuade them in a kind manner. He therefore said, "Prepare yourselves and prepare others. I shall continue with you unless I receive an opinion that is more appropriate."

Hadhraf Umar then sent for men of insight and the cream of Rasuluilaah companions and the most prominent Aran leaders gathered together. Hadhrat umar (RA) said to them, "r feel that I should proceed with the army, hut I wish you to give me your opinion on the matter." The men gathered for discussion and unanimously agreed that another companion of Rasuluilaah should be sent (as commander of the army) while Hadhrat Umar (RA) stayed behind (in Madinah) to dispatch reinforcements. They felt that if victory is achieved, the result would be what everyone desired and if not, another commander and another army could always be sent. In this manner (they said), the Kuffaar would be further enraged, the Muslims would guard against making mistakes and Allaah's assistance would arrive according to His promise. Hadhrat Umar (RA) then again announced that the people should gather as they do for salaah and they did. Hadhrat Umar (RA) also sent for Hadhrat Ali whom he had appointed as his deputy in Madinah and for Hadhrat Talha whom he had sent ahead with the scouting party. At the same time, he also sent for Hadhrat Zubayr (RA) and Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf, whom he had appointed as commanders of the two flanks of the army. (When everyone was present,) Hadhrat Umar (RA) then stood amongst the people and said: "Verily Allaah has gathered the Muslims around istaam, has created love between their hearts and made them brothers in islaam. The Muslims are therefore like a single body in their relationship with each other. No part is free from pain when another part is suffering, it is therefore incumbent on the Muslims that their matters be decided by mutual consultation between their men of insight (the consultative assembly). The masses need to follow the one who is their leader and are also bound by the decision of the consultative assembly. The people will have to adopt the course that these men plan. In fact, even the Ameer is bound by the decision that the consultative assembly make. People are also bound to follow the battle strategies that these men outline and approve of. O people! I was also a man like the rest of you (marching in Jihaad) until the men of knowledge and insight amongst you stopped me from proceeding ahead, l am now also of the opinion that I should rather stay behind (in Madinah) and send someone else (as commander of the army), r have already presented this matter to all whom I have sent ahead and all who have been left behind." Although Hadhrat Umar (RA) has appointed Hadhrat Ali (RA) as his deputy in Madinah and had made Hadhrat Talha (RA) the commander of the scouting group that had already reached a place called Ahwas, he ensured that even they were present to make the decision. (,)

Hadhrat Umar bin Abdul Azeez (RA) narrates that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) was informed about the martyrdom of Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah bin Mas'ood and that the Persians had rallied around a common leader from the house of the Kisra, he summoned the Muhaajireen and the Ansaar and marched until they reached a place called Siraar. The rest of the narration is similar to the one mentioned above.
sources: Jbn Jareer.

paras: Hadhrat Muhammad bin Sallaam Baykindi narrates that even during the Period of Ignorance Hadhrat Amr bin Ma'diyakrib (RA) had achieved many feats. He became a Muslim after arriving with a delegation to meet Rasulullaah ﷺ. Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab (RA) sent him to Hadhrat Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas (who was commanding the Muslim army) in Qaadssiyyah, where he (his military genius) was being put to the test. Hadhrat Umar (RA) wrote to Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) saying, "I am reinforcing you with two thousand men. They are Amr bin Ma'diyakrib and Tulayha bin Khuwaylid (Asadi). Consult with them in military matters but do not appoint them to posts of command (because their daunting courage would place the lives of others at risk)."
sources: Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.5 Pg.319) has commented on t lie chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Sa'd bin Abi waqqaas (RA) narrates, "When Rasulullaah ﷺ arrived in Madinah, the Juhayna tribe approached him with the request, 'Now that you have arrived in our midst, do make a treaty with us so that we may bring our people to you.' After Rasulullaah ﷺ had made the treaty with them, they accepted islaam. Rasulullaah ﷺ then dispatched us during the month of Rajab with instructions to attack the Banu Kinaana tribe, who Jived close to where the juhayna tribe lived. We were not even a hundred men when we attacked them, ([) Ibn Jareer. whereas they were greater in number, when we sought assistance from the Juhayna tribe, they refused to render any saying, 'why are you fighting during a sacred month.' we told them that we were only fighting people who had exiled us from a sacred place (Makkah) during a sacred "We then asked each other what to do. While some of us felt that we should report the matter to Rasulullaah ﷺ, others were of the opinion that we should remain where we were. Me and a few others opted lo rather attack a caravan Of the Quraysh. During those times, the practice was that whoever took anything as booty from the enemy, the possessions became his own property. So while we proceeded to attack the caravan, our companions went back to Rasulullaah ﷺ and reported the incident to him. Rasulullaah ﷺ's face became red with anger and he stood up saying, You left me as a united group and return separatedl it was this very disunity that destroyed the nations before you. I shall now appoint as your commander a man who may not be the best of you but who is certainly the most enduring through hunger and thirst.' Rasulullaah ﷺ then appointed Abdullaah bin Jahash Asadi as our commander, who was the first commander appointed in Islaam."
sources: The Arabs considered the months or Dhul Qa'dah, Dhul Hijjah, Muharram and Rajab as sacred months in which fighting was forbidden.

paras: Hadhrat shihaab Ambari narrates, "I was the first to set alight the gates of Tustar when Hadhrat Ash'ari (RA) was struck down by an arrow. When the city was conquered, Hadhrat Ash'ari (RA) appointed me as Ameer over ten members of my tribe."
sources: Ahmad. Ibn Abi Shayba has also reported the narration, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal tyol.7 Pg.60), as did Baghawi, as quoted in Isaaba (Vol. 2 Pg.278). Bayhaqi has also reported the narration in his Dalaa'il with the following difference; They asked, "Why are you fighting during a sacred month." We said to them, "In this sacred month we are only fighting people who had exiled us from a sacred place (Makkah)." This is reported in Al Bidaaya wan Nihaaya (Vol.3 Pg.248). Haythami (Vol.6 Pg.66) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat limar (RA) once said, ''When there are three person travelling, they should appoint one of them as Ameer. This appointment has been commanded by Rasulullaah ﷺ
sources: Ibn Abi Shayba, as quoted in isaaba (Vol.2 Pg 159).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once dispatched an exceptionally large expedition. Rasulullaah ﷺ made each one of them recite whatever portion of the Qur'aan he knew. When Rasulullaah ﷺ came to a man who was one of the youngest and asked him what portion of the Qur'aan he knew, he named several Surahs that he knew including Surah Baqara. "Do you not like to taint them with this world."
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his ibn Asaakir, as quoted in Karvul Ummaal (Vol.1 Pg.146).

paras: Hadhrat lmraan bin Abdullaah reports that Hadhrat ubay bin Ka'b (RA) once asked Hadhrat Umar (RA), "What is it that you do not give me command'" Hadhrat Umar (RA) replied, "I do not like to taint your Deen."
sources: Ibn Sa'd Pg.60).

paras: Hadhrat Haaritha bin Mudarrib narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) wrote the following letter to them: l have sent Ammaar bin Yaasir as your Ameer and Abdullaah bin Mas'ood as your teacher and minister. They are both amongst the chosen companions of Rasulullaah ﷺ and veterans of Badr, Learn from them and follow their example. By sending Abdullah to you, I have actually sacrificed my own need for him. 1 have also sent uthmaan bin Hunayf as to survey the rural areas of Iraq. I have stipulated that their wages should be a goat every day. Half the goat and its innards should be given to Ammaar (because as the Ameer, he would naturally have guests to feed) and the other half should be shared between the other three men (i.e. Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA), Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Hunayf (RA) and Hadhrat Hudhayfa bin Yamaan (RA), who was sent as an assistant surveyor)."
sources: Ibn Sa'd, Kaakim and Sa'eed bin Mansoor, as quoted in Kanzul ummaal Pg.314). Tabraani has also reported the narration without the part mentioning Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Hunayf (RA). Haythami ' (vol.9 Pg.29l) has commented on the chain of narrators and Bayhaqi (Vol.? Pg.136) has also reported the narration in detail with another chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Sha'bi narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once asked, "Tell me who I should appoint to take charge of a public matter that is of great concern to me?" When the name of Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA) was suggested, Hadhrat Umar (RA) noted that he was not up to the task, when another name was suggested, Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "I have no need for him." When Hadhrat Umar (RA) was asked who it was that he required, he replied, "Someone who will be like one of the people when he becomes the Ameer of his humility) and when he is not the Ameer, he appears to be the Ameer (because of his high sense of responsibility)." The people (with Hadhrat Umar then said, "we know of none suitable besides Rabee bin Ziyaad Haarithi," "That is true," confirmed Hadhrat umar (RA).
sources: Abu Ahmad Haakim in his Kuna, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal fyol.Z Pg.164).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Waa'il Shaqeeq bin Salama reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once appointed Hadhrat Bishr bin Aasim (RA) to collect the Zakaah of the Hawaazin tribe. However, when Hadhrat Bishr (RA) failed to do so, Hadhrat Umar (RA) met him and asked, "what has kept you back? is it not necessary to listen to me and to obey mc?" "Of course," replied Hadhrat Bishr (RA), "but I have beard Rasulullaah ﷺ say, "Whoever is appointed to carry out a public task shall be brought forward on the Day of. Qiyaamah and made to stand on the bridge spanning jahannam. if he carried out the task well, he will be saved, but if he did not fulfil the responsibility, the bridge will shatter and he will fall for seventy years into jahannam.'"

Hadhrat Umar (RA) left in a very distressed and worried state. Hadhrat Abu Dharr then met him and asked, "Why do I see you so distressed and worried?" Hadhrat Umar (RA) replied, "Why should I not be distressed and worried when I have heard Bishr bin Aasim say, "I have heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say, "whoever is appointed to carry out a public task be brought forward on the Day of Qiyaamah and made to stand on the bridge spanning Jahannam. If he carried out the task well, he will be saved, but if he did not fulfil the responsibility, the bridge will shatter and he will fall for seventy years into jahannam.'" Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) asked, "Did you not hear Rasulullaah say this?" When Hadhrat Umar (RA) said that he had not, Hadhrat Abu Dharr said, "I testify that I Had certainly heard Rasulullaah ﷺ state, "Whoever is appointed to carry out any public task shall be brought forward on the Day of Qiyaamah and made to stand on the bridge spanning Jahannam. if he carried out the task well, he will be saved, but if he did not fulfil the responsibility, the bridge will shatter and he will fall for seventy years into Jahannam, and Jahannam is extremely black and dark.' Now which of these two narrations instils more fear in your heart?" Hadhrat Umar (RA) replied, "They have both instilled great fear in my heart. Who will then be able to accept the responsibility and do justice to it?"

Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) replied, "The person whose nose Allaah intends cutting and whose cheek Allaah wishes to bring to the ground (whom Allaah wishes to. However, we know only good of your Khilaafah. Then again, it is possible that if you hand over the post to someone who does not exercise justice, you will also not be saved from the sm (of his injustice)."
sources: Tabraani, as quoted in Targheeb wat Tarheeb (Vol. 3 Pg.44). Haythami (Vol.5 has commented on the chain of narrators. Abdur Razzaaq, Abu Nu'aym, Abu Sa'eed Naqqaash, Baghawi and Daar Qutni have also reported the narration, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.3 Pg.l63). lbn Abi Shayba and ibn'Mandah have also reported it with another chain of narrators, as quoted in Pg.152). 96 (Vol-2) an Ameer. He replied, "I was helped to sit and to stand (the men gave me great honour) to the extent that I feel as if I am no longer myself (my humility has been diminished)." Rasulullaah ﷺ commented, "Leadership it like that (it does that to a person)." Hadhrat Miqdaad (RA) then said, "I swear by the Being Who has sent you with the truth that I shall never again assume any post of leadership." Thereafter, Hadhrat Miqdaad (RA) would even decline when people asked him to lead them insalaah. '" Another narration from Hadhrat Anas (RA) quotes that Hadhrat Miqdaad (RA) said, "I was helped on to my conveyance and helped to dismount until I felt as if 1 was superior to the others." Rasulullaah ﷺ then told him, "Such is leadership. You may therefore either accept it or reject it." Hadhrat Miqdaad (RA) then swore, "I swear by the Being who has sent you with the truth that 1 shall never again assume command of even two persons," ^ The Narration of Tabraani about the Incident of Hadhrat Miqdaad (RA) Hadhrat Miqdaad bin Aswad (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ sent me on an expedition. When we returned, he asked me, 'How do you find yourself?' I replied, 'I. gradually started to think that the others were my servants. 1 swear by Allaah that after this I shall never again take command of even two persons." ^ it is reported that Rasulullaah ﷺ once appointed someone to lead an expedition. When the man had completed his duties and returned, Rasulullaah ﷺ asked him, "How was it to be the Ameer?" The man replied, "Although I behaved like one of them, they all mounted when 1 did and dismounted when I did." Rasulullaah ﷺ commented, "Leaders stand at the door of oppression (are prone to oppress) except for those whom Allaah saves (from committing oppression)." The man then said, "1 swear by Allaah that I shall never again accept command from you or from anybody else." Rasulullaah ﷺ then smiled broadly until even his back teeth were visible. ^ The Advice Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) gave to Hadhrat Raafi Taal About Being an Ameer Hadhrat Raafi Taa'i (RA) narrates that he accompanied Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) on an expedition and when they were returning, he asked Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) for some advice. Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) said, "Establish the Fardh saiaah at its fixed hours, pay the zakaah due on your wealth with the pleasure of your heart, fast during the month of Ramadhaan and perform pilgrimage to the House of Allaah (Hajj). Remember well that Hijrah in islaam is an excellent virtue, and to make Jihaad in Hijrah is very good. Also remember that you should never

paras: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once appointed Hadhrat Miqdaad bin Aswad as Ameer of a troop of cavalrymen. When he returned from the expedition, Rasulullaah ﷺ asked him what he thought about being command from anyone after Rasulullaah ﷺ, I would accept a post from Abu Bakr because of his virtue and his early entry into Islaam, However, I would still not want to accept any post of command from anyone after Rasulullaah ﷺ

When Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) consulted with the Sahabah (RA) about whom to send to Bahrain, Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) said, "Send the person whom Rasulullaah ﷺ had sent to them (the people of Bahrain), the one who made them Muslims and subservient. Someone whom they will recognise, who recognises them and who knows their land." Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) was referring to Hadhrat Alaa bin Hadhrami (RA). Hadhrat umar (RA) however, refused to accept the proposal and said, "Force Abaan bin Sa'eed bin Al Aas to return because he is a man who has been there several times." Hadhrat Abu Bakr refused to force him saying, "i shall not do it. I cannot force a person who says that he will not accept a post of command from anyone after Rasulullaah Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) then confirmed that Hadhrat Alaa bin Hadhrami would be sent to Bahrain.
sources: Ibn as quoted in Kanzul Ummaaliyol.'i Pg.133).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once summoned him to accept a post as governor, but he refused to accept the post. Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "You dislike an appointment to a post when someone better than you actually asked for it." When Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) asked who was that asked for a post, Hadhrat Umar (RA) replied, "Yusuf bin Ya'qoob Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) then said, "Yusuf was the Nabi of Allaah and the son of a Nabi, while I am merely Abu Hurayrah the son of Umayma. 1 fear three and two things (equalling five)." "Why don't you just say 'five things?" enquired Hadhrat Umar (RA). Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) replied, "I fear that I should say anything without knowledge, pass wrong judgement (as a governor, because of which I would) have my back lashed, have my wealth taken away and my reputation insulted."
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.MO). Abu Moosa has also reported the narration in his Dhayl. but the author of Isaaba. 4 Pg.241) has commented on the chain of narrators, ibn sa'd (Vol.4 Pg.59) has also reported the narration with some additions at the beginning. 100 (Vol-2) seeks protection from Allaah has sought a great source of protection.'" When Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) confirmed that he had heard the Hadith, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin umar (RA) said, "I then seek Allaah's protection from being a judge." Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) then asked, 'What prevents you when your father was a judge?" Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) replied, ''l have heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say, 'The person who is a judge and passes judgement in ignorance shall be one of the inmates of Jahannam. As for the one who is a knowledgeable judge and passes correct and just judgement, he plead Allaah on the Day of Qiyaamah) for an acquittal (that he should neither receive any rewards nor any sin).' What have I to hope for after this?"'1' A narration of Ahmad adds that after this, Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) excused Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) and told him not to inform anyone else about it. (otherwise none would be prepared to act as judge and society would suffer). Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) wanted him to act as judge, but he refused saying, "I have heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say, 'Judges are of three types; one will attain salvation while two will end up in Jahannam. Those who pass judgement unjustly or by the dictates of their desires shall be destroyed while the one who passes judgement with the truth will attain salvation." The Incident that Occurred Between Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) and Ummul Mu'mineen Hadhrat Hafsah (RA) Concerning Dowmatul Jandal Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Uinar (RA) narrates, "it was on the day that Hadhrat Ali (RA) and Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA) gathered at Dowmatul Jandal (to reconcile their differences) that (my sister) Ummul Mu'mineen Hafsa said to me, 'It is really not nice that you refrain from participating in a reconciliation that Allaah has brought about between the ummah of Muhammad ﷺ since you are the brother-in-law of Rasulullaah ﷺ and the son of Umar bin Khattaab That day, Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA) arrived on a huge Bactrian camel and announced, "Who is desirous of Khilaafah? Who is willing to risk his neck for it?" Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) says, "Never before had my heart ever aspired for worldly things and I almost said, 'That person (myself) desires the Khilaafah who had hit your neck and the neck of your father to accept Islaam until he made you two enter its fold!' However, I thought of Jannah and its 11) Tabraani in his Kabeer and Awsat, Bazaar and Ahmad narrating from reliable sources, as confirmed by Haythami (Vol A Pg.l'J3). Tabraani in his Kabeer and Awsat, narrating from reliable sources in his Kabeer, as confirmed by Ha. ythami (Vol.4 pg.193). Abu Yala has reported a similar narration and Ibn Sa'd (Vol. 4 Pg.108) as well, but in more detail.

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mowhab reports that Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) once said to Hadhrat Abdullaah bin umar (RA), "Go and pass judgement between the people." Hadhrat Abdullaah bin umar (RA) requested, "Will you not excuse me. O Ameerul Mu'mineen?" Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) emphatically said, "Never! l have sworn that you must be the judge." "Do not be hasty," Hadhrat Abdullaah bin umar spoke, "have you heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say, 'The person who bounties and refrained from saying it."
sources: Tabraani in his Kabeer, narrating from reliable sources, as confirmed by Pg.208). lbn Sa'd. 4 Pg.134) has reported a similar narration. (2) ibn Sa'd. 102 Ti S/UIABAH (Vol said to the person, 'Had he fallen into the fire, both of them would have entered jahannam. There is no obedience (to anyone) when it entails disobeying Allaah." Hadhrat Hakam (RA) confirmed that he remembered the Hadith. Hadhrat imraan (RA) then said, "I only wished to remind you of this Hadith."(l) Respecting the Khalifahs and Ameers and Obeying their Commands The Incident that occurred between Hadhrat Khaalid (RA) and Hadhrat Ammaar (RA) During an Expedition Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA), narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once dispatched Hadhrat Khaalid bin Waleed bin Mughiera Makhzoomi on expedition, with him was Hadhrat Ammaar bin Yaasir (RA). The expedition left and finally drew close to the people whom they intended to ambush early in the morning. They set up camp there late at night. However, someone warned the people the presence of the Sahabah (RA) and they all fled to a place of safety. One of the men amongst them who had accepted islaam together with his family stayed behind. He instructed his family to load their goods and then told them to wait until he returned. He then proceeded to meet Hadhrat Ammaar (RA) and said, "O Abu Yaqdhaan! My family and I have accepted Islaam, Will this help me if 1 stay behind (in the town) because all my people had fled when they heard about your arrival?" Hadhrat Ammaar (RA) said to him, "You may stay behind, for you are safe," The man and his family then went back. When Hadhrat Khaalid (RA) launched the attack the next morning, he found that the people had all fled. He then captured the man and his family. Hadhrat Ammaar (RA) said, "You can do nothing to a man who has accepted islaam." Hadhrat Khaalid (RA) said, "What have you to do with this? When 1 am the Ameer, how could you grant a person amnesty without my permission?" Hadhrat Ammaar (RA) replied, "I can indeed grant amnesty without your permission even though you are the Ameer. This man has accepted lmaan and if he wished to, he could have left with the others. Because he has lmaan, I instructed him to stay behind." The two Sahabah (RA) then argued until they started abusing each other. When they returned to Madinah, they both went to Rasulullaah ﷺ and Hadhrat Ammaar (RA) told him about the man and what he had done. Rasulullaah ﷺ then authorised the amnesty that Hadhrat Ammaar (RA) had granted but at the same time forbade people from granting amnesty to others without the permission of the Ameer. The two Sahabah (RA) then again

paras: A narration of Abu Husayn states that Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA) said, "Who is more worthy than us of this post (of Khilaafah)?" Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar said, "I wanted to say, 'More worthy than you is the one who hit your neck and your father's neck (to bring you into Islaam).' However, I then thought about the bounties of Jannah and feared that I would be spoiling them (by saying this)."
sources: Ahmad, narrating from reliable sources, as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.5 Pg.226). Tabraani has also reported the narration and according to some of his narrations, Rasulullaah ﷺ said. "There is no obedience lo the creation when it entails disobeying the Creator.'' UVF.S (Vol-2) started arguing in the presence of Rasulullaah ﷺ. To this, Hadhrat Khaalid (RA) remarked, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ This slave is insulting me in your presence! I swear by Allaah that had you not been here, he would have never used such terms for me." Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "O Khaalid! Do not harass Ammaar because Allaah dislikes anyone who dislikes Ammaar and Allaah curses anyone who curses Ammaar." Hadhrat Ammaar (RA) then stood up and left. Hadhrat Khaalid (RA) followed him, grabbed hold of his clothing and continuously made attempts to please Hadhrat Ammaar (RA) until Hadhrat Ammaar (RA) was pleased with him. Another narration states that it was then that Allaah revealed the verse- .jiji ^ ill £ J 'ytyj Obey Allaah, obey the Rasool ﷺ and those in command among you (your military commanders), if you dispute regarding any matter, then refer it to Allaah and the Rasool ﷺ (so that Allaah and His Rasool ﷺ may pass judgement in the matter i.e. find the solution in the Qur'aan or in the Ahaadeeth) if you believe in Allaah and the Last Day, This is best (for all) and gives the best result (because you will then not be basing your decisions on your personal opinions). Nisaa, verse The Incident that occurred Between Hadhrat Auf bin Maalik (RA) and Hadhrat Khaalid bin Waleed (RA) Hadhrat Auf bin Maalik Ashja'ee (RA) reports that he was amongst those Muslims who marched with zaid bin Haaritha for the Battle of Mu'ta. His companion was a man who had come with reinforcements from Yemen. He had nothing but his sword with him. When one of the Muslims slaughtered a camel, the man (from Yemen) asked him for a piece of the leather, which he gladly gave. The man made the piece of leather into a shield for himself and we then proceeded. When we faced the large Roman army there was a man amongst them riding a red horse. His saddle and his weapons were gold plated and he attacked the Muslims very fiercely. The man from Yemen waited for him behind a boulder and when the Roman passed by, the Yemeni hamstrung his horse. As the Roman fell, the Yemeni attacked and killed him. He then took possession of the Roman's

paras: A narration of tmaarn zuhri states that when Hadhrat (Hasan bin) Ali (RA) and Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA) got together, Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA) announced, "Who is most worthy of the post of Khilaafah then me?" Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar said, "I wanted to say, 'More worthy than you is the one who hit your neck and your father's neck because of your Kufr (myself).' However, l feared that (if 1 said this) thoughts would be entertained about me that are not true (people would think that I desired to be the Khalifah which was not true)."

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Saamit (RA) reports that when Ziyaad wanted to dispatch Hadhrat Imraan bin Husayn (RA) as governor of Khurasan, he refused to accept the post. His friends asked, "Are you forsaking the opportunity to be governor of Khurasan?" He replied, "it does not please me at all that I should suffer the heat of Khurasan (do the hard work of governing) while they (Ziyaad and his followers) enjoy its coolness (by using the income from the region). I fear that if I am ever facing the enemy in battle and then a letter would come to me from Ziyaad, which if I obey will result in my destruction and if I ignore it, will result in my execution (at the hands of Ziyaad)."

Ziyaad then appointed Hadhrat Hakam bin Amr Ghifaart (RA) as governor of Khurasan and Hadhrat Hakam (RA) accepted the post. Hadhrat imraan (RA) then asked someone to summon Hadhrat Hakam (RA) to him. A messenger went to Hadhrat Hakam (RA) and when he arrived, Hadhrat imraan (RA) said to him, "Did you hear Rasulullaah ﷺ say that no person should be obeyed when it (obedience to the person) entails disobedience to Allaah?" When Hadhrat Hakam confirmed that he had heard this from Rasulullaah ﷺ, Hadhrat Imraan exclaimed, "Alhamdu Lillaah!" or "Allaahu Akbar!" Another narration from Hadhrat Hasan states that when Ziyaad appointed Hadhrat (Hakam) Ghifaari (RA) as commander of the army, Hadhrat Imraan bin Husayn went to see him. Hadhrat imraan (RA) met him in public and asked, "Do you know why I have come to you?" When Hadhrat Hakam asked why he had come, Hadhrat Imraan (RA) said, "Do you remember what Rasulullaah ﷺ said to the person whose Ameer told him to throw himself into the fire and he was then stopped and prevented (by others from doing what he was commanded), when the incident was reported to Rasulullaah ﷺ, he oppose the Ameer), Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) looked up and said to him, "Undoubtedly, enjoining good and forbidding evil is an excellent deed. However, drawing weapons against your Ameer is certainly not a Sunnah practice."

A Narration of Hadhrat Abu Bakrah (RA) Concerning Respect for an Ameer Hadhrat Ziyaad bin Kusayb Adawi reports that Abdullaah bin Aamir used to deliver lectures to the people wearing fine clothing and with well groomed hair. After leading the salaah one day and entering his room, Mirdaas Abu Bilaal commented, "Would you look at the people's Ameer and leader! He wears fine clothes and adopts the appearance of the sinners!" Hadhrat Abu Bakrah (RA) was sitting next to the pulpit. When he heard this, he told his son Usayli to call Abu Bilaal. when Abu Bilaal arrived, Hadhrat Abu Bakrah (RA) said to him, "I have heard the comment you have just made about the Ameer, t have heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say, 'Allaah will honour the person who honours His Ameer and will disgrace the person who disgraces Allaah's Ameer." The Ameer is Obeyed only when he Instructs what is Right Hadhrat Alt bin Abi Taalib (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once appointed a commander of an expedition. Rasulullaah ﷺ dispatched the expedition with instructions to listen'to and to obey their commander. However, the others happened to aggravate their commander in some way and he ordered them to gather firewood, when they did as they were ordered, he instructed them to light a fire. After they had lit the fire, he said to them, "Did Rasulullaah ﷺ not instruct you listen to me and to obey me?" When they acknowledged the instruction, he said, "Then enter this fire," The men started looking at each other saying, "it was the fire (of jahannam) that we were escaping from when we went to Rasulullaah ﷺ in the meantime, the commander's anger abated and the fire died off.

When the men returned and reported the incident to Rasulullaah ﷺ, he said, "Had they entered it, they would have never emerged from it (because after death they would have entered the fire of Jahannam). Obedience is only in matters of good." (U Bazzaar, Pg.224) has commented on the chain of narrators. when we fulfil the rights we owe to them."

The next morning, Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked Hadhrat Khaalid bin Waleed "what has Alqama said to you since last night?" Hadhrat Khaalid (RA) replied, "By Allaah! He has not said anything to me!" Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "And you are even swearing in Allaah's name about it." The narration of Hadhrat Abu Nadhrah adds that Hadhrat Alqama then said to Hadhrat Khaalid (RA), "Be quiet, O Khaalid (Do not deny Another concludes with the words of Hadhrat Umar (RA) who said, "You are both speaking the truth." The narration of Zubayr bin Bakkaar states that Hadhrat umar (RA) then granted Hadhrat Alqama what he wanted and thus satisfied his need. This narration also adds that (during the night- conversation) when Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked Hadhrat Alqama what he had to say, Hadhrat Alqama replied, "All I can advocate is that we listen and obey. Hadhrat Umar (RA) later said (to Hadhrat Alqama) that if everyone else shared his attitude, it would be more precious to him (Hadhrat Umar (RA)) than all the wealth in the world.
sources: Bayhaqi (Vol.8 Pg.163).

Bukhari and Muslim. Bukhari and Muslim have also reported the narration from Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA), as quoted in Al Bidaaya wan Nihaaya (Vol. 4 Pg 226), ibn jareer has also reported the narration from Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) while Ibn Abi Shaybah has reported it from Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA). According to a narration in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.3 Pg.170), Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA) has named the Ansaari commander as Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Hudhaafa Sahmi (RA). (RA) quoted in Isaaba (Vol. 2 Pg.296), Bukbari has also given the same name in the narration of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA). (RA) jVol-2) 107 The Narration of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) Concerning Respecting the Ameer Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ was once with a group of the Sahabah (RA) when he turned to them and. said, "Do you not know that I am verily the Rasul of Allaah sent to you?" The Sahabah (RA) replied, "But of course. We testify that you are certainly the Rasul of Allaah." Rasulullaah ﷺ then asked them, "Do you not know that whoever obeys mc obeys Allaah and obedience to me is part of obedience to Allaah?" The sahabah responded by saying, "But of course. We testify that whoever obeys you obeys Allaah and obedience to you is part of obedience to Allaah." Rasulullaah ﷺ went on to say, "For you to obey me is part of obedience to Allaah and for you to obey your leaders is part of obedience to me. In fact, even if they perform salaah sitting down, you should also perform salaah sitting down." '*' The Advice Rasulullaah ﷺ gave to Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) Concerning Showing Respect to the Ameer Hadhrat Asmaa bint Yazeed (RA) reports that Hadhrat Abu Dharr Ghifaari (RA) used to serve Rasulullaah ﷺ and would return to the Masjid after he had completed. The Masjid was his home where he used to lie down (to sleep). Rasulullaah ﷺ happened to enter the Masjid one night where he found Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) sleeping on the ground. Rasulullaah ﷺ prodded him gently. with his foot until Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) sat upright. Rasulullaah ﷺ then said to him, "Did 1 not see you sleeping in the Masjid?" "Where should I sleep?" asked Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA), "I have no home besides this." Rasulullaah ﷺ then sat with him and said, "What will you do when the people expel you from the Masjid?" Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) replied, "I shall then go to Shaam, which is the place of migration (of the previous Ambiyaa), the place where mankind will be resurrected and the land of many Ambiyaa. 1 shall then become one of its people." Rasulullaah ﷺ asked further, "What will you then do if they exile you from Shaam?" "I shall then return (to Madinah), which will be my home and place of residence." Rasulullaah ﷺ again enquired, "And what if they exile you from here for the second time?" Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) resolved, "I shall then take up my sword and Oght until I die." Rasulullaah ﷺ smiled at him and placed his hand on him saying, "Should I rather guide you to something that is better than that?" Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) exclaimed, "Why not, O Rasulullaah ﷺ May my parents be sacrificed for you!" Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Follow them wherever they lead you and go along to wherever they drive you until you eventually meet me in that condition."'2' (!) Abu Ya'ia and ibn Asaakir, both narrating from reliable sources, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.3 Pg.l6H). (2) lbn Jareer, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal Pg.168). Ahmad has also reported the narration but Haythami Pg.223) has com men led on the chain of narrators. 108. (Vol-2) Another narration from Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) states that Rasulullaah ﷺ asked, "What will you then do when you are removed from there (Madinah)?" Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) replied, "I shall take my sword and strike anyone who wants to remove me." Rasulullaah ﷺ then placed his hand on the shoulder of Hadhrat Abu Dharr t and said, "Overlook (what they O Abu Dharr. You should rather follow them wherever they lead you and go along to wherever they drive you even though you have to adopt this attitude even with an Abyssinian slave." Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) says, "When I settled in Rabdha (on the instruction of Ameerul Mu'mineen Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA), it once occurred that the fqaamah (for salaah) was already called out and an Abyssinian man who had been appointed to collect Zakaah went forward (to lead the salaah). However, when he saw me, he started going back and putting me forward. I said to him, 'Stay where you are, for I am obeying the command of Rasulullaah ﷺ Another narration states that when Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) went to Rabdha, he once found an Abyssinian slave of Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) there. The man called out the Adhaan and the Iqaamah and then asked Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) to go forward (to lead the salaah). Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) said, "No. Rasulullaah ﷺ instructed me to listen and to obey even an Abyssinian slave." The slave then went forward and Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) performed salaah behind him.
Ya'qoob bin Sufyaan and Zubayr bin Bakkaar, as quoted in Isaaba (Vol.2 Pg.504).

paras: Hadhrat Ibn Abi Mulaykah says that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once passed by a lady suffering from leprosy as she was busy performing Tawaaf. He said to her, "O servant of Allaah! Do not cause difficulty to the people (because they are afraid to perform Tawaaf with you here), it would be best for you to remain at home." she then remained at home (and stopped going to the Masjidul Haraam). It later occurred that a man passing by her said to her, "The person who had prevented you has passed away. You may now come out." She responded by saying, "It is not befitting of me to obey him while he was alive and then disobey him after his death."
sources: Maalik, as quoted in Kanzut '(Vol.5 Pg.l?2).

paras: Hadhrat Shamar narrates from a man who had been the chief of an area during the Khilaafah of Hadhrat Ali (RA) that Hadhrat Ali (RA) once issued an order to them and then asked, "Will you do as you have been ordered?" when the said that they would not, Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "I swear by Allaah that you must do as you have been commanded otherwise the Jews and the Christians will definitely mount you necks."
sources: Ibn Abi Shaybah, as quoted in Kanzuf Ummaal. 110 (Vol-2) Hadhrat Arnr bin Al Aas (RA) (as Ameer) on a military expedition to the rural towns of Shaam, where the Battle of Dhaatus Salaasil was fought. The towns were those of the Banu Baliy tribe, the Banu Abdullaah tribe and the Banu Qudaa'ah tribe next to them. It was from the Banu Baliy tribe that the maternal uncles of Aas bin waa'il hailed (Aas bin Waa'il was the father of Hadhrat Amr bin (RA) Aas (RA)). When Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas (RA) arrived at the place, he was apprehensive of the large numbers of the enemy and sent a message to Rasulullaah ﷺ asking for reinforcements. Rasulullaah ﷺ prepared the early Muhaajireen for the task and amongst the most senior Muhaajireen who got ready for the task were Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) and Hadhrat umar (RA). Rasulullaah ﷺ appointed Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah bin Jarraah (RA) as their Ameer and when they met Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas (RA), he said to them, "I am your Ameer now for I had sent the message to Rasulullaah ﷺ asking for you to come here as reinforcements. However, the group of Muhaajireen said, "You may be the Ameer of your army, but our Ameer is Abu ubaydah Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas (RA) reiterated what he said by saying, "You are only the reinforcements that I had requested." Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah (RA) was a man of excellent character and very soft-hearted. When he saw what was happening, he said, 'You ought to know O Amr that the parting instruction Rasulullaah ﷺ gave to me was, 'When you reach your companion, co-operate with him.' I shall therefore obey you even if you wish to disobey me." With this, Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah (RA) handed over the commend to Hadhrat Amr (RA). (RA) Another narration from Zuhri states that Rasulullaah ﷺ dispatched two expeditions against the Banu Kalb tribe, the Ghassaan tribe and other Kuffaar tribes located in the rural towns of Shaam. Rasulullaah ﷺ appointed Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah bin Jarraah (RA) as Ameer of one expedition and Hadhrat Amr bin (RA) Aas (RA) as Ameer of the other. Marching in the army of Hadhrat Abu ubaydah (RA) was Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) and Hadhrat Umar (RA). when the two armies were about to leave, Rasulullaah fflefflig called for Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah (RA) and Hadhrat Amr (RA) and said to them, "Never oppose each other." When the two armies had left (Madinah), Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah (RA) took Hadhrat Amr (RA) aside and said to him, "Rasulullaah ﷺ had emphatically advised us never to oppose each other, it is either you who will obey me or t that will obey you," Hadhrat Amr (RA) replied, "I'd rather that you obey me." Hadhrat Abu ubaydah (RA) then accepted to be under the command of Hadhrat Amr (RA), who became the commander of both armies. Hadhrat Umar (RA) became angry at this arrangement and said (to Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah (RA)), "You have chosen to be under the command of Naabigha's son and have made him your Ameer, the Ameer of Abu Bakr and our Ameer?!" what sort of idea is this?" Hadhrat Abu ubaydah (RA) pacified Hadhrat umar (RA) by saying, "Dear brother! Rasulullaah ﷺ emphatically

paras: Hadhrat Urwa bin zubayr (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once sent (!) From Sayf bin Amr, also narrating from Hadhrat Hasan.

Umar bin Khattaab and said, "O Abu Abdur Rahmaan! Sometimes we sit with these leaders of ours and we confirm what they say even though wc know that it is not true. Even when they make unjust decisions, we still support them and make it seem credible to them. What do you think about this?" Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar said, "Dear nephew! During the time we were with Rasulullaah ﷺ we regarded this to be an act of hypocrisy but I do not know what you regard it to be." ' '

Another narration from the father of Hadhrat Aasim bin Muhammad states that someone once said to Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA), "When we are with our leaders, wesaythingsthatare quite the opposite of what we say when we leave them," Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) commented, ,rWe used to regard this as an act of hypocrisy." Bukhari has reported a similar narration from Hadhrat Muhammad bin Zaid but adds that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) said, "During the time of Rasulullaah ﷺ, we regarded this to be an act of hypocrisy." Hadhrat Mujaahid reports that when a man came to Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar the latter asked him, "How is the relationship between you people and Abu Unays (the Ameer)?" The man replied, "Our relationship is that when we meet with him, we tell him what he likes to hear and sing a different tunc when we go away from him." Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) commented, "when we were with Rasulullaah ﷺ, this is the thing we regarded as hypocrisy."
sources: Ibn Asaakir, as quoted in Kanzu! Ummaa! Pg.93).

paras: Hadhrat Sha'bi reports that they once said to Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar "When we enter the courts of these people (our leaders), we say the things they like to hear but then say the opposite when we leave their presence." Hadhrat Abdullaah bin (RA) said, "During the time of Rasulullaah ﷺ, wc used to regard this as an act of hypocrisy."
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.4 Pg.332). uayhaqi (Vol.8 Pg.165).

paras: Hadhrat Alqama bin Waqqaas narrates that there was a useless man who used to enter the courts of the governors and make them laugh. Hadhrat Alqama's grandfather said to the man, "Shame on you! why do you enter the courts of these people and make them laugh?! I have heard from Bilaal bin Haarith who was a companion of Rasulullaah f)SSI that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, 'A servant (of Allaah) may utter a word that pleases Allaah without him realising its true potential and because of it, Allaah becomes pleased with him until the day he meets Allaah. On the contrary, a servant (of Allaah) may utter a word that displeases Allaah without him realising its true potential and because of it, Allaah becomes displeased with him until the day he meets Allaah.'"'ss Another narration from Hadhrat Alqama states that Hadhrat Bilaal bin Haarith (Vol. 8 Pg., as quoted in Targheeb wat Tarheeb (Vol.4 Pg.382).

Muzani said to him, "I see that you enter the courts of these governors and overwhelm them. Do check what you are saying to them because 1 have heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say, " A servant (of Allaah) may utter a word..." The rest of the narration is like the one mentioned above.

Hadhrat Hudhayfa (RA) once said, "Beware of the dens of evil!" "What are the dens of evil, O Abu Abdullaah?" someone enquired from him. He replied, "The doors of the rulers. A person enters the court of a ruler and then confirms the lies he speaks and praises him for qualities he does not possess." ( '

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that his father (Hadhrat Abbaas once said to him, "Dear I notice that the Ameerul Mu'mineen calls for you, allows you to be close to him and even consults with you together with the Sahabah (RA) of Rasulullaah ﷺ. Now remember these three things that I am telling you. Fear Allaah and never let him encounter any lies from you (never tell him a lie). You should also never disclose any of his secrets and never backbite about anyone in his presence." One of the narrators by the name of Aamir says that he said to Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA), "Each one of these advices are belter than a thousand." Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) in turn said, "Each one of them is better than ten thousand."
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.227).

paras: Hadhrat Sha'bi reports that Hadhrat Abbaas (RA) once said to his son Hadhrat Abdullaah, "1 notice that that great man (referring to Hadhrat Umar allows you to sit close to him and includes you amongst people with whom you do not belong (the veterans of Gadr). You should therefore remember three things that I shall tell you. Never let him encounter any lies from you, (never tell him a lie), never disclose any of his secrets and never backbite about anyone in his presence."

Hadhrat Hasan (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once refused to accept a verse or the Qur'aan from Hadhrat Ubay (RA) (saying that it is either not in the Qur'aan or not as Hadhrat Ubay (RA) said it appeared). (RA) Ubay said, "I had heard it from Rasulullaah ﷺ at a time when you were preoccupied with trade in Baqee." Hadhrat umar (RA) then said, "You have spoken the truth, (t knew that the verse is in the Qur'aan but I refused to accept it because) I only wanted to test whether there are people amongst you who would speak the truth (before the Ameer). There is no good in an Ameer in whose presence the truth cannot be spoken and who does not speak the truth."
sources: Surah Maa 'id ah, verse 107.

paras: Hadhrat Abu Mijlaz reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) accused Hadhrat Ubay of lying when he recited the versed Hadhrat Ubay (RA) retorted by saying, "Your lie is worse!" Someone reprimanded Hadhrat Ubay (RA) by saying, "Are you calling the Ameerul Mu'mineen a liar?" Hadhrat ubay (RA) replied, "I have more respect for the rights of the Ameerul Mu'mineen than you have. However, 1 have falsified him only to confirm the truth of Allaah's Book and I can never confirm what the Ameerul Mu'mineen says when it entails falsifying the Book of Allaah." Hadhrat Umar then said, "He has spoken the truth.''
sources: Abd bin Hurr,ayd, Ibn larcer and Adi, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal Pg 285). (4) ibn Asaakir and Abu Dharr Harawi in his Majaami. as quoted in Kanzul Pg. 148).

paras: Hadhrat Nu'maan bin Basheer (RA) reports that in a gathering of Muhaajirecn and Ansaar, Hadhrat Umar (RA) once asked, "What will you people do if I were permissive in certain matters?" when everyone remained silent, Hadhrat Umar repeated the question for a second and then a third time. Hadhrat Basheer bin Sa'd then responded by saying, "If you do that, we will set you straight as an arrow is straightened." Hadhrat Umar (RA) commented, "You are then certainly the ones (capable of being with You are then certainly the ones!"

Hadhrat Moosa bin Abu Isa narrates that when Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab went to the pond of the Banu Haaritha, he met Hadhrat Muhammad bin Maslama there. Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked him, "What do you think of me?" Hadhrat Muhammad bin Maslama (RA) replied, "I swear by Allaah that in my opinion you are as 1 like to see you and as anyone who likes good likes to see you. 1 see that you are meticulous in collecting wealth, are also abstinent from it (i) Ibn Raahway, as quoted in Kanzul ' Ummaai '(Vol.7 Pg.2). and distribute it justly. If however, you stray, we shall straighten you just as arrows are straightened with weights." Hadhrat umar (RA) then said "Excellent! (You say,) 'if however, you stray, we shall straighten you just as arrows are straightened with weights'. All praise belongs to Allaah Who has placed me amongst people who will rectify me when I stray." ! ' '

Hadhrat Abu Qabcel narrates that Hadhrat Mu'aawiya Sii'SKs once ascended the pulpit on the day of Jumu'ah and said in his lecture, "The wealth is all ours and the spoils of war are all ours. We shall give it to whom we will and refuse whoever we will." Since no one responded to this statement, Hadhrat Mu'aawiya repeated it the following Jumu'ah. When no one objected this time as well, he again repeated it on the third Jumu'ah. On that occasion, a man in the Masjid stood up and said, "Never! The wealth is ours and the spoils of war are ours. If anyone poses an obstacle between us and it, we shall have him dealt with by Allaah or by our swords."

After Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA) descended from the pulpit, he sent for the man, who was allowed in his court. "He is destroyed!" the people commented. However, when the people entered the court of Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA), they found the man sitting with Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA) on his bed. Hadhrat Mu'aawiya then said to the people, "This man has given me life, may Allaah give him life. 1 have heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say, 'Soon after me there shall come rulers who will say (wrong) things and no one would object to them. They will fall over each other in Jahannam just as monkeys (jumping from a tree) fall over each other.' when no one objected to what ! said on the first Jumu'ah, I feared that I would be amongst these rulers. When no one objected on the second Jumu'ah, I said to myself that I must be from amongst them. However, when I spoke on the third Jumu'ah, this man objected. He has given me life, may Allaah give him life."
sources: lbn Mubaarak, as quoted in Muntakhah Kanzui.

paras: Hadhrat Khaalid bin Hakeem bin Hizaam reports that when Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah was governor of Shaam, he punished some of the local (Kuffaar) persons (for not paying the Jizya(3)). Hadhrat Khaalid bin waleed (RA) stood up and spoke to him (about the error of his act). The people commented, "You have made the Ameer angry." Hadhrat Khaalid bin Waleed (RA) said, "I had never intended to make him angry but I have heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say that the people who will be most severely punished on the Day of Qiyaamah will be those who punished people most severely in this world."
sources: ibn Abi Aasim, Baghawi, Ahmad, Bukhari in hip Taareekh, Baawardi and Tabraani, as quoted in isaaba (Vol.l Pg.403). Pg.234) has com in en ted on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Hasan reports that when Ziyaad dispatched Hadhrat Hakam bin Amr Ghifaari as governor of Khurasan, the Muslims there managed to win a large amount of booty. Ziyaad then wrote to Hadhrat Hakam (RA) saying, "The Ameerul Mutnineen (Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA)) has written to say that all the gold and silver should be reserved for him and should therefore not be distributed amongst the Muslims." Hadhrat Hakam (RA) wrote back to Ziyaad saying, "You have written to me about the letter of the Ameerul Mu'mineen: However, I have received the Book of Ailaah before the letter of the Ameerul Mu'mineen (1 shall therefore not obey his command which contradicts that of the Qur'aan). I swear by that even if the skies and earth have to close up on a person, Ailaah will create an escape for him between them and give him peace if he is one who fears Ailaah."

Hadhrat Hakam (RA) then had an announcer announce to the people that they should present themselves for the booty by the morning. He then distributed the booty (including the gold and silver) amongst the people. When he did this, Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA) sent some people to arrest Hadhrat Hakam (RA) and place him in shackles. Hadhrat Hakam (RA) passed away in these shackles and was buried in Khurasan. He said, "l shall contest (my case against Mu'aawiya in the court of Another narration adds that after Hadhrat Hakam (RA) had distributed the booty amongst the people, he prayed, "O Ailaah! If You have any good for me with You, then raise me to You." He then passed away in the town of Maroo in Khurasan. Isaaba (Vol.1 Pg.347) states that it was actually when Hadhrat Hakam received the letter of Ziyaad noting his displeasure, he prayed to Ailaah (for a swift death), after which he passed away.

Hadhrat Ataa reports that-Ziyaad or his son once sent Hadhrat Imraan bin Husayn to collect Zakaah. When Hadhrat Imraan (RA) returned, he brought nothing back. "Where is the money?" asked Ziyaad (or his son). "Did you send me to bring back any money?" Hadhrat Imraan (RA) asked, "I collected it as we used to do during the time of Rasulullaah ﷺ and used it in the avenues we used it during the time of Rasulullaah ﷺ (1 distributed it amongst the needy of the area)." punishment on his governors (when they deserved it) and whenever a complaint was brought to him about any governor, he would gather the complainant and the governor in one place. Thereafter, if the complaint was proven to be valid and the governor needed to be taken to task, Hadhrat Umar (RA) would take him to task.

Hadhrat Abu Khuzayma bin Thaabit (RA) reports that whenever Hadhrat umar appointed someone as governor, he would make a group of the Ansaar and some others witness (to the appointment) and say (to the new governor), "I am not sending you to give you sovereignty over the blood of people..." The rest of the narration is similar to the one quoted earlier.
sources: Haakim (vol.3 Pg.442). (Vol.! Pg.316).

paras: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Saabit reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once sent for Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Aamir Jumhi (RA) and said to him, "We wish to appoint you in command of this regiment whom you should lead into enemy territory to wage war with them," Hadhrat Sa'eed (RA) said, (RA) Umar! Please do not try me." Hadhrat Umar (RA) resolved "I shall never leave you. You people have cast this responsibility (of Khilaafah) on my neck and now you wish to leave me all alone! I am sending you with a group of people from whom you are not the best. I am not sending you to whip them or to humiliate them but only to lead them in jihaad against their enemies and to distribute their booty amongst them." ,3)

Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) once addressed the people saying, "The Ameerul Mu'mineen Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab (RA) has sent me here to teach you the Book of your Rabb, the Sunnah of your Nabi ﷺ and to administrate over municipal affairs."
sources: Tabari (Vol. 5 Pg.19).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Saalih Ghifaari narrates that Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas (RA) (while in Egypt) once wrote to Hadhrat Umar (RA) stating: "We have reserved a house for you here next to the Jaami Masjid." Hadhrat Umar (RA) wrote back saying. "Why should a man living in Hijaaz have a house in Egypt?" Hadhrat umar (RA) then ordered that the area be converted into a marketplace for the Muslims.
sources: )bn Abdul Hakam. as quoted in gamut Ununaal Pg.l48l.

paras: Hadhrat Tameem jayshani (RA) reports that Hadhrat umar (RA) wrote the following letter to Hadhrat Amr bin M Aas (RA)

"The news has reached me that you have had a pulpit made by which you climb high above the people's necks (when delivering a sermon), is it not sufficient for you to remain standing with the Muslims beneath your heels. 1 command you in the name of Allaah that you should demolish it."
sources: Ibn Abdul Hakam. as quoted in Uinmaa! Pg.166).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Uthmaan reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) wrote a letter to them when they were in Azerbaijan. He wrote: "O Utba bin Farqad! Your position and wealth has not been the fruits of your efforts, nor the fruits of your father's or mother's efforts. Feed the people in their homes with that which you feed yourself in your home. Guard yourself against indulging in luxuries, from imitating the appearance of the Mushrikeen and from wearing silk clothing."
sources: Muslim, as quoted in Targheeb wat Tarheeb (Vol.3.

paras: Hadhrat urwa bin Ruwaym narrates lhat Hadhrat umar (RA) was inquiring about the condition of the people (during the Hay) when some people from Hims passed by him. "How is your Ameer?" asked Hadhrat umar (RA). They replied, "He is the best of Ameers except for the fact that he had built a lofty residence in which he lives.

Hadhrat Umar (RA) then wrote a letter, which he sent with a messenger with instructions to burn the building down, when the messenger reached Hims, he gathered firewood and set fire to the door. When the Ameer was informed about it, he said, "Leave him alone because he has been sent (by the Ameerut Mu'mineen)." The messenger then handed the letter over to the Ameer, (After reading the letter) The Ameer did not even put the letter down when he rode off to Hadhrat Umar (RA). When Hadhrat Umar (RA) saw him arrive, he told the Ameer to meet him at Harra where the Zakaah camels were kept. (When he met him there) Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked him to remove his clothes and then gave him a garment of camel hide to wear. Hadhrat Umar (RA) then instructed him to fetch water from the well to give the camels to drink. The man continued going in and out of the well until he was exhausted. Hadhrat Umar then asked him, "How much longer will you be in this world?" "For only a short while," came the reply. Hadhrat umar (RA) commented, 'Then is it for this short while that you have built the mansion and adopted a standard of living that exceeds those of the poor, the widows and orphans? Go back to your post and never repeat yourself." "'

Hadhrat Attaab bin Rifaa'ah narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once received the news that Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) had built a mansion and had a door put on it, saying that the noise from the marketplace has now been cut off (form entering the mansion), Hadhrat Umar (RA) then dispatched Hadhrat Muhammad bin Maslama, whom he always sent when he needed a task done exactly as he wanted. The instructions he gave Hadhrat Muhammad bin Maslama (RA) was to bring Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) to him and to burn down the door. (When Hadhrat Muhammad bin Maslama (RA) arrived in Someone cameto Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) and informed him (about the arrival) and when the features (of Hadhrat Muhammad bin Maslama (RA)) were described to Hadhrat Sa'd (RA), he recognised him, Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) then went to meet Hadhrat Muhammad bin Maslama (RA), who said to him, "The news has reached the Ameerul Mu'mineen that you commented about the noise being cut off." When Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) swore that he never made such a statement, Hadhrat Muhammad bin Maslama (RA) said, "We shall do as we have been commanded while you will have to convey what you said (to the Ameerul Mu'mineen)."

When Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) offered to provide Hadhrat Muhammad bin Maslama with provisions for the journey, he refused to take any and rode off until he reached Madinah. when Hadhrat Umar (RA) saw him, he said, "if I did not have a good opinion of you, I would have thought that you did not fulfil the task," Hadhrat Muhammad bin Maslama (RA) informed Hadhrat Umar (RA) that he had hurried back and assured Hadhrat umar (RA), "I have fulfilled the task. However, Sa'd excuses himself and swears that he had never made the statement,"

Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked, "Did he give you any provisions for the journey?" Hadhrat Muhammad bin Maslama (RA) replied, "No, but what prevented you from giving me provisions?" Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "I disliked giving you any provisions because although you would have had ease, I would have had to suffer for it (in the Aakhirah) since hunger is killing the people around me in Madinah. Have you not heard Rasululiaah say that a Mu'min should not fill his belly while his neighbour goes hungry?" you, do absolve me of your command and permit me to remain here,"

When Hadhrat Umar (RA) read this letter, his eyes welled with tears and he began to weep. The people with him asked, "O Ameerul Mu'mineen! Has Abu Ubaydah passed away?" "No," replied, Hadhrat Umar (RA), "but it is as if he already has." Hadhrat Umar (RA) then wrote back to Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah t saying: "Indeed the entire land of Jordan has been affected by the epidemic whereas the region of Jaabiya is free from it. You should therefore take the Muhaajireen there."

When Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah t had read the letter, he said, "We shall certainly listen to and obey this command of the Ameerul Mu'mineen," Hadhrat Abu Moosa reports further, "Abu Ubaydah then ordered me to mount my animal and to keep the people in their living quarters. In the meantime, my wife also got affected by the plague. When 1 reported this to Abu Ubaydah he personally proceeded to confine the people to their quarters, after which he was also afflicted and passed away. The plague then came to an end."
Hadhrat Abul Muwajjih says, "It is believed that Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah (RA) was part of an army of thirty six thousand people. Every one of them save six thousand died."
sources: ibn Asaafcir, as quota! in Kanzul Ummaal '(Vc!,3 Pg.lfifi). (2) ibn Mubaarak, Ibn Kaahway and Musaddad, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol. 3 Pg.165). The jVol-2) 121 .another narration from Iladhrat Abu Bakrah and Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) states that the news that reached Hadhrat Umar (RA) stated that Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) kept aloof from the people and locked them out of his house. Hadhral Umar then dispatched Hadhrat Ammaar bin Yaasir (RA) with instructions to go to Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) and if he found the door locked, he was to burn il down. '" The Incident Between Hadhrat Umar (RA) and a group of Sahabah (RA) in Shaam Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) once sought permission from Hadhrat umar (RA) to go to Shaam. Hadhrat Umar (RA) told him that he would be allowed to go there onlyoncondition that he became a governor of one of the areas. When Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) refused to be a governor, Hadhrat Umar (RA) refused to grant the permission. Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) then said, "I shall go there to teach people the Sunnah of their Nabi ﷺ and lead them in salaah." Hadhrat Umar (RA) then granted him permission. Hadhrat Umar (RA) later visited Shaam and when he drew close to where the Sahabah (RA) were staying, he stopped until evening fell. When the night cast its veil over him, he called to his slave saying, "O Yarfa! Let us go to Yazeed bin Abi Sufyaan, You will see that he has story-tellers with him, lanterns will be burning and rugs of and velvet will be spread out, which have been taken from the booty belonging to the Muslims, You will greet him and he will reply, after which you will ask permission to enter and he will not grant permission until he enquires who you arc." The two men proceeded until they reached the door of Hadhrat Yazeed bin Abi Sufyaan (RA). Hadhrat Umar (RA) greeted by saying, "As Salaamu Alaykum!" to which Hadhrat Yazeed (RA) replied, "Wa Alaykumus Salaam," When Hadhrat Umar JUls/iSei asked whether he could enter, Hadhrat Yazeed (RA) first asked, "who arc you?" To this Yarfa replied, "This is the one who is about to spoil your fun. This is the Ameerul Mu'mineen." Hadhrat Umar (RA) then opened the door and found story-tellers there, lanterns burning and rugs of silk and velvet. Hadhrat Umar (RA) urgently instructed Yarfa to shut the door and struck Hadhrat Yazeed (RA) with his whip right between the ears. Hadhrat Umar (RA) then folded up all the goods and placed it at the centre of the room. He then issued the command that no one should move until he returned. Hadhrat Umar (RA) and Yarfa then left Hadhrat Yazeed (RA). Hadhrat Umar entire narration is reported in Isaaba (Vol .3 pg.384) except that the narrator's name appears as Abaaya bin Rtfaa'ari instead of Attaabbin Rifaa'ah. Haythami (vol. 8 Pg.i67) has commented on the chain of narrators.
Haakim, narrating from reliable sources, as confirmed by Dhahabi.

paras: Another narration states that (when he read the letter from Hadhrat Umar Hadhrat Abu ubaydah (RA) said, "May Allaah forgive the Ameerul Mu'mineen. He wishes to preserve the lives of people who cannot remain living (forever)." Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah (RA) then wrote back to Hadhrat Umar saying, "Verily, I am with an army from amongst the armies of the Muslims whom 1 am not prepared to leave to save my own life from that which had afflicted them." Yet another narration states that Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah (RA) wrote to Hadhrat Umar saying: "O Ameerul Mu'mineen! I knew well your need from me. However, I am part of a Muslim army that I do not wish to leave to save my own life. I have no desire to leave them until Allaah passes His decree concerning me and concerning them. O Ameerul Mu'mineen! Do release me from your command (to return to Madman) and leave me with my army."
sources: Ibn is'haaq, as quoted in Bidaaya wan Nihaaya (Vol.7 Pg.78). Tabari (Vol, 4 Pg.201) has also reported the narration. 01' (Vol-2) 127 "Yes," replied Hadhrat Abu Usayd (RA). "To which tribe?" Rasulullaah ﷺ asked further. Hadhrat Abu Usayd (RA) replied, "To the Banu Abs tribe." Rasulullaah ﷺ then instructed Hadhrat Abu Usayd (RA) saying, "Ride to them and bring him back yourself." '*' The Lecture of Hadhrat Umar (RA) in this Regard Hadhrat Buraydah (RA) narrates that he was sitting with Hadhrat Umar (RA) one day when he heard a scream. Hadhrat Umar (RA) instructed his slave Yarfa to see where the noise was coming from. After checking, Yarfa reported, "The mother of a girl from the Quraysh is being sold (as a slave, because of which the child is screaming)." Hadhrat Umar (RA) then instructed him to summon the Muhaajireen and the Ansaar. After a short while, the room and the entire house was filled. After praising Allaah, Hadhrat Umar (RA) then said: "Do you people know whether the severing of family ties was amongst the teachings that Rasulullaah ﷺ brought?" When they replied in the negative, Hadhrat Umar (RA) Mi continued, "Because it has started to spread rapidly amongst you." He then recited the following verse of the Qur'aan: It is possible that if you are given authority (to rule over others), you would spread corruption on earth and (let alone harming others, you would even) sever family ties. Muhammad ﷺ, verse Hadhrat Umar JD'SSSs continued, "What form of severing family ties is worse than selling the mother of a girl from amongst you when Allaah has given you abundance?" The Sahabah (RA) said, 'Do as you see fit." Hadhrat Umar (RA) then wrote to all the regions (of the Islaamic Empire) instructing that the mother of no free woman should be sold a slave) because it entails severing family ties which is not permissible. '2' A Hadith of Abu Uthmaan Nahdi in this Regard Hadhrat Abu Uthmaan Nahdi reports that after Hadhrat Umar (RA) had appointed a man from the Banu Asad tribe as governor, the man came to him to collect the certificate of appointment. In the meantime, one of Hadhrat Umar (RA)'s children was brought to him and he started kissing the child. The man from the Banu Asad tribe asked, "Do you kiss children, O Ameerul Mu'mineen? By Allaahl I have never kissed a child to this day." Hadhrat Umar (RA) then said, "In that case, I swear by Allaah that you will be even less compassionate towards people. Give the certificate of appointment back. You should never act as governor for me ever again." Hadhrat Umar (RA) then cancelled his appointment. * ' (1) lbn Abi Shaybah, as quoted in Kanzvl Ummaal Pg.229). (2) lbn Mundhir, Haakim and Bayhaqi, as quoted in K3p7.ul Umsnaal '(Vol.2 Pg.226).

paras: Hadhrat Abu ja'far reports that Hadhrat Abu Usayd (RA) once brought to Rasulullaah ﷺ some captives from Bahrain, Looking at a woman from amongst them weeping, Rasulullaah ﷺ asked, "What is the matter?" She replied, "He has sold my son." "Have you sold her son'" Rasulullaah ﷺ asked.
(l)lbnAsaakir, as quoted in Kanzul Umuiaal Pg.324)

A narration of Hadhrat Muhammad bin Sallaam states that Hadhrat Umar (RA) said (to the man), "what trime is it of mine that mercy has been extracted from your heart? Allaah has mercy only on those servants of his who show mercy." Hadhrat Umar (RA) then removed him from the post and said, "If you have no mercy for your own children, how will you have mercy on the masses?"' ' '

Hadhrat Urwa (RA) narrates that in the time of Rasulullaah ﷺ a woman stole during the conquest of Makkah. The members of her tribe (the Banu Makhzoom) hurried to Hadhrat usaama bin Zaid (RA) to ask him to intercede (on her behalf before Rasuluilaah so that her hand should not be cut off), when Hadhrat Usaama (RA) spoke about it to Rasulullaah ﷺ, Rasulullaah face turned red (with anger) and he said, "Are you talking to me about (waiving) a penalty that Allaah has imposed?" Hadhrat Usaama (RA) cowered and said, "Seek Allaah's forgiveness for me, O Rasulullaah ﷺ That evening, Rasulullaah ﷺ stood up to deliver a lecture. After duly praising Allaah, he said: "The nations before you were destroyed because whenever a noble person amongst them stole, they let it be. However, when a weak person (from a family holding no status) stole, they imposed the penalty on him, l swear by the Being Who controls my life that even if Faatima the daughter of Muhammad ﷺ has to steal, I would cut off her hand."

Rasulullaah ﷺ then issued the necessary instructions and the woman's hand was cut off. She then repented sincerely to Allaah and even got married. Hadhrat Aa'isha says, "Thereafter, she used to come to me and I would present her needs to Rasulullaah ﷺ
sources: Daynowri, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal '(Vol.8 Pg,3l0).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Qataadah (RA) reports, "After we had left with Rasulullaah ﷺ for the Battle of Hunayn and met with the enemy, we suffered a temporary defeat.
