sources: Ibn Asaakir, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol. 8 Pg.299). (2) lbn Sa'd (Vol.3 Pg.237).

paras: Hadhrat Sha'bi narrates that when Hadhrat Bilaal (RA) and his brother extended marriage proposals to family from Yemen, Hadhrat Bilaal (RA) said, "I am Bilaal and this is my brother. We were both slaves from Abyssinia. When we were misguided, Allaah guided us and when we were slaves, Allaah set us free. If you marry us (to your daughters), then all praise is due to Allaah (we shall be grateful) and if you refuse, (we will not mind because) Allaah is still the Greatest (and He will open other avenues for us). (The family agreed and got them married), Hadhrat Maymoon reports that one of Hadhrat Bilaal (RA) brothers claimed that he was of Arab descent and considered himself an Arab. When he once proposed for an Arab woman, the family said, "We will marry you only if Bilaal is present." Hadhrat Bilaal (RA) presented himself and after reciting the words of the Khutbah, he said, "I am Bilaal bin Rabaah and this is my brother. He is a man who is poor in his character arid religious practices. You may get him married if you- please and if you chose to refuse him, you are at liberty to do so." The family said, "We shall certainly marry anyone who is a brother of yours." They then got him married.

Hadhrat Urwa bin Ruwaym reports that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Qurt Thumaali who was a companion of Rasulullaah ﷺ was appointed governor by Hadhrat Umar (RA). He was patrolling the streets of Hims one night when he passed by a bride in front of whom people were lighting several fires. Hadhrat Abdullaah started hitting the people with his whip until they all dispersed. The next morning he sat on his pulpit and after duly praising Allaah, he said, "When Abu Jandalah married Umaamah, he prepared some handfuls of food (as a Waleemah) for (his marriage to) her. May Allaah shower His compassion on Abu Jandalah and may He shower His special mercies on Umaamah. May Allaah however curse your wedding of last night! The people were lighting fires and imitating the Kuffaar whereas Allaah has extinguished their light!"
sources: Abu Shaykh in his Kitaabun Nikaah, as quoted in Isaabah (Vol.4 Pg.38). (2)lbnSa'd(Vol.8Pg.l61).

paras: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) reports that that the dowry Rasulullaah ﷺ gave (her) was twelve Awqiya and a Nash, which totalled an amount of five hundred Dirhams. She then went on to specify that an Awqiya amounted to forty Dirhams and a Nash amounted to twenty Dirhams.

Hadhrat Masrooq narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once mounted the pulpit and said, "I do not know who increased dowries above four hundred Dirhams because the dowry that Rasulullaah ﷺ and the Sahabah (RA) gave was always four hundred Dirhams or less. Had larger dowries been an act of Taqwa or honour, people would have never beat- Rasulullaah ﷺ and the Sahabah to it," After Hadhrat Umar (RA) had alighted from the pulpit, a woman from the Quraysh objected. "O Ameerul Mu'mineen!" she said, "Are you forbidding the people from paying dowries in excess of four hundred Dirhams?" When Hadhrat Umar (RA) confirmed it, she said, "Have you then not heard Allaah say in the Qur'aan: '...when you have given one of them (your wives) a fortune (as Hadhrat Umar (RA) then said, "Allaah forgive me! Everyone has more understanding than Umar." He then returned to the pulpit and said, "O people! I had forbidden you from paying dowries in excess of four hundred Dirhams (the prohibition no longer stands). Therefore whoever wishes to give whatever he pleases from his wealth, he may do so."
sources: Surah Nisaa, verse 20.

paras: Hadhrat Sha'bi reports that Hadhrat umar bin Khattaab (RA) once delivered a

Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) reports, "I once brought Rasulullaah ﷺ some Hareerah that I had cooked. Sauda was sitting between between Rasulullaah ﷺ and I, so I told her to have some as well. When she refused, I said, 'If you do not eat, I shall smear it on your face.' She however still refused so I put my hand in the Hareerah and plastered it on her face. Rasulullaah ﷺ laughed as he put his hand in it saying, 'Now you smear her face.' Sauda then smeared it on my face and again Rasulullaah ﷺ laughed. Just then Umar passed by calling out for (someone called) Abdullaah. Thinking that he would soon enter, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Get up and wash your faces!' Thereafter, I always stood in awe of Hadhrat Umar (RA) because of the respect Rasulullaah ﷺ had for him."

Another narration adds that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) said, "Rasulullaah ﷺ lowered his knee for Sauda (to step on) so that she could get even with me. She then took some (Hareerah) from the dish and spread it on my face as Rasulullaah ﷺ laughed."
sources: Abu Ya'la Haythami (Vol. 4 Pg.316) has commented on the chain of narrators. Ibn Asaakir has reported a similar narration, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Unimaal. Pg 393), as has lbn Najjaar, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal Pg.302),

paras: Hadhrat Razeenah (RA) who was a freed slave of Rasulullaah ﷺ reports that Hadhrat Sauda Yamaaniyyah (RA) once visited Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) at a time when Hadhrat Hafsah (RA) was with her. Hadhrat Sauda (RA) arrived looking stunning and well-dressed with a Yemeni shawl and matching scarf. She also wore two spots of aloe and saffron on their places (near her eyes) which resembled two pimples. A narrator called Ulayla says that she found women beautifying themselves with aloe and saffron.

Hadhrat Hafsah (RA) said to Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA), "O Ummul Mu'mineen! Rasulullaah ﷺ is due to arrive when this woman is gleaming here between us." "Fear Allaah, O Hafsah!" Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) warned. However, Hadhrat Hafsah said, "I am going to ruin her adornment for her." Hadhrat Sauda who was hard of hearing asked, "What are you two saying?" "O Sauda!" Hadhrat Hafsah (RA) said, "The one-eyed (Dajjaal) has appeared!" "Really!

Hadhrat Sauda (RA). cried out. She was extremely shocked and started to shiver. "Where shall I hide?" she asked. 'You will have to go to the tent," Hadhrat Hafsah told her. The tent was made of palm leaves and was a hiding place for the people, it was however filled with dirt and spider webs. Hadhrat Sauda went to hide there as Rasulullaah ﷺ arrived. Seeing the two women laughing so much that they were unable to talk, Rasulullaah ﷺ asked, "What is all the laughter about?" Rasulullaah ﷺ had to repeat the question thrice before they pointed towards the tent. Rasulullaah ﷺ went to the tent where he found Hadhrat Sauda (RA) shivering (with fear). "What is the matter, O Sauda?" Rasulullaah ﷺ asked. "O Rasulullaah iii?!" she said, "The one-eyed one has appeared." "He has not appeared," Rasulullaah ﷺ clarified, "but he is still to appear. He has not appeared but is still to appear." Rasulullaah ﷺ then helped her out and dusted the dirt and spider webs off her.
sources: Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.4 Pg.316) has commented on the chain of narrators. (3) ibn Adi and lbn Asaakir, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzui Ummaal (Vol.4 Pg.393).

paras: Another narration adds that Hadhrat Hafsah (RA) said to Hadhrat Aa'isha "Rasulullaah ilil is coming to see us and we are looking so unkempt while she is gleaming between us." Rasulullaah ﷺ Relationship with Hadhrat Aa'isha Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates, "Rasulullaah ﷺ was sitting down when he heard the people and children making a lot of noise. (When he looked out) He saw some Abyssinians dancing with the people around them. Aa'isha!' Rasulullaah ﷺ called out, 'Come and have a look.' Placing my cheek against his shoulder, I started looking from between his shoulders and head, 'o Aa'isha,' Rasulullaah ﷺ kept saying I kept looking for a long time), 'have you not had your fill?' To assess my status with Rasulullaah ﷺ, I kept saying that I had not. I saw Rasulullaah ﷺ taking support on one leg and then the other (as he grew tired of standing so long), when Umar appeared, the people and children all dispersed and Rasulullaah ilii remarked, 'I see the human and Jinn devils all flee from Umar The narration still continues further.
sources: Bukhaari and Muslim, as quoted in Mishkaatul Masaabeeh (Pg.272). (Vol-2) 691 collaborated and that whichever of us Rasulullaah ﷺ came to would tell him, 'I get the smell of. Have you eaten Maghaafeer (suggesting that the bees that made the honey ate Maghafeer).' Consequently, when Rasulullaah ﷺ came to one of us, she said the piece. Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, 'Not at all. But I did have honey by Zaynab bint jahash. I shall however never do so again.' It was then that Allaah revealed the verses: •>?„' i ', ,'M ' , ' »' > '< e Vt -"tii Si ' .* *,, J't''u '*' ' £ £ ' -i s idsa 01 t_jjP ^ */ (i lj) ^ o' V O Nabi ﷺ In seeking the pleasure of your wives, why do you declare unlawful that which Allaah has made lawful for you? Allaah is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful. Allaah has ordained that you release yourselves from your oaths (such as this one and pay the relevant Kaffaara). Allaah is your Protecting Friend and He is the All Knowing, the Wise, (The Incident deserves mention) When the Nabi ﷺ whispered something to one of his wives (Rasulullaah ﷺ 's statement, "But I did have honey") and she informed (another of his wives) about it. When Allaah disclosed this to him, he made a part of it (his knowledge of the incident) known (to her) and ignored a part of it (to save her from added embarrassment). When he informed her about it, she exclaimed, "Who told you about it?" He replied, "The All Knowing, The Informed One told me." If the two of you (Hafsa and Aa'isha) repent to Allaah, then your hearts have surely turned (turned back towards the best course after straying for a while). Tahreem, verses Hadhrat Hishaam says that the words "When the Nabi ﷺ whispered something to one of his wives" refer to the statement Rasulullaah ﷺ made to one of his wives when he said, "1 shall never do so (drink honey) again and this is a vow. However, you should not inform anyone about this." ® Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ loved sweet things and honey. After performing the Asr salaah, it was his practice to visit all his wives and get close to one of them. When he once went to Hafsah the daughter of Hadhrat Umar (RA), he stayed longer than he usually stayed. Overcome with covetousness, I made enquiries about this and was informed that a woman from her family had given her a container of honey, which she mixed into a drink and gave Rasulullaah ﷺ , 'By Allaah!' I resolved, 'I am definitely going to make some scheme.'
Maghaafer is the odorous resin of a particular type of palm tree called the Urfut palm.

paras: In another narration, Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) says, "By Allaah! I saw Rasulullaah standing at the door of my room as some Abyssinians amused the people with their spears in the of the) Masjid. Rasulullaah ﷺ screened me with his shawl as I watched their feats between his ear and shoulder. Rasulullaah ﷺ then remained standing because of me until I tired and) turned away. You can well imagine how eager a young girl (as I) is for amusement (and for how long I stood watching)."
sources: Bukhaari and Muslim.

paras: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) reports, "Rasulullaah ﷺ used to spend time at Zaynab bint jahash's place drinking honey, Hafsah and I therefore I then said to Sauda bint Zam'ah, 'Rasulullaah (Self will soon be coming to you. When he gets close to you, ask him whether he ate Maghaafeer. When he tells you that he has not eaten any, ask him what it is then that you can smell. He will then tell you that Hafsah gave him a drink of honey, to which you should say, 'The bee must have sucked nectar from the Urfut palm (the palm containing Maghaafeer)! I will also say the same thing and you O Saflyya should also do likewise."

Hadhrat Sauda (RA) later reported (to Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA)), "By Allaah! Because of my fear for you, I almost called out what you told while Rasulullaah was still standing at the door. (Controlling myself however) When he drew closer, I said, 'O Rasulullaah ﷺ -Have you eaten Maghaafeer? 'No,' he replied. 'Then what is that I smell on you?' I asked. He replied, 'Hafsah gave me a drink of honey.' I then said, 'The bee must have sucked nectar from the Urfut palm.'" When Rasulullaah ﷺ went to Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA), shealsosaid the same thing and Hadhrat Safiyya (RA) also followed suit. When Rasulullaah ﷺ again went to Hadhrat Hafsah (RA) and she offered him some honey to drink, he declined saying, "I do not need any." "By Allaah!" Hadhrat Sauda (RA) said to Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA), "we have stopped Rasulullaah ﷺ from honey." "Be quiet!" Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) told her. (1 '

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) reports, "I had always been eager to ask Umar about the two wives of Rasulullaah ﷺ concerning whom Allaah 'If the two of you repent to Allaah, then your hearts have surely turned (turned back towards the best course after straying for a while)! (Surah Tahreem, verse 4) This (thought) lingered on until the time when Umar performed Hajj and I performed Hajj with him. We were still travelling when Umar went off the road (to answer the call the nature). I also veered off taking a jug (of water) along with me. After he had completed, Umar came to me and I started pouring water into his hands as he made wudhu. 'O Ameerul Mu'mineen!' I said, 'Who were the two wives of Rasulullaah ﷺ concerning whom Allaah says: If the two of .you repent to Allaah, then your hearts have surely turned (turned back towards the best course after straying for a whiiej.'?" (Surah Tahreem, verse 4) Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "I am surprised at you, O Ibn Abbaas! (That despite your vast knowledge, you are still unaware of this incident)." Hadhrat Zuhri comments that although Hadhrat Umar (RA) was surprised at the question, he enter. Yet again the slave went in and emerged saying, 'I mentioned your name to him but he merely remained silent.' As I turned to leave, the slave suddenly called for me saying. You may enter, for Rasulullaah ﷺ has granted you permission.' When I entered, I four.d Rasulullaah ﷺ reclining against a straw mat that had left imprints on his side. 'Have you divorced your wives, O Rasulullaah ﷺ I asked. Raising his head, he replied, 'Allaahu Akbar!' I cried out. I then said, 'O Rasulullaah ﷺ You have seen that we the members of the Quraysh always had the upper hand over our wives. When we arrived in Madinah, we encountered people Ansaar) whose women had the upper hand over them. Our women then started learning from their women. When I became angry with my wife one day (and told her something), she surprised me by back chatting. When I objected to her back chatting, she said, What are you objecting about my back chatting when I can swear by Allaah that the wives of Rasulullaah ilif backchat to him? In fact some of them (when angry) shun him morning to evening. I said, of them does that is at a loss and destroyed! Does any of them not fear that Allaah would be angry with her because His Rasool ﷺ is angry with her? She will then most certainly be destroyed.' This made Rasulullaah ﷺ smile. - 'O Rasulullaah ﷺ I continued, 'I then went to Hafsah and told her, 'Never be deceived by the fact that your companion (Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA)) is prettier than you and more beloved to Rasulullaah ﷺ Rasulullaah ﷺ smiled again. Then I asked, 'Should I continue with this light-hearted talk?' 'By all means,' Rasulullaah ﷺ said. I then sat down and I swear by Allaah that when I looked about the room, all I saw was three pieces of undyed leather. 'O Rasulullaah I said, 'Pray to Allaah to grant an abundance of wealth to your Ummah. Allaah has given abundance to the Romans and Persians even though they do not worship Him he will readily give us as well).'

Rasulullaah ﷺ then sat up straight and said, 'Are you also in doubt, O son of Khattaab? They are people whose rewards (for their good deeds) have been brought forward to this world (without any share left for the Aakhirah).' I then quickly said, 'Do seek forgiveness for me, O Rasulullaah ﷺ .' Because he was so angry with them at the time, Rasulullaah till had vowed not to go to his wives for an entire month until Allaah directed him otherwise."
sources: Ahmad, Bukhaari, Muslim, Tirmidhi and Nasa'ee.

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "When Rasulullaah ﷺ separated from his wives, I entered the Masjid where I saw the people fondling pebbles as they said, 'Rasulullaah ﷺ has divorced his wives!' This incident took place before the injunction of Hijaab was ordained, I said to myself, 'I am going to find out properly what is happening Rasulullaah g!8f had divorced them or not).'" The Hadith continues to mention how Hadhrat Umar (RA) went to both Hadhrat Hafsah (RA) as well as Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) to admonish them. Thereafter, the narration quotes Hadhrat Umar (RA) who says, "When I then went to Rasulullaah ﷺ, I found him on the doorstep of the room on the upper storey. I called out saying, 'O Secure permission for me to see Rasulullaah ﷺ ..."' The rest of the narration is like the one above until the part where Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "O Rasulullaah iffif ! Do not let the matter of your wives disturb you. If you have divorced them, then Allaah is with you as well as His angels, Jibreel, Mikaal, myself, Abu Bakr and all the Mu'mineen. I praise Allaah for the fact that whenever I "spoke, I had firm hope that Allaah would confirm what I said. It was therefore with reference to this that Allaah revealed the following verse: if the two of you and Aa'isha, two wives of Rasulullaah ﷺ repent to Allaah, then your hearts have surely turned (turned back towards the best course after straying for a while.). However, if you two assist each other against him (Rasulullaah ﷺ), then his protecting friends are Allaah, Jibreel and the pious Mu'mineen. Besides these, the angels are also his assistants. If he (Rasulullaah ﷺ) has to divorce all of you (wives), then his Rabb shall certainly replace you with wives better than yourselves who will be Muslims, Mu'minaat, obedient, repentant, worshippers, women who fast, previously married women and virgins. (Surah Tahreem, verses 4,5)

'Have you divorced them?' I asked. 'No,' Rasulullaah ﷺ replied. I then stood at the door of the Masjid and called out in my loudest voice, "Rasulullaah ﷺ's wives have not been divorced!' it was with reference to this that Allaah revealed the verse: :s.uaJl 5j_j-j) '1 J-)'

If they had (first) referred the matter to the Rasulullaah ﷺ and to those of them who have understanding (to the learned Muslims with insight), it would surely be known to those of them who research (verify) the matter. (Surah Nisaa, verse 83)
Hadhrat Umar (RA) continues, "it was I who researched this matter."
sources: Muslim, as quoted in Tafseerot Ibn Katheer (Vol.4 Pg.389). Abdur Razzaaq, lbn Sa'd, lbn Hibbaan, Bayhaqi, lbn Jareer, lbn Mundhir, lbn Mardway and other have reported a similar narration, as quoted in Kaniul ' t/mmaaJ Pg.269).

paras: Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ was sitting in his house while the Sahabah (RA) were sitting by his door. When Hadhrat Abu Bakr arrived and sought permission to enter, Rasulullaah ﷺ did not grant him permission. Hadhrat Umar (RA) then arrived and Rasulullaah ﷺ did not grant him permission to enter either. Rasulullaah ﷺ later granted permission to both Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) and Hadhrat Umar (RA) and they both entered the room where Rasulullaah ﷺ was sitting in silence with his wives around him. Hadhrat Umar (RA) said to himself, "I am going to say something to make Rasulullaah ﷺ laugh." He then proceeded to say, "O Rasulullaah fli?! If only you had seen (my wife) the daughter of Zaid just now when I slapped her across the neck when she asked me for (an increase in her) allowance!" Rasulullaah ﷺ smiled so broadly that his molars became visible. He said, "Here are my wives around me also asking me for (an increase in) their allowances."

Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) then stood up to hit (his daughter) Hadhrat Aa'isha and Hadhrat Umar (RA) also got up to hit (his daughter) Hadhrat Hafsah Both men were rebuking their daughters saying, "How can you ask Rasulullaah ﷺ for something he does not have?!" Rasulullaah ﷺ however stopped the two men and the women said, "By Allaah! After this, we shall never again ask Rasulullaah iil? for something he does not have." It was on this occasion that Allaah revealed the verse offering a choice (to Rasulullaah ﷺ wives). Rasulullaah ﷺ first approached Hadhrat Aa'isha saying, "I am about to present to you an offer that I do not want you to be hasty in deciding until you have consulted with your parents." "What is it?" she asked. Rasulullaah ﷺ then recited for her the verse: O Nabi ﷺ Say to your wives, "if you desire the life of this world and its adornments, then come forward. I shall grant you a generous provision and separate from you (divorce you) in a cordial manner.

However, if you desire Allaah, His Rasool ﷺ and the home of the Aakhirah, then (you may continue enjoying the status of being his wives and living with the allowance he provides because) Allaah has certainly prepared a grand reward for those of you who do good deeds (Allaah will reward you tremendously for your sacrifice)." (Surah Ahzaab, verses 28,29)

Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) immediately said, "Should I consult my parents about (having) you?! I definitely choose Allaah and His Rasool ﷺ. Please do not inform any of your other wives what I have decided." Rasulullaah ﷺ told her, "Allaah has sent me to make matters easy for people and not to make them difficult Therefore, if any of them asks me about you decision, I will certainly inform her,"
sources: Ahmad, Muslim and Nasa'ee; (2) ibn Abi Haatim. Bukhaari and Muslim have reported a similar narration.

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas Slifflg reports that Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) said, "When the verses giving (us) the choice were revealed, Rasulullaah ﷺ began with me before any of his other wives. He said, 'I am about to present to you a choice about which you are in no hurry to decide until you have consulted with your parents.' Rasulullaah ﷺ said this despite knowing well that my parents would never tell me to separate from Rasulullaah ﷺ. Rasulullaah ﷺ then continued, 'Allaah says: Sp-?! a-5j2 O Nabi ﷺ Say to your wives, "If you desire the life of this world and its adornments, then come forward. I shall grant you a generous provision and separate from you (divorce you) in a cordial manner.

However, if you desire Allaah, His Rasool ﷺ and the home of the Aakhirah, then (you may continue enjoying the status of being his wives and living with the allowance he provides because) Allaah has certainly prepared a grand reward for those of you who do good deeds (Allaah will reward you tremendously for your sacrifice)." (Surah Ahzaab, verses 28,29)

Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) says, "I immediately .said, "Is there anything to consult my parents about? I certainly want Allaah, His Rasool ﷺ and the home of the Aakhirah.'" Rasulullaah ﷺ then presented the choice to all his wives and the reply each of them gave was similar to that of Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA)
Another narration quotes that Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) said, "When Rasulullaah gave us a choice and we chose (to remain with) him, he did not count this (choice as a divorce) against us." ®

Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once said to her, "I know exactly when you are happy with me and when you are angry." When she asked Rasulullaah ﷺ how he knew that, he replied, "When you are happy with me, you say, 'No, by the Rabb of Muhammad ﷺ and when you are angry with me, you say, 'No, by the Rabb of Ibraheem "That's true," Hadhrat Aa'isha said, "but it is only your name that I leave out (while the love for you in my heart remains just as strong)."
sources: Bukhaari, Muslim and Ahmad, as quoted in Tafseerof ibn Katheer (Vol.3 Pg.48i) (4! Bukhaari and Muslim, as quoted in Mishkaatul Masaabeeh (Pg.272). 698. (Vol-2) when I ran a race with him and beat him. After I had put on some weight, I again ran a race with him, but this time he beat me. He then said, 'This is in lieu of the lastrace.",(1) Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) relates, "(As a young boy) I was once the guest of (my maternal aunt) Maymoona on a night when she was not performing salaah. She brought one shawl and then another, which she lay it down by the head-side of the bedding. She then lay down, pulled the shawl over her and made a bed for me beside her. I shared her pillow with her. Rasulullaah ﷺ arrived after performing the Isha salaah and when he reached the bed, he took the shawl lying by the head-side of the bed and tied it as a lower garment. Thereafter, he removed the two garments he was wearing, hung them up and got in to the bed with his wife. Towards the final hours of the night, he got up and took a water bag that was hanging there. He opened it and started making wudhu. I was about to get up to pour the water for him when it occurred to me that I would not like him to know that I had been awake. He then came to the bed, got dressed in his two garments and removed the shawl. Thereafter, he stood at the place where he performed salaah and started performing salaah. I also got up, made wudhu and stood on his left. Rasulullaah ﷺ held me from his back and made me stand on his right. With me following him, he then proceeded to perform thirteen Rakaahs of salaah. Rasulullaah ﷺ then sat down and as I sat beside him, his cheek leaned towards mine (as he fell asleep) and I could hear him breathing like a sleeping person. Bilaal then arrived and called out, 'Salaah, O Rasulullaah ﷺ Rasulullaah ﷺ then stood up in the place where he performed salaah and started performing two Rakaahs salaah as Bilaal started calling out the Iqaamah."

paras: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates, "I was once on a journey with Rasulullaah ﷺ anyone else.1 Rasulullaah iisl explained, 'She used to visit us when Khadeeja was alive. Do you not know that honouring bonds of affection is a part of Imaan?'"

Hadhrat Abu Tufayl (RA) relates, "I saw Rasulullaah ﷺ distributing meat in Ji'irraanah when I was a young boy who could carry only the limb of a camel. When a particular lady came to him, he spread out his shawl for her (to sit on). When I asked someone who she was, I was informed that she was the woman who suckled him as a baby."
sources: Bukhaari in his Adab (Pg.188).

paras: Hadhrat Umar (RA) reports that when he once went to see Rasulullaah ﷺ. Rasulullaah ﷺ 's short Abyssinian slave was busy rubbing his back. "O Rasulullaah ﷺ Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked, "Did you hurt yourself?" Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, "The camel dropped me down last night."
sources: Tabraani and Bazzaar, as quoted in Kamul Ummaal (Vol.4 Pg.44).

paras: Hadhrat Qaasim bin Abdur Rahmaan reports that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood used to put on Rasulullaah ﷺ 's shoes for him. He would then walk ahead with Rasulullaah ﷺ 's staff in his hand. When Rasulullaah ﷺ reached the gathering, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) would remove Rasulullaah ﷺ's shoes, place it under his arms and hand the staff over. As soon as Rasulullaah ﷺ decided to get up, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood would give him his shoes and again walk ahead with the staff until he entered the room before Rasulullaah Sip.

Another narration state that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) used to screen Rasulullaah ﷺ when he bathed, would wake him up when he slept and would walk about with him when there was no one else. ®

Hadhrat Anas (RA) says, "When Rasulullaah ﷺ arrived in Madinah, I was a young boy of ten and when he passed away, I was only twenty. It was my mother and aunts who encouraged me to serve Rasulullaah ﷺ
sources: IbnSa'd(Vol.3Pg.l53).

paras: Hadhrat Thumaamah narrates that when someone asked Hadhrat Anas (RA) whether he was present during the Battle of Badr, he replied, "Shame on you! How could I ever absent myself?" Hadhrat Muhammad bin Abdullaah Ansaari reports that Hadhrat Anas (RA) accompanied Rasulullaah ﷺ to Badr to serve him while he was still a young boy. one of them (the narrator is unsure) arrived and climbed upon his back. When Rasulullaah ﷺ got up, he held the child or the two children with his hand and (after completing the salaah) said, "What an excellent mount you had Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) says that he once went to Rasulullaah ﷺ as he was on all fours with Hadhrat Hasan (RA) and Hadhrat Husayn (RA) on his back. Rasulullaah ﷺ was saying, "You two have an excellent camel and are both excellent loads,"
sources: Ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Nu'aym. (5) lbn Sa'd and lbn Asaakir, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.5 Pg.141). 700 Ot (Vol-2) The Services that the Ansaar Youth and the Sahabah (RA) Rendered to Rasulullaah ﷺ Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that there were twenty youngsters from the Ansaar who always stuck close to Rasulullaah ﷺ. Rasulullaah ﷺ would always dispatch them whenever he needed something done. ''' Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA) reports that there were always four or five Sahabah (RA) who never parted from Rasulullaah ﷺ (when on journey) or from Rasulullaah ﷺ's door (when at home). '2' Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA) relates, "We used to take turns (to be at Rasulullaah ﷺ's service) so that we could fulfil any need he had or he could dispatch us for any errand. Eventually, the people anticipating rewards (for this service) increased and there were plenty of people taking turns. As we were one day discussing Dajjaal, Rasulullaah ﷺ came out to ask, 'What are these whispered discussions all about? Have I not forbidden you from whispered discussion?'"'3' Hadhrat Assim bin Sufyaan says that it was either Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) or Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) whom he heard say, "I once sought permission from Rasulullaah ﷺ to spend the night at his door so that he could awaken me for any need he may have. Rasulullaah ﷺ granted permission and 1 spent the night there."
Tabraani, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.9 Pg.182).

paras: Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) reports that it was midday when they were sitting around Rasulullaah tflf and Hadhrat Ummu Ayman (RA) arrived saying, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ Hasan and Husayn are lost!" Rasulullaah ﷺ said to the Sahabah (RA), "Get up and look for my sons!" Every person went in the direction he was facing and Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) went in the direction Rasulullaah ﷺ went. Rasulullaah ﷺ kept searching until he was at the foot of a mountain when he saw the two boys clinging on to each other. In front of them was a snake standing on its tail with flames flashing from its mouth (Allaah had perhaps sent it to ensure that the boys ventured no further). As Rasulullaah darted towards it, it turned to look at him and then slid away into a hole. Rasulullaah ﷺ then went to the boys and as he separated them, he wiped their faces saying, "May my parents be sacrificed for you! How honourable you two are in the sight of Allaah!" when he then carried one of them on his right shoulder and the other on his left shoulder, Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) remarked, "Glad tidings to you two. What an excellent mount you have!" To this, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "What excellent riders are they and their father is even better than them."
sources: Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.9 Pg.182) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) says, "We were with Rasulullaah ﷺ when we were invited for a meal. When we came across Husayn playing with other children in the street, Rasulullaah ﷺ ran ahead of the others and stretched out his hands (to grab the boy). Husayn started running to and fro as Rasulullaah ﷺ made him laugh in front of everyone there. Rasulullaah ﷺ then stretched out his arms and held the boy with one hand on his chin and the other between his head and ears. Thereafter, Rasulullaah ﷺ hugged and kissed him saying, 'Husayn is from me and I am from him. May Allaah love those who love him. Hasan and Husayn are two (distinguished) grandsons from amongst grandsons. ",
sources: Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.9 Pg.182) has commented on the chain of narrators. Tabraani has reported a similar narration from Hadhrat Ya'la bin Murrah, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.7 Pg.107).

paras: Hadhrat ibn is'haaq Sabee'ee reports that the wife of Hadhrat uthmaan bin Madh'oon once came to the wives of Rasulullaah ﷺ dressed in unattractive and old clothes. When they asked her what the problem was, she informed them that her husband stood in salaah all night and fasted all day (and therefore had no time for her, because of which she felt no need to look attractive), when Rasulullaah ﷺ was informed of what she said, he met Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Madh'oon (RA), rebuked him and said, "Do you not have an excellent example in me?" Hadhrat uthmaan bin Madh'oon (RA) replied, "Certainly. May my parents be sacrificed for you!" Thereafter, his wife was always looking attractive and wearing enchanting scents. On his deathbed, his wife recited some couplets (which meant): "Dear eyes! Be generous with your tears and never let them stop Over the demise of Uthmaan bin Madh'oon Over a man who spent the entire night pleasing his Creator Over the loss of someone who will be buried. Glad tidings ofjannah to him!

Baqee ^ and its Gharqad trees are graced to be his home And after being troubled (by having Kuffaar buried there), the ground shall be illuminated All that the heart shall inherit will be grief that knows no end Until death comes, my tear ducts shall never dry"
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg,l06). Ibn Sa'd (Vol.3 Pg.394) has reported a similar narration without the couplets.

paras: Another narration names the wife of Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Madh'oon (RA) as Hadhrat Khowla bint Hakeem (RA) and that it was Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) whom she visited. The narration also states that Rasulullaah ﷺ said to Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Madh'oon (RA) Uthmaan! Monasticism has not been ordained or us. Am I not a perfect example for you? By Allaah! It is I who fears most and who is most mindful of the limits He has set."
sources: Abdur Razzaaq, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.8 Pg.305) .

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr bin Al Aas reports, "My father got me married to a woman from the Quraysh. However, when she first came to me, I paid no attention to her because of my overriding enthusiasm for acts of Ibaadah such as salaah and fasting. (My father) Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas (RA) once came to his daughter-in-law (my wife) and asked, 'How do you find your husband?' She ( 1 ) The graveyard of Madinah. replied, 'He is the best of husbands but has not yet ventured to expose any part of my body and has not even come near our bed.' My father then came to me and rebuked me most severely. Biting into me with his tongue, he said, 'I got you married to an honourable lady of the Quraysh and you have left her dangling in suspension?!' After enumerating more of the things I was doing, he then went to complain about me to Rasulullaah ﷺ.

Rasulullaah ﷺ sent for me and when I arrived, he verified, 'Do you fast every day?' Yes,' I replied. He then asked further, 'And do you stand in salaah all night?' When I again replied in the affirmative, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, 'But while 1 fast regularly, there are also days when I do not fast. While I perform salaah (at night) I also sleep and I also touch my wives. Whoever turns away from my way of life cannot be my follower.' Rasulullaah ﷺ then proceeded to say, 'Complete a recitation of the Qur'aan once a month.' 'But I can do more than that,' I said. 'Then complete it once every ten days,' Rasulullaah ﷺ permitted. When I ' insisted that I could do more than that as well, Rasulullaah ﷺ told me that I could then complete a recitation in three days.

Thereafter, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, 'Fast only three days a month.' when I informed Rasulullaah ﷺ that I was capable of much more, he continued increasing the number of days until he finally said, 'Then fast one day and skip the next. This is the best type of fast and was the manner in which my brother Dawood used to fast.'"

In his narration, Hadhrat Husayn states that Rasulullaah ﷺ added, "Every keen worshipper has a period of great enthusiasm but every such period comes with a waning phase. When this phase comes, the person either resorts to the Sunnah or towards Bid'ah. Whoever during this phase resorts towards the Sunnah has been rightly guided and whoever turns towards Bid'ah has been destroyed."

Hadhrat Mujaahid says that when Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr bin Al Aas grew old and weak, he would fast several days consecutively and then skip several days to regain his strength. When reciting the Qur'aan he would also sometimes recite more and sometimes less. Nevertheless, he would ensure that he completed a recitation within a period of either seven days or three days. Thereafter (when he grew even weaker), he would say, "Had I accepted the concession Rasulullaah ﷺ offered me, I would have liked it more than what (extra Ibaadah) he had to send my way (because of my insistence). However, (I shall now not reduce it because) I would not like to do anything other than what I was doing at the time I separated from Rasulullaah ﷺ (when he passed away)."
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.285). Bukhaari has also reported a similar narration, as quoted in Safwatus Safwah (Vol. 1 Pg.27 1). (Vol-2) 705 brotherhood between Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) and Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA). When Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) once came to visit, Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA), he found (his wife) Hadhrat Ummu Dardaa (RA) in a dishevelled condition. When he enquired what the matter was, she replied, "Your brother Abu Dardaa has no need for this world." Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) then arrived and when he got a meal prepared for Hadhrat Salmaan (RA), he said, "You eat because I am fasting." Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) refused saying, "I shall not eat until you eat." Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) was then forced to (terminate the fast and) join in the meal. That night when Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) started to perform salaah, Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) instructed him to sleep. Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) slept awhile and was again about to get up when Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) again told him to go back to sleep. It was only when the night was drawing to an end that Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) said to Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA), 'You may now get up." The two men then performed (Tahajjud) salaah. Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) then advised Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) saying, "You have rights owing to your Rabb as well as rights owing to your body and rights owing to your wife. You should therefore give every recipient their due rights." When Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) reported the matter to Rasulullaah ﷺ, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Salmaan is right."

paras: Hadhrat Abu Juhayfah (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ had made a bond of met me while I was carrying the date stones on my head. When he made his camel sit down for me to ride on, I felt too shy and also thought of your possessiveness.' He said, 'By Allaahl Your carrying the date stones is more difficult for me to bear than your riding with Rasulullaah ﷺ This continued until (my father) Abu Bakr sent me a servant who relieved me of tending to the horse and it seemed like he had set me free."
sources: IbnSa'd(VoI.8Pg.251).

paras: Another narration states that Hadhrat Asmaa (RA) the daughter of Hadhrat Abu Bakr was married to Hadhrat Zubayr bin Awwaam (RA). When she complained to her father about her husband's strict nature, Hadhrat Abu Bakr said, "Dear daughter! Be patient because when a woman has a pious husband and she does not remarry after he dies, Allaah will reunite them in jannah." ,

Hadhrat Kahmas Hilaali reports that they were once sitting with Hadhrat Umar when a lady arrived. She sat down and said, "O Ameerul Mu'mineen! While the evil nature of my husband has increased, his good nature has dwindled." "Who is your husband?" Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked. When she informed him that her husband was a man called Abu Salamah, Hadhrat Umar said, "He was a companion of Rasulullaah ﷺ and is a righteous man." He then asked the men around him, "Is he not so?" "O Ameerul Mu'mineen!" they replied, "We know him to be just as you say." Hadhrat Umar (RA) then instructed someone sitting there to call for the husband. When her husband was sent for, the lady got up and sat behind Hadhrat Umar (RA). It was not long before the two men arrived together and the husband sat in front of Hadhrat Umar (RA). "What has this woman sitting behind me have to say?" Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked. "Who is she, O Ameerul Mu'mineen?" the man asked. "She is your wife," Hadhrat Umar (RA) replied. "And what has she to say?" he asked. Hadhrat Umar (RA) replied, "She claims that while your evil nature has increased, your good nature has dwindled." The husband said, "A terrible thing she has said, O Ameerul Mu'mineen! She is amongst the most righteous women of her tribe, in addition to this, she also has the most clothing and the most comfortable home. However, her husband is an old man." Addressing the wife, Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked, "And what have you to say?" "He has spoken the truth," she replied. ' Hadhrat Umar (RA) got up with his whip and struck her with it saying, "O enemy of yourself! You have eaten his wealth and finished his youth and then go even further to make false allegations against him!" "O Ameerul Mu'mineen!" she pleaded, "Do not be hasty. I swear by Allaah that I shall never sit in this position (as complainant against my husband) ever again."

Hadhrat Umar (RA) then instructed that she be given three garments and said, "Take this in lieu of what I have done to you (when I hit you). However, I am warning you never to complain about this old man again." The narrator says, "(I remember the incident so vividly that) it is as if I can actually see her standing up with those garments." Hadhrat Umar (RA) then turned to her husband and said, "Let not what you have seen me do to her ever provoke you to treat her badly." The husband promised that he would not and they both left. Hadhrat Umar then said, "I have heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say, 'The best period of my Ummah is that in which I am (the first period), followed by the second period and then the third. Thereafter, such people shall come who will take oaths before testifying and who will testify before being asked to do so. They will also be people whose marketplaces will be very noisy.m
sources: Tayaalisi, Bukhaari in his Taareekh and Haakim in his Kuna, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.8 Pg.303). Abu Bakr bin Abu Aasim has also reported the narration, as quoted in Isaabah (Vol.4 Pg.93).

paras: Hadhrat Sha'bi narrates that a woman once came to Hadhrat Umar (RA) saying, "I have come to complain to you about a man who is the best of all men apart from a man whose deeds are superior or whose deeds match his. He stands in salaah all night until dawn and fasts all day until evening." She was then overcome with bashfulness and said, "Excuse me, O Ameerul Mu'mineen." "May Allaah reward you tremendously," Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, 'You have certainly praised him well. You are excused." When she left, Hadhrat Ka'b bin Soor remarked, "O Ameerul Mu'mineen! She has certainly been eloquent in her complaint to you." "What was her complaint?" Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked. "Her husband," Hadhrat Ka'b replied.

Hadhrat Umar (RA) then sent for the couple and (when they arrived) said to Hadhrat Ka'b, "Now you pass judgement between them." Hadhrat Ka'b said, "How can I pass judgement when you are present?" Hadhrat Umar (RA) insisted saying, "it was you who understood what I did not." Hadhrat Ka'b then said, "Allaah has mentioned: "then marry two, three of four women with whom you are pleased (to have as your wives)." (Surah Nisaa, verse 3) You should therefore fast for three days and then not fast the next day which you will spend with your wife. You may also spend three nights in salaah and then a night with your wife." Hadhrat Umar (RA) remarked, "This (decision) I find more astounding than your first statement." Hadhrat Umar (RA) then appointed him as judge of Basrah.
sources: Ibn Sa'd. 708 (Vol-2) with me and do not shy away from the truth." She then said, "O Ameerul Mu'mineenl I am a woman who desires what all women desire." ^' Hadhrat Qataadah narrates that a woman once said to Hadhrat Umar (RA), "My husband stands in salaah all night and fasts all day." Hadhrat Umar (RA) said to her, "Are you instructing me to stop him from performing salaah at night and from fasting during the day?" She then went away, but returned some time later with the same complaint. Hadhrat Umar (RA) again repeated what he had said the first time. However, Hadhrat Ka'b bin Soor pointed out, "O Ameerul Mu'mineenl She has a right." "What is her right?" Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked. Hadhrat Ka'b replied, "Allaah has permitted four wives for him, so count her as one of four. She is therefore entitled to one night in every four nights and one day in every four days." Hadhrat Umar (RA) then summoned the husband and instructed him to spend one of every four nights with her ana' to skip a fast in every four fasts. ^ The Incident of Hadhrat Abu Gharzah (RA) and Hadhrat Umar • (RA) Hadhrat Abu Gharzah (RA) once led Hadhrat Ibn Arqam by the hand to his wife and asked her, "Do you hate me." "Yes I do," she replied. "What made you do this?" Hadhrat Ibn Arqam (RA) asked. Hadhrat Abu Gharzah (RA) explained, "People have been saying too many things about me." When Hadhrat Ibn Arqam (RA) reported the matter to Hadhrat Umar (RA), the Ameerul Mu'mineen called for Hadhrat Abu Gharzah (RA) and asked, "What made you do that?" Again Hadhrat Abu Gharzah (RA) replied, "People have been saying too many things about me." Hadhrat Umar (RA) then sent for the wife. She arrived with the shrewd aunt of hers who told her, "When he questions you (about your curt statement), say, 'Because he made me say it on oath, I did not like to tell a lie.'" (When she came before him) Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked, "What made you say what you did?" She replied, "Because he made me say it on oath, I did not like to tell a lie." Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "Why not? One of you ought to lie and say something nice because every home is not built on love. Many homes are built on polite interaction stemming from social status and Islaam." The Incident of Hadhrat Aatika (RA) the Daughter of Hadhrat Zaid bin Amr (RA) Hadhrat Abu Salamah bin Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf narrates that Hadhrat Aatika (RA) the daughter of Hadhrat Zaid bin Amr bin Nufayl (RA) was married to Hadhrat Abdullaah (RA) the son of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA). He loved her very much and even gave her an orchard on condition that she does not remarry after his death. He was struck by an arrow during the battle at Taa'if (l)Yashkari.

paras: Another narration states that Hadhrat Umar (RA) said to the lady, "Be honest and it was forty days after the demise of Rasulullaah ﷺ that the wound ruptured and he passed away. In his memory, Hadhrat Aatika (RA) recited the following couplets meant): "I swear that my eye shall always remain hot (with tears) over you and that my skin shall always be covered in dust (because I shall never adorn myself for anyone else)
(This I shall do) Forever, as long as the doves of the dense forest coo and as long as the night issues forth the bright morning"

When Hadhrat Umar (RA) proposed for her afterwards, she informed him that Hadhrat Abdullaah (RA) had given her an orchard with the condition that she should not remarry after him. Hadhrat Umar (RA) advised her to acquire a verdict from someone. She then enquired from Hadhrat Ali bin Abi Taalib (RA) whose verdict was that she was free to remarry after returning the orchard to the family of Hadhrat Abdullaah (RA). Hadhrat Umar (RA) then married her and invited a few Sahabah (RA) for the Waleemah meal. Amongst the guests was Hadhrat Ali (RA), who also happened to be the person with whom Hadhrat Abdullaah (RA) had made a bond of brotherhood. "Permit me to have a word with her (with your new bride)," Hadhrat Ali (RA) asked Hadhrat Umar With Hadhrat Umar (RA)'s permission, Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "O Aaatika!
'I swear that my eye shall always remain hot (with tears) over you and that my skin shall always be covered in dust'"
(Upon hearing this) Hadhrat Aatika (RA) started weeping very loudly. Hadhrat Umar said (to Hadhrat Ali (RA)), "May Allaah forgive you! Do not upset my wife's mood for me."
sources: Wakee, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal ' (Vol.8 Pg.302). ibn Sa'd has reported a similar narration, as quoted in isaabah (Vol.4 Pg.356).

paras: Hadhrat Nadbah the freed slave of Hadhrat Maymoonah (RA) reports that her mistress, (Hadhrat Maymoonah (RA)) once sent her to Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas. When she entered the house, she found that there were two beds. When she returned to Hadhrat Maymoonah (RA), she said, "It appears to me that Ibn Abbaas has separated from his wife." Hadhrat Maymoonah (RA) then sent for Ibn Abbaas's wife who was the daughter of Sarj findi. When she asked her about it, the wife replied, "There is nothing between us. I am only menstruating." Hadhrat Maymoonah (RA) then sent a message to Hadhrat Abdullarh bin Abbaas reprimanding him, "Are you averse to the Sunnah of Rasulullaah ﷺ Rasulullaah ﷺ used to touch his wives while they were menstruating and wearing a cloth that reached up to the knees or halfway down " the thighs."
sources: Abdur Razzaaq, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal WeA.5 Pg.138).

paras: Hadhrat ikrama says that he is not sure whether it was Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas who invited his cousin for a meal or whether it was his cousin who invited him. Nevertheless, while a slave woman was working in front of them (as they were eating), one of them called her an adulteress. "Stop that!" Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) cautioned, "Even though you will not be lashed for that (slander) in this world, you will certainly be punished in the Aakhirah." The cousin said, "But what if she is as I have said?" Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas replied, "Verily Mlaah does not like people who are vulgar and who adopt offensive language (it is therefore inappropriate for you to make such a statement)."
sources: Bukhaari in his Adab (Pg.49).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Imraan of Palestine reports that while the wife of Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas was busy cleaning his hair of lice, she called for her slave woman. When the slave delayed in arriving, Hadhrat Amr (RA)'s wife called her an adulteress. "Have you seen her commit adultery?" Hadhrat Amr (RA) asked. When his wife replied that she had not, Hadhrat (RA) said, "By Allaah! On the Day of Qiyaamah, you will certainly be lashed eighty times (as punishment for slander)." His wife then spoke to the slave and asked her for forgiveness. When the slave forgave her, Hadhrat Amr (RA) remarked, "She has no option but to forgive you because she is in your control. You had rather set her free." "Will that compensate for it?" his wife asked. "Perhaps," Hadhrat Amr (RA)

Hadhrat Abul Mutawakkil narrates that Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) had a Negro slave who had caused grief to the entire household because of something she had done. Raising his whip over her one day, Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) said, "Had it not been for Qisaas (on the Day of Qiyaamah), I would have beat you unconscious. However, I shall sell you to someone who pay your price in full. Go (free)! You are Allaah's."
sources: Ibn Asaakir, as quoted Kanzul Vmmaal (Vol.5 Pg.84).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Qais or ibn Abul Qais says that he was with the delegation of Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah bin jarraah (RA) that received Hadhrat Umar (RA) when he arrived in Shaam. As Hadhrat Umar (RA) was travelling, he was met by some entertainers from Adhri'aat who were carrying their swords (to entertain Hadhrat Umar (RA) as he entered their town). "Hold on!" Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "Stop them and send them back." "O Ameerul Mu'mineen!" Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah said, "This is the custom of the non-Arabs. If you stop them, they will think that you wish to annul the pact with them (that you wish to prevent them from freely practising their customs)." Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "Then leave them. Umar and his family are all under the command of Abu Ubaydah."
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.384), as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.7 Pg.334).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) reports that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) and Hadhrat, Zubayr (RA) once had a race, Hadhrat Zubayr (RA) beat Hadhrat Umar and cried out, "I beat you! By the Rabb of the Kabah!" when they raced a second time, Hadhrat Umar (RA) beat Hadhrat Zubayr (RA). Hadhrat Umar then called out, "I beat you! By the Rabb of the Kabah!"
sources: Muhaamili, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.7 Pg.334).

paras: Hadhrat Saleem bin Handhalah reports, "We once went to Hadhrat Ubay bin (RA) iliaiis to listen to Ahadeeth from him. (When he had completed) He stood up and we also stood up and walked with him. Hadhrat Umar (RA) then met him and said, "Don't you think that this (walking with people following you) is a danger (source of pride) for the one being followed and a source of dishonour for the ones following?"
sources: Ibn Abi Shaybah and Khateeb in his Jaami, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.8 Pg.6l).

paras: Hadhrat Abul Bakhtari narrates that a man once came to Hadhrat Salmaan and said, "How pleasant was the behaviour of people today! I had been travelling and I swear by Allaah that every person I stayed with seemed to be the son of my own father. Each one of them treated me exceptionally well and was extremely kind towards me." Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) said, "My dear brother's son! That is a sign of Imaan being fresh and superb. Don't you see that when an animal is just loaded, it carries the load quickly (because it is fresh) but when the journey is prolonged, it walks in a staggered motion?" (Therefore when Imaan is continually refreshed, it is capable of doing much.)
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.8 Pg.61).

paras: Hadhrat Hayya bint Abu Hayya reports, "it was midday when a man came to my house. 'What is it you want, O servant of Allaah?' I asked. He explained, 'My friend and I have been searching for our camel and while he is still out looking, I have come here to take some shade and to have something to drink.' I got up and gave him some yoghurt to drink. I then looked at him closely and asked, 'Who are you, 0 servant of Allaah?' when he told me that his name was Abu Bakr, I asked, 'The same Abu Bakr who was the companion of Rasulullaah ﷺ and about whom I heard so Yes,' he replied. 1 then started mentioning to him the battles that my tribe had fought with the Banu Khath'am and all the fights we (Arabs) had been having with each other during the Period of ignorance. I then spoke of the love that Allaah had created between us (because of Islaam) and asked, 'O servant of Allaah! Until when will this status quo (of mutual love) 'As long as the leaders are upright,' he replied. "Who are the leaders?' I enquired. He said, 'Do you not see that every tribe has a leader whom they follow and whom they obey? it shall last as long as these people remain upright."
sources: Musaddad, Ibn Munee and Daarmi, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.3 Pg.162).

paras: Hadhrat Haarith bin Mu'aawiya narrates that when he came to Hadhrat Umar Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked, "In what condition did you leave the people of Shaam?" After he had informed Hadhrat Umar (RA) about the condition of the people there, Hadhrat Umar (RA) praised Allaah and said, "Are you people perhaps socializing with the Mushrikeen?" when Hadhrat Haarith assured Hadhrat Umar (RA) that they were not, Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "When you start socialising with them, you will start eating and drinking with them and your situation will remain good only when you do not do that."
sources: Ya'qoob bin Sufyaan, Bayhaqi and Ibn Asaakir, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.2 Pg.300).

paras: Hadhrat Ayaadh narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once instructed Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari to present to him all his earnings and expenditure (as governor) on a single piece of leather. Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) had a Christian accounts keeper and when he presented it, Hadhrat Umar (RA) was impressed and said, "He has an excellent memory. Will you read out a letter that has come from Shaam in the Masjid?" "He will be unable to do so," Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari said. "Why not?" Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked, "Is he impure?" "No," Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) replied, "he is a Christian." Hadhrat Umar (RA) then reprimanded Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) and hit him on the thigh saying, "Dismiss him!" He then recited the verse: O you who have Imaan! Do not take the Jews and Christians as friends (confidantes). They are only the friends of each other (and cannot be your friends). Whoever of you befriends them, then he is surely from among them. Verily Allaah does not guide a nation of wrong-doers (who befriend the Kuffaar). (Surah Maa'idah, verse 51)
sources: Ibn Abi Haatim, as quoted in Tafseerof Ibn Katheer (Vol.2 Pg.68).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrates, "Rasulullaah ﷺ never found fault with food ever. If he liked it, he ate and if he did not, he would leave it (without comment)."
sources: Bukhaari and Muslim, as quoted in wan Nihaayah (Vol.6 Pg.40). (5) ibn Asaakir, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal Pg.37).

paras: Hadhrat All (RA) reports that the portion Rasulullaah ﷺ liked most of a goat was the foreleg.
Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ liked the foreleg of an animal. When the foreleg was once poisoned, everyone suspected that it was the Jews who poisoned it."

Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ came to visit them in their house, they slaughtered a goat in his honour. Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "It seems like they knew we like meat." There is a more detailed story attached to this incident. ® Hadhrat Anas (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ loved bottle gourd so when some food was served, I started searching for it (in the plate) and placing them in front of him because I knew that he loved it."
sources: Tirmidhi in his Shamaa'il (Pg.12).
Tirmidhi in his Shamaa'il.

paras: Hadhrat Anas giisig also narrates that whenever Rasulullaah ﷺ ate food, he licked his three fingers (with which he ate).
sources: A variety of gourd called "Doodi" in Urdu.

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ (was so humble that he) ate on the floor, tied the feet of goats when they were to be milked and even accepted the invitation of slaves to eat (plain) barley bread."
sources: Tirmidhi in his Shamaa'il.

paras: Hadhrat Yahyaa bin Abu Katheer reports that a plate of Thareed came to Rasulullaah ﷺ every day from Hadhrat Sa'd bin ubaadah (RA). It went with him to the house of whichever wife he was with.
sources: Tirmidhi in his Shamaa'il.

paras: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that when some goat's milk was milked for Rasulullaah ﷺ , he drank it and then gargled his mouth saying, "It has some stickiness (which needs to be rinsed out to preserve oral hygiene)."
sources: Ibn Najjaar, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vo!.4 Pg.44).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) reports that when Rasulullaah ﷺ once stopped over at a certain place, a woman sent her son with a goat to Rasulullaah ﷺ .

Rasulullaah ﷺ milked the goat and told the boy to take it to his mother. After she had drunk to her fill, the boy brought another goat. After milking it, Rasulullaah ﷺ gave the milk to Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA). When the boy then brought a third goat, Rasulullaah ﷺ milked it and only this time did he drink.
sources: Ibn Asaakir, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (vol.4 Pg.37).

paras: Hadhrat Ibraheem (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ used to keep his right hand free for acts such as eating, drinking and making wudhu. His left hand he would keep free for acts such as Istinfaa, cfeaning his nose and other such Hadhrat Ja'far bin Abdullaah bin Hakam bin Raafi says, "When Hakam once saw me eating from various parts of the plate, he said, 'Dear boyl Do not eat like that as Shaytaan eats. When Rasulullaah ﷺ ate, his fingers would not stray from his hands (they stayed in front of Mm)."
sources: Abu Nu'aym, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.8 Pg,46). The author of isaabah (Vbl.l Pg.344) has commented on the chain of narrators. .

paras: Hadhrat Umar bin Abu Salamah (RA) reports, "I was once eating with Rasulullaah ﷺ when I started taking meat from all over the plate. Rasulullaah said to me, 'Eat from that which is in front of you.m
sources: Ibn Najjaar, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.8 Pg.46).

paras: Hadhrat Ummayyah bin Makhshi (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once saw a man eating without first reciting Bismillaah, When there was only a single morsel left, he lifted it to his mouth and eating it, he) recited: Rasulullaah ﷺ then laughed and said, "By Shaytaan continued eating with you until you took Allaah's name. He then vomited out everything that was in his belly." Another narration states that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "...until when you took Allaah's name, he forcefully vomited out everything in his belly." Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) narrates that they were once with Rasulullaah ﷺ when a platter (of food) was brought and placed before them. When Rasulullaah held back his hand, the Sahabah (RA) did the same because they never ate until Rasulullaah ﷺ did. A Bedouin then came appearing as if he was being shoved along. As he was about to grab at the platter to eat from the food, Rasulullaah ﷺ caught hold of his hand. Just then, a little girl came also appearing as if she was being pushed along, when she also attempted to get her hand into the food, Rasulullaah ﷺ grabbed her hand as well. Rasulullaah ﷺ then said, "Verily people's food becomes lawful for Shaytaan when they do not take Allaah's name. When Shaytaan saw that we were holding our hands back, he brought the girl so that the food could become lawful for him (when she eats without saying Bismillaah). I however, grabbed her hand. He had also brought the Bedouin to make the food lawful for himself, but I had grabbed his hand as well. I swear by the Being besides Whom there is none worthy of worship! His hand is now in my hands; together with the hands of the two of them."
sources: Ahmad, Abu Dawood, Nasa'ee, Ibn Qaani, Tabraani, Haakim and others, as quoted in Kanzul ummaal (vol.8 Pg.45).

paras: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) that Rasulullaah ﷺ was eating with six others when a Bedouin came and ate all the food in two morsels. Rasulullaah remarked, "Had he recited Bismillaah, the food would have sufficed for them all. When any of you eats, he should take the name of Allaah and if he forgets, he should recite:

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Busr (RA) relates, "Nabi ﷺ once stopped over by my father, who served him a meal of Saweeq W and Hais. After Rasulullaah ﷺ had eaten, my father brought something to drink. After drinking, Rasulullaah passed the cup on to the person on his right. When eating dates, Rasulullaah ﷺ threw the stones like this." Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Busr (RA) then pointed with his fmger towards his back (to indicate that Rasulullaah ﷺ threw the stones behind him). Narrating further, he says that when Rasulullaah got on his mule, his father held the reins and said, "Do make du'aa for us, O Rasulullaah ﷺ Rasulullaah ﷺ then made the following du'aa: "O Maah! Bless them in the sustenance You give them, forgive them and have mercy on them."
sources: A type of porridge prepared from barley.

paras: In another narration, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Busr (RA) says, "When my father once asked my mother to prepare some food for Rasulullaah ﷺ, she prepared some Thareed. My father then proceeded to invite Rasulullaah ﷺ for the meal and (when he arrived) Rasulullaah ﷺ placed his hand on the top of the dish saying (to the Sahabah (RA)), 'Dish out taking the name of Maah.' They then dished" out from the sides. After everyone had eaten, Rasulullaah ﷺ made the following du'aa: "O Allaah! Forgive them, have mercy on them and bless them in the sustenance You give them."
sources: A sweet dish prepared with dates, butter and flour.

paras: Hadhrat ibn A'bad reports that Hadhrat (RA) once asked, "O Ibn A'bad! Do you know what is the right of food?" "What is the right of food?" Ibn A'bad asked. Hadhrat Ali (RA) replied, "That you recite: "Luljj Ci U 411! 'I begin with the name of Allaah. O Allaah! bless us in the sustenance You give us'" Thereafter, Hadhrat Ali (RA) asked, "And do you know how to express gratitude after you have finished?" "How do you express gratitude?" Ibn A'bad asked. Hadhrat Ali (RA) replied, "By saying: 'All praise is for Allaah Who has given us food and drink. ",
sources: Ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Nu'aym.
Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Abi Dunya in his Du'aa, Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya and Bayhaqi, as quoted in (Vol.8 Pg.46).

paras: Hadhrat Umar (RA) once said, "Beware of excessive and drinking because it harms the body, is the cause of many diseases and leads to lethargy in salaah. Rather be moderate in your eating and drinking because it is healthier for the body and further from extravagance. Allaah detests the obese scholar (whose makes eating a priority) and a person shall never be destroyed until he gives precedence to his desires over his Deen."
sources: Abu Nu'aym, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.8.

paras: Hadhrat Abu Mah'dhoora (RA) reports that he was once sitting with Hadhrat Umar when Hadhrat Safwaan bin Umayyah (RA) brought a platter (of food). Hadhrat Umar (RA) summoned some poor people and slaves in the vicinity and they all shared the food with him. Thereafter, Hadhrat Umar (RA) remarked, "May Allaah curse the people who are averse to their slaves eating with them." To this, Hadhrat Safwaan said, "We are not averse to them eating with us. We eat by ourselves only because we do not find sufficient good food to feed both us and them."
sources: Ibn Asaakir, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.5 Pg.48).

paras: Hadhrat Maalik bin Anas reports that when Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) stopped over in Juhfah, Ibn Aamir bin Kurayz instructed his baker to take food to Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA). When he brought one plate of food, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) told him to put it down. When the baker returned with another plate of food was going to take the first plate away, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) asked, "What are you doing?" "I am taking the plate away," the baker replied. "No," said Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar "just pour the food into this other food." Thereafter, every time a different dish was served, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) made the man pour it into the other food. When the baker eventually returned to Hadhrat Ibn Aamir, he remarked, "That man must be an uncultured Bedouin!" Hadhrat Ibn Aamir corrected the baker saying, "That man is your leader. He is Ibn Umar
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya Pg.301)

paras: Hadhrat ja'farnarratesthatbecauseHadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) always ate the seeds of the pomegranate, someone asked, "O Ibn Abbaasl Why do you do that?" He explained, '" have heard that every pomegranate on earth grows from a seed from amongst the seeds from Jannah. This seed is perhaps the

Hadhrat Saalim says, "I was with my master Zaid bin Sowhaan when Hadhrat Salmaan Faarsi passed by us after purchasing a wasaq of grain. 'O Abu Abdullaah!' Zaid called out, You are doing this (buying so much) when you are the companion of Rasulullaah ﷺ Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) replied, The soul is at ease when it has secured its sustenance. It can then free itself for Ibaadah and Waswaas /the devil that whispers evil into the heart) loses hope in Hadhrat Abu Uthmaan Nahdi narrates that Hadhrat Salmaan Faarsi (RA) said, "I love to eat from the efforts of my own hands."
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.207).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) once said, "I had fifteen dates so I broke my fast with five, ate Sehri with five and kept the other five to break my fast with."
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol. 1 Pg.200).

paras: Hadhrat Muslim who was the freed slave of Hadhrat Ali bin Abi Taalib (RA) says, "When Hadhrat Ali (RA) once asked for a drink, I brought him a cup of water and blew into it. He refused to drink it and returned it to me saying, "You drink it.w
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.384).

paras: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Abu Layla says that he was once with Hadhrat Umar when he said, "I saw Abu Qaasim (Rasulullaah) ﷺ wearing a narrow-sleeved cloak made in Shaam."
sources: Ibn Sa'd (Vol.6 Pg.237). (5) ibn Sa'd, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.4 Pg.37).

paras: Hadhrat Jundub bin Makeeth (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ wore his best clothing whenever he received a delegation and would instruct the senior Sahabah to do the same. On the day a delegation arrived from Kindah tribe, I saw Rasulullaah ﷺ wearing clothing made in Yemen and both Abu Bakr and Umar were wearing the same."
Hadhrat Salamah bin Akwa (RA) says that Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA)'s loincloth always reached halfway up his calves and he would say, "Such was the garment of my beloved (Nabi) ﷺ
sources: Ibn Sa'd (Vol.4 Pg.346).

paras: Hadhrat Ash'ath bin Sulaym reports from his aunt that her uncle said, "I was walking in Madinah one day when someone behind me said, 'Lift up your loincloth because it keeps it cleaner and makes it last longer.' When I turned around, I saw that it was Rasulullaah ﷺ. 'O Rasulullaah (sagr. I said, 'it is but a simple black and white striped shawl.' Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, 'Do you not have an example in me?' When I looked at him, I saw that Rasulullaah ﷺ's garment reached halfway up his calves."
The Describe the Attire of Rasulullaah ﷺ

Hadhrat Abu Burdah narrates that Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) once took out and showed them a patched shawl and a loincloth made of coarse cloth. She then said, "It was in these two garments that the soul of Rasulullaah ﷺ was taken away."
sources: Tirmidhi in his Shamaa'il (Pg.9).

paras: Hadhrat Urtimu salamah'ESSSSfc'says, "The garment Rasulullaah ﷺ loved most was his Qamees "
sources: Tirmidhi in his Shamaa'il (Pg.9).

paras: Hadhrat Asmaa bint Yazeed (RA) reports that the sleeve of Rasulullaah ﷺ 's Qamees reached his wrists.
Hadhrat jaabir (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah illjl was wearing a black turban when he entered Makkah the day he conquered it.
Hadhrat Amr bin Hurayth (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once delivered a sermon wearing a black turban.
Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) says that once (during his illness)
Rasulullaah ﷺ delivered a sermon while wearing an oily bandage.

Hadhrat Naafi reports from Hadhrat Abdullaah bin umar (RA) that when Rasulullaah ﷺ tied his turban, he would let the tails hang between his shoulders. Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) also tied his turban in the same manner and a narrator called Abdullaah says that he saw Hadhrat Qaasim bin Muhammad and Hadhrat Saalim also do the same.
sources: A long, loose tailored upper garment. •(4) Tirmidhi in his Shamaa'il (Pg.5).

paras: when Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) was once asked about Rasulullaah ﷺ's bedding, she replied, "it was made of leather and stuffed with the bark of a date palm."
sources: Tirmidhi in his Shamaa'il (Pg.9).

paras: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) relates, "A lady from the Ansaar once visited me and saw that Rasulullaah ﷺ's bedding comprised of cloak that was double-folded. She then left and later sent a bedding stuffed with wool. When Rasulullaah ﷺ came to me, he asked, What is this, O Aa'isha?' I then informed him about the lady from the Ansaar who had seen his bedding and then sent this. Rasulullaah ﷺ told me to return it Because I liked to have it in my room, I did not return it until Rasulullaah ﷺ repeated the instruction three times. He finally said, 'Return it, O Aa'isha. I swear by Allaah that if I willed, Allaah would have made mountains of gold and silver travel with me (wherever I went),"'
sources: Hadhrat Hasan bin Arafah, lbn Sa'd (Vol.1 Pg.465) has reported a similar narration.

paras: Hadhrat Muhammad narrates that he once asked Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA), "what was Rasulullaah ﷺ's bedding like in your home?" She replied, "it was made of leather and stuffed with the bark of a date palm." When he then posed the same question to Hadhrat Hafsah (RA), she replied, "Rasulullaah ﷺ used to sleep on a coarse sheet that we double-folded. One night I thought to myself that it would be more comfortable if I four-folded it (so I did that). The following morning, Rasulullaah ﷺ asked, "What did you spread down for me last 'It was the same bedding,' I explained, 'all that I did was to four-fold it so that it would be more comfortable for you.' Rasulullaah ﷺ said, 'Leave it as it was because its softness prevented me from performing salaah last night."'
sources: Tirmidhi in his Shamaa'il, as quoted in At Bidaayah wan Nihaayah (Vol.6 Pg.53). lbn Sa'd (Vol.1 Pg.465) has also reported the narration but from Hadhrat Aa'isha WSRS6.- (3) lbn Mubaarak, Tabraani, Haakim, Bayhaqi and others, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.8 Pg.55).

paras: Hadhrat Omar (RA) reports that he saw Rasulullaah ﷺ send for some new clothing. When it reached his collar-bone as he was putting it on, he recited: "All praise is for Allaah Who has given me clothing to conceal my private areas and with which I can look beautiful in this life." Rasulullaah ﷺ then said, "I swear by the Being who controls my life! When a Muslim wears new clothing, recites these words and then purely for Allaah's pleasure gives the old clothes that he is removing to a poor person, he will remain in the care, the security and the protection of Allaah as long as there remains even a single thread of the garment left (on the poor person). This applies whether he is alive or dead. This applies whether he is alive or dead."

Hadhrat All (RA) reports that he was sitting with Rasulullaah ﷺ near (the graveyard of) Baqee on a rainy day when a woman passed by on her donkey, carrying a heavy load. As she passed through a depression in the ground, she fell off the donkey. Rasulullaah ﷺ turned his face away (so as not to see her body as it became exposed because of the fall). When someone informed Rasulullaah that the lady was wearing trousers (because of which her body did not become exposed), Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "O Allaah! Forgive all the women of my Ummah who wear trousers." Addressing the Sahabah (RA), Rasulullaah ﷺ then said, "O people! Always wear trousers because it is amongst the most concealing of clothing. Ensure that you protect your women with it whenever they go out."
sources: Bazzaar, Uqayli, lbn Mi and others, reporting from various chains of narrators, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.8 Pg.55). lbn Jowzi has wrongly included this narration in his Mowdu'aat.

paras: Hadhrat Dihya bin Khalifah Kalbi (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once sent him as envoy to Heraclius (the Byzantine Emperor), upon his return, Rasulullaah gave Hadhrat Dihya (RA) a delicate white Egyptian cloth saying, "use a part of it to make a Qamees for you and give your wife the other portion to use as a scarf." As Hadhrat Dihya (RA) was leaving, Rasulullaah ﷺ called him back saying, "Tell her to wear something underneath (the scarf) so that it is not revealing."
sources: and Ibn Asaakir, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.8 Pg,6l).

paras: Hadhrat Usaamah bin Zaid (RA) relates, "Rasulullaah ﷺ gave me some of the thick but delicate white Egyptian cloth that he had given Dihya. I subsequently gave it to my wife to (make something out of it to) wear. Rasulullaah ﷺ later asked me, "what is the matter? why are you not wearing the white Egyptian cloth?' When I informed Rasulullaah ﷺ that I had given it to my wife to wear, he said, 'Tell her to wear something underneath because I fear that it would reveal the shape of her bones."
sources: Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Sa'd, Ahmad, Rooyaani, Baaroodi, Tabraafti, Bayhaqi and Sa'eed bin Mansoor, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol. 8 Pg.62).

paras: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) reports that when she once wore some clothing, she kept looking down at it as she walked about in the room, turning about as she did so. (Her father) Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) then entered and said to her, "Don't you know that Allaah is presently not looking at you (with affection),"
sources: Ibn Mubaarak and Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya.

paras: In another narration, Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) says, "I once wore a new upper garment of mine and was very taken aback by it as I looked at it. Hadhrat Abu Bakr said to me, "What are you looking at? Allaah is not looking at you (with affection).' 'Why not?' I asked. He replied, 'Don't you know that when self-adoration enters a servant because of worldly beauty, Allaah detests the person until the beauty is lost (and the self-adoration with it).' I then took off the garment and gave it away as Sadaqah. Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) then said, 'That shall perhaps atone for

Hadhrat Abdl Azeez bin Abu Jameelah Ansaari reports that the sleeves of Hadhrat Umar's Qamees never extended past his wrists. ® Hadhrat Badeel bin Maysara reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once went for the Jumu'ah salaah wearing a cloak made in Sumbulaan. Apologising to the people (for coming late), he said, "It was this cloak that delayed me." He pulled his sleeves forward and as he let go of them, they returned to the ends of his Hadhrat Hishaam bin Khaalid reports that he saw Hadhrat Umar (RA) tie his loincloth above his navel.

Hadhrat Aamir bin Ubaydah Baahili narrates that when he once asked Hadhrat Anas about Khazz (a material in which there is a small element of silk), Hadhrat Anas (RA) replied, "I wish that Allaah had never created it. Apart from Umar and his son, all the Sahabah (RA) wore it." (Hadhrat Anas (RA) disliked it because it was a fabric worn by affluent non-Muslims)
sources: Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.4 Pg.4 1 9) .

paras: Hadhrat Masrooq narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once came out to them wearing cotton clothing. When the people stared at him, he recited a couplet (which meant): "The beauty of everything you see will never last Allaah will last when all wealth and children will be destroyed"
He then remarked, "By Allaah! compared to the Aakhirah, this world is just a leap of a

Hadhrat Abu Abdullaah who was the freed slave of Hadhrat Shaddaad bin Haad says, "It was on a Friday that I once saw Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Affaan (RA) standing on the pulpit wearing a shawl made in Kufa and a coarse loincloth made in Aden that was worth a mere four or five Dirhams. He was a thin, handsome man with a long beard.''
sources: Hannaad and lbn Abi Dunya, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal '(Vol .4 Pg.405),

paras: Hadhrat Moosa bin Talha says, "Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) used to lean on a staff (as he came to the Masjid) on Fridays. He was one of the most handsome men wearing his cream-coloured loincloth and shawl as he came to the pulpit and sat on it."
sources: Haakim (Vol.3 Pg.96). Tabraani has reported a similar narration from reliable sources, as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.9 Pg.80).

paras: Hadhrat SulaymAbuAamirsays,"lsaw Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Affaan (RA) wearing a Yemeni shawl worth a hundred Dirhams."
sources: Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.9 Pg.80) has commented on the chain o' narrators. (6) lbn Sa'd (Vol.3 Pg.58).

paras: Hadhrat Muhammad bin Rabee'ah bin Haarith says, "The Sahabah (RA) used to spend generously on such clothing for their wives that was both beautiful as well as concealing. I once saw Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) wearing a shawl edged with silk that was worth two hundred Dirhams. He said, This belongs to (my wife) Naa'ilah. I had given it to her to wear and am wearing it now only to make her happy."
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol. l Pg.82).

paras: Hadhrat Zaid bin Wahab narrates that a delegation from Basrah once came to see Hadhrat Ali (RA).
