As for the one who follows the Qur'aan, the Qur'aan shall lead him tojannatul Firdous. So as far as you can, let it be an intercessor for you and never let it be a complainant against you. The person for whom the Qur'aan intercedes shall enter Jannah and the one against whom the Qur'aan complains shall surely enter Jahannam. Always bear in mind that the Qur'aan is a fountainhead of guidance, a flower of knowledge and the final scripture from the Most Merciful. It is by this Qur'aan that Allaah opens blind eyes, deaf ears and locked hearts.

You must also bear in mind that when a man wakes up at night, brushes his teeth with a Miswaak, performs wudhu, says 'Allaahu Akbar' and then recites the Qur'aan, an angel places his mouth on the person's mouth and says, 'Recite, recite. You are doing an excellent thing and it is most excellent for you. ' If he performs wudhu without using the Miswaak, the angel protects him and does nothing else. Behold! Recitation of the Qur'aan in salaah is a protected treasure and an ordained excellence. You should therefore do as much of it as you possibly can. Salaah is a celestial light, zakaah is a symbol, patience is an illumination, fasting is a shield and the Qur'aan is a- proof either for you or against you. You should therefore honour the Qur'aan and never cause it disgrace because Allaah will honour the one who honours the Qur'aan and will disgrace the one who brings it disgrace. You also ought to know that the person who recites the Qur'aan, memorises it, practises on it and abides by its injunctions shall have his du'aas accepted by Allaah. If Allaah pleases, He may accept them in this world and if He wills, he may reserve them as a treasure for the Aakhirah. Remember that what remains with Allaah is better and more lasting for those who have Imaan and who rely on their Rabb. "''*

Hadhrat Abu Kinaanah reports that when Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) gathered together the Huffaadh (of the army he commanded), they numbered close t. three hundred. Hadhrat Abu Moosa (RA) lectured to them about the greatness of the Qur'aan saying, "Verily this Qur'aan shall be either a source of reward for you or a burden (in the Aakhirah). You should therefore follow the dictates of the Qur'aan and never force it to follows yours because the one who follows the Qur'aan shall be with it in the gardens of Jannah while the one who forces the Qur'aan to follow his desires shall have it shoved on his neck and it will fling him into Jahannam."

Hadhrat Abul Aswad Daly reports that Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) once gathered all the Qurraa, emphasising that none but the Huffaadh should come to him. It was approximately three hundred men who came to him. He then addressed them saying, "You men are the Qurraa of the city and should therefore never allow the passage of time to harden your hearts as it happened to the Ahlul Kitaab. A Surah had been revealed that we thought resembled Surah Baraa'ah in length and in the stern subject matter it contained. A verse from it which 1 had memorised stated that if man had two valleys of gold he would seek to have a third and it would only be the sand (of his grave) that would be able to fill his belly. Thereafter, another Surah was revealed which we thought resembled the Musabbihaat because it begins with the (Sabbaha Lillaah). The verse from it that 1 had memorised is: (Tc-il) tji O you who have Imaan! Why do you say that which you did not do?
(Surah Saff, verse 2) Testimony will therefore be taken for everything you do and you will be questioned about it on the Day of Qiyaamah." '''
sources: Ibn Zanjway, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol. 1 Pg.217).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) once addressed the people of Kufa. After greeting them with Salaam and instructing them to observe Taqwa, he said, "Never dispute about the Qur'aan and never oppose each other concerning it because there are no discrepancies in the Qur'aan, it will never be (completely) forgotten and constant repetition of the Qur'aan will never tire one. Do you not see that the restrictions, the Faraa'idh and Allaah's explicit commands in the Shari'ah of Islaam are one? It would be said that the Qur'aan has discrepancies if a part of it commands an act which another part forbids. Every part of the Qur'aan rather complements the rest of it. I am convinced that such deep understanding and knowledge shall surface amongst you people that surpasses all other people. If a camel could take me to a person who has more knowledge of what has been revealed to Muhammad ﷺ than I have, I shall certainly go to him to increase the knowledge I have. I know well that while the entire Qur'aah would be recited to Rasulullaah ﷺ once every year, it was recited to Rasulullaah ﷺ twice during the year that he passed away (every Ramadhaan Hadhrat Jibra'eel (RA) would recite the Qur'aan to Rasulullaah ﷺ and Rasulullaah ﷺ would recite to him). Whenever I recited Qur'aan to Rasulullaah ﷺ, he would approve of my recitation, therefore whoever recites Qur'aan in the manner that I recite, should not turn away and forsake it. In a like manner, whoever recites the Qur'aan in another authentic manner should also not turn away and forsake it because whoever rejects any one of the various manners of recitation will reject them all."

A student of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) from Hamdaan narrates that before Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) left for Madinah, he gathered all his students together and said, "By Allaah! I am convinced that such religiousness, deep understanding of Deen and knowledge of the Qur'aan shall surface amongst you people that surpasses that of all other Muslims..." The narration continues until it states that he said, "Verily there are no discrepancies in the Qur'aan, neither does the Qur'aan ever age or lose its dignity by Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) also said, "It is only befitting that a man of the Qur'aan be recognised by his nights (when he is engaged in Ibaadah) when others are asleep, by his days (spent fasting) when others are eating, by his sorrow (pondering about his plight in the Aakhirah) when others are rejoicing, by his weeping when others are laughing, by his silence when others are socialising and by his humility when others are behaving arrogantly. It is also befitting of a man of the Qur'aan to be weeping and sorrowful, wise and tolerant, knowledgeable and composed. It does not behove a man of the Qur'aan to be uncouth, negligent, boisterous, rowdy and short-tempered." Another narration states that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "Do your best to be a listener (rather than always speaking) and take careful note when you hear Allaah say, 'O you who have Imaanf because it is only something good that you are being instructed to do or something evil that you are being prohibited from."

Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ was busy narrating Ahadeeth when a Bedouin arrived and asked, "When will Qiyaamah take place?" When Rasulullaah ﷺ continued narrating, some of the Sahabah isB!2ffi!sgi said that Rasulullaah ﷺ (was not giving a reply because he) heard the man but did not like the question. Others said that Rasulullaah ﷺ did not hear the man at all. When Rasulullaah ﷺ had completed narrating Ahadeeth, he asked, "Where is he (the Bedouin)?" "Here am I over here!" the man said. Rasulullaah (Self then said, "Wait for Qiyaamah when a time arrives in which trusts are misappropriated." "How will they be misappropriated?" the man asked. Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, "Wait for Qiyaamah when authority is placed in the hands of unworthy people."
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Pg.130).

paras: Standing before the people in the largest Masjid of Riqqa during the days of Eidul Fitr and Eidul Adhaa, Hadhrat Waabisah (RA) used to say, "I was present with Rasulullaah ﷺ during the Farewell Hajj when he addressed the people saying, 'O people! Which month is most sacred?' 'This month (of Dhul Hijjah) is,' the people replied. Rasulullaah ﷺ asked further, 'O people! Which city is most sacred?' 'This city (of Makkah) is,' the people replied. Rasulullaah ﷺ then declared, 'Until the day you meet your Rabb, your blood, your wealth and your honour are as sacred to you as this day, this month and this city are. Have i conveyed the message?' 'You certainly have,' the people replied. Rasulullaah ﷺ then raised his hands to the sky saying, 'You be the witness, O Allaah.' Thereafter, he said, 'Those of you present here should pass the message on to those who are absent.' Do come closer so that I may convey to you what Rasulullaah ﷺ said to us."
sources: Bazzaar, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.1 Pg.139).

paras: Hadhrat Makhool says, "Ibn Abu Zakariyyah, Sulaymaan bin Habeeb and 1 once went to Hadhrat Abu Umaamah (RA) in Hims. After we had greeted him with the words of Salaam, he said, 'This sitting of yours here is a means Allaah has used for the Deen to reach you and will also be Allaah's evidence against you (if you do not propagate it). Rasulullaah ﷺ propagated, so you too should propagate."

In another narration, Hadhrat Saleem bin Aamir says, "When we would sit with Hadhrat Abu Ubaadah (RA) and he narrated to us many Ahadeeth of Rasulullaah ﷺ, he would say to us after he had completed, 'Have you understood? Now propagate as it has been propagated to you.'"
sources: Tabraani in his Kabeer, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.1 Pg.140).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once prayed, "O Allaah! Shower Your mercy on my successors." "O Rasulullaah (illli?!" the Sahabah (RA) asked, "Who are your successors?" Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, "Those who will come after me, who will narrate my Ahadeeth and teach them to the people."

Hadhrat Aasim bin Muhammad narrates from his father that he saw Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah come to the Masjid of Rasulullaah ﷺ on the day of Jumu'ah. Standing and holding the two knobs of the pulpit, he said, "Abul Qaasim Rasulullaah ﷺ the truthful and veritable narrated to us..." He then continued to narrate Ahadeeth until he heard the door of the Imaam's room open as the Imaam emerged to lead the salaah. He then sat down.
sources: Haakim, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Dhahabi.

paras: Hadhrat Aslam reports that when they used to ask Hadhrat Umar (RA) to narrate Ahadeeth to them, he would say, "I fear that I may add a word or omit a word because Rasulullaah ﷺ said, The person who intentionally lies about me is headed for Jahannam."

Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Haatib says, "I have not seen any of the Sahabah narrate Ahadeeth as well and as thoroughly as Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA). However, he was a man who was extremely reluctant to narrate Ahadeeth."
sources: Ahmad, Ibn Adi, Uqayli and Abu Nu'aym in his Ma'rifah, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol. 5 Pg.239).

paras: Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) used to say, "What prevents me from narrating Ahadeeth from Rasulullaah ﷺ is not the fact that I was not one of those Sahabah (RA) with the best memories. What prevents me is that 1 can testify that I heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say, 'Whoever attributes anything to me that I never stated should prepare for his abode in Jahannam.'" Another narration quotes Rasulullaah ﷺ's words as, "Whoever speaks lies about me should prepare for a house in Jahannam."
sources: Ibn Sa'd and Ibn Asaakir, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.5 Pg.9).

paras: Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "When narrating Ahadeeth to you, I prefer falling from the sky rather than stating something that Rasulullaah Wife never said. However, when speaking to you about matters between us, then (precautions need not be so strict because) wars are won by strategy."

Hadhrat Amr bin Maymoon reports that sometimes an entire year would pass by without Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) narrating a single Hadith. When he narrated a Hadith one day, he started to shiver and perspiration beaded up on his forehead. He then said, "Rasulullaah ﷺ said something like that or stated similar words."

Hadhrat Masrooq reports, "Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) started to narrate a Hadith one day, but as soon as he said, 'Rasulullaah ﷺ said,' he started to shiver so much that even his clothing shook. He then added, 'Rasulullaah ﷺ said something to the effect or something similar.'"
sources: Ahmad, Abu Ya'la and Bazzaar. Haythami (Vol. 1 Pg.1 43) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Abu Idrees Khowlaani says, "I noticed that whenever Hadhrat Abu Dardaa completed narrating Ahadeeth, he would add, 'Rasulullaah ﷺ said that, something similar to that or something resembling Hadhrat Muhammad bin Seereen narrates that whenever Hadhrat Anas bin Maalik narrated Ahadeeth from Rasulullaah ﷺ, he would end with the words, "It was something like this that Rasulullaah ﷺ said."
sources: Tabraani, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol. I Pg.141). Abu Ya'la, Rooyaani and Ibn Asaakir have reported a similar narration, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal ' (Vol.3 Pg.156).

paras: In another narration, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Hadhrat Anas bin Maalik (RA) narrated few Ahadeeth from Rasulullaah ﷺ, but when he did, he would end with the words, "It was something like this that Rasulullaah ﷺ said." Hadhrat Abu Ja'far Muhammad bin Ali says, "There was no companion of Rasulullaah ﷺ more cautious of adding anything to or omitting anything from the Ahadeeth of Rasulullaah ﷺ than Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA)
sources: Ibn Abdul Birr in his Jaami (Vol. 1 Pg. 79).

paras: Hadhrat Sha'bi says, "I sat in the company of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) for an entire year without hearing him narrate anything from Rasulullaah

Hadhrat Imraan bin Husayn (RA) said, "I have heard many Ahadeeth from Rasulullaah ﷺ which I have memorised. All that prevents me from narrating them is that some of my companions may differ with me in the narration."
sources: Ahmad, Abu Ya'la and Haakim, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.5 Pg.240). (4)lbnSa'd(Vol.4Pg.l44). (S)lbnSa'd(Vol.4Pg,145).

paras: Hadhrat Mutarraf reports that Hadhrat Imraan bin Husayn (RA) said to him, "O Mutarraf! By Allaah! I am certain that if I chose to do so, I could narrate Ahadeeth from Rasulullaah ﷺ for two days continuously without repeating a single Hadith. However, what makes me reluctant to do so and makes me disapprove of doing such a thing is that although I was there when many Sahabah (RA) of Muhammad ﷺ were there and I also heard what they heard, they confuse the sequence of the words when they narrate." Sometimes, Hadhrat Imraan bin Husayn would say, "If I were to narrate to you what Rasulullaah ﷺ said, I am certain that I will be accurate." When he quoted the words of Rasulullaah ﷺ, Hadhrat Imraan bin Husayn (RA) would do so with great certainty and say, "I heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say..."
sources: Tabraani in his Kabeer, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol. 1 Pg. 1 4 1 ).

paras: Hadhrat Sulaymaan bin Abu Abdullaah reports that he heard Hadhrat Suhayb say, "By Allaah! I shall never intentionally narrate Ahadeeth to you saying that it is what Rasulullaah ﷺ said. However, I shall gladly relate to you what I experienced in the expeditions I participated in with Rasulullaah ﷺ. Then again, I shall never say, 'Rasulullaah ﷺ said'."
sources: Ibn Sa'd (Vol.3 Pg.229), as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal Pg.203).

paras: Hadhrat Makhool relates, "Abul Azhar and I once went to Hadhrat Waathila bin Asqa and said, 'O Abu Asqa! Narrate to us a Hadith that you heard from Rasulullaah ﷺ without any uncertain words, and without any additions or omissions.' Hadhrat Waathila (RA) asked, 'Has any of you recited any part of the Qur'aan last night?' 'Yes,' we replied, 'But since we are not Huffaadh, we tend to add a Waawd) or an To this, Hadhrat Waathila (RA) remarked, 'And that is the Qur'aan which you have still not mastered when it has been in your midst for such a long time. When you feel that you are adding or omitting letters to it, what about the Ahadeeth that we had perhaps heard only once from Rasulullaah ﷺ It is sufficient for you that we narrate only their intended meanings to you."
sources: Ibn Abdul Birr in his Jaami (Vol.1 Pg.?9).

paras: Hadhrat Ibraheem bin Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf relates, "By Allaah! Before he passed away, Hadhrat Umar (RA) sent messengers to various distant places to summon Sahabah (RA) such as Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Hudhaafa (RA), Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA), Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) and Hadhrat Uqba bin Aamir. When they had gathered, he said to them, 'What Ahadeeth have you people spread to even the far distant lands?' 'Are you forbidding us from narrating them?' they asked. 'No,' Hadhrat Umar (RA) replied, 'I just want you to remain with me. By Allaah! I do not want you to part from me (here in Madinah) for as long as I live because we know best which of your narrations we shall accept and which ones we will not.' They therefore did not part from Hadhrat Umar (RA) until he passed away."

Hadhrat Ibraheem bin Abdur Rahmaan relates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) sent for Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA), Hadhrat Abu Mas'ood Ansaari and Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) and said to them, "What are the Ahadeeth that you are so frequently narrating to the people?" He then confined them to Madinah until he was martyred.
sources: Ibn Asaakir, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.5 Pg.239).

paras: Hadhrat Ibn Abu Awfa (RA) reports that when they used to request Hadhrat Zaid bin Arqam to narrate the Ahadeeth of Rasulullaah ﷺ to them, he would say, "We have aged and have begun to forget. Narrating the Ahadeeth of Rasulullaah ﷺ is a very serious matter (which cannot be taken lightly)."
sources: Ibn Asaakir, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.5 Pg.239).

paras: Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA) and Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) both said, "Learn as much as you wish to learn but Allaah will place no benefit in your knowledge until you practise what you know."
Hadhrat Anas (RA) said, "Learn as much as you please, but I swear by Allaah that you will not be rewarded for your knowledge until you put it into practise."
sources: Ibn Adi and Khateeb.

paras: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Ghanam says, "Ten Sahabah (RA) of Rasulullaah informed me that they were learning in the Masjid of Quba when Rasulullaah ﷺ came to them and said, 'Learn...'" The remainder of the words are like the narration above.
sources: Ibn Asaakir.

paras: Hadhrat Ali (RA) reports that a man came to Rasulullaah ﷺ and said, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ What will satisfy the evidence that ignorance will hold against me?" "Knowledge," Rasulullaah ﷺ replied. "And what will satisfy the evidence that knowledge will hold against me?" he asked further. Rasulullaah Seal's reply was, "Action."
sources: Abul Hasan bin Akhram in his Amaali, as quoted in Jaami'us Sagheer.

paras: Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "Study the Book of Allaah and you will be known for it. Practise on its teachings and you will be amongst its worthy bearers."
Pg.153) has reported a similar narration which states the name of Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) in place of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA).

Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "Study and you will be known for it. Practise on your knowledge and you will be amongst its worthy bearers because soon a time will come when nine-tenths of the truth will be rejected and the only person who will be saved will be one who remains anonymous and aloof from people. Such people are the beacons of guidance and the lanterns of knowledge. They are not hasty, do not promote immoral behaviour or immoral speech."
sources: Ahmad in his Zuhd, Abu Ubayd, Deenowri in his Ghareeb and Ibn Asaakir, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.5 Pg. 229).

paras: Hadhrat Ali (RA) once said, "O men of knowledge! Practise on your knowledge because only that person is an Aalim whose knowledge is followed by practise and whose practise conforms with his knowledge. There shall soon come people whose knowledge will not even transcend their collar-bones. Their private lives will contradict their public lives just as their actions will contradict their knowledge. They will sit in groups, boasting to each other and will get angry if anyone sitting in their group had to leave to sit with another group, The actions of such people will not even transcend their gatherings on its way to reach Allaah."
sources: Ibn Abdul Birr in his Jaami (Vol.2 Pg.7), as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.5 Pg.233).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "O people! Study, but whoever studies should practise what he learns."

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Ukaym says, "It was in this very Masjid that I heard Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) begin his speech with an oath as he said, 'Your Rabb shall be Alone with every one of you just as you see the fourteenth moon all by itself. Allaah will say, 'O son of Aadam! What deceived you about Me? O son of Aadam! How did you respond to the Ambiyaa? O son of Aadam! Did you practise on your knowledge?'"

Hadhrat Adi bin Adi narrates that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) repeated the following words: "Destruction be to the person who does not acquire knowledge. Still, if Allaah wills, Allaah shall educate him. However, seven times destruction be to the person who has the knowledge but does not practise." Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "Everyone has fantastic words to say but only those will be successful whose deeds are consistent with their words. The one whose deeds contradict his words shall have only himself to blame." It was also Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) who said, "People are in need of anyone who is engrossed in Allaah. People are also in need of that person's knowledge who practises on his knowledge."
sources: Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.1 Pg.164) has commented on the chain of narrators. Abu Nu'aym has also reported the narration in his Pg.131) from Hadhrat Alqama.

paras: Hadhrat Luqmaan bin Aamir narrates that Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) used to say, "What I fear most about Allaah on the Day of Qiyaamah is that he would call me in front of all creation saying, 'O Uwaymir!' Then when I respond by saying, '1 am at Your service, O my Rabb!', Allaah shall ask, 'Did you practise on your Another narration quoted Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) as sayjng, "What I fear most is that 1 should be asked on the Day of Qiyaamah, 'O Uwaymir! Did you acquire knowledge or remain ignorant?' If I reply that I had acquired knowledge, every verse containing a command and every verse containing an admonition shall claim their rights. The verses containing commands will ask, 'Did you carry out (what was commanded)?' and every verse containing an admonition will ask, 'Did you take heed (to the admonition)?' I seek Allaah's protection from knowledge that does not benefit, from desires that are not sated and from du'aas that are not answered."

Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) said, "None can possess Taqwa until he has knowledge and one can attain beauty through knowledge only if one practises on Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) also said, "The worst of people in Allaah's sight on the Day of Qiyaamah shall be that person with knowledge whose knowledge does not benefit him (which he does not practise on)."

Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA) said, "No person will be able to move his feet on the Day of Qiyaamah until he is questioned about four things; (1) about how he used his body, about how he spent his life, about how he earned and spent his wealth and about how he practised on his knowledge."
sources: Ibn Abdul Birr in his jaami (Vol.2 Pg.10), as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal '(Vol. 5 Pg.243).
Bayhaqi, as quoted in Targheeb wat Pg.90). Abu Nu'aym has also reported a similar narration in his Hilya Pg.214).
Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.214).

Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.213). Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.21 1) has also reported from Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) a narration similar to the one Hadhrat Adi reported from Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA).

paras: Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA) also said, "Learn as much as you want but Allaah shall not reward you for it until you practise on your knowledge."

Hadhrat Anas (RA) said, "Learn as much as you want to learn but Allaah shall not reward you for it until you practise on your knowledge. While the objective of true Ulema (when acquiring knowledge) is to remember (and practise), the objective of foolish people (when acquiring knowledge) is to relate it to others (without practising)." '''

Hadhrat Ubay bin Ka'b (RA) said, "Hold fast to the straight path and the Sunnah because Allaah shall never punish a person who is steadfast on the straight path and the Sunnah and whose tears then flow from his eyes out of fear for Allaah when he thinks of Allaah. When a person who is steadfast on the straight path and the Sunnah thinks of Allaah and his hairs stand on end out of fear for Allaah, is just like a tree with dry leaves. Just as its leaves fall off when a strong wind blows, all his sins fall off him in the same manner. Moderation when doing something for the pleasure of Allaah and according to the Sunnah is better than exerting oneself in something that is not for the pleasure of Allaah and against the Sunnah. You should therefore check well that your deeds conform with the pattern of the Ambiyaa and their Sunnah, regardless of whether the deeds be an exerted effort or something done in moderation."
sources: Ibn Abdul Birr in his Jaami (Vol. 2 Pg.6).

paras: Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Musayyib narrates that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) arrived back in Madinah, he addressed the people saying, "O peoplel The Sunan have been demonstrated to you and the Faraa'idh have been ordained for you. You have therefore been left on a clear and distinct path, (which you will be able to follow with ease) unless people lead you to the right and to the left (lead you astray). " When lecturing the people every Thursday, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood would say, "There are only two matters of importance. One is a way of life and the other is speech. While the best and truest of speech is that of Allaah, the best way of life is that of Muhammad ﷺ. Everything newly introduced (into the Deen) is a Bid'ah and every Bid'ah is a means of leading people astray. Behold! Prolonged periods (of stagnation) should never pass over you, causing your hearts to harden and distant hopes should never make you negligent (of the Aakhirah) because everything still pending is nearby and something far off is that which is never to come."
sources: Laalkaa'ee, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.1 Pg.97). Abu Nu'aym has reported a similar narration in his ///Tea (Vol.1 Pg.253).
Ibn Abdul Birr in hisjaami (Vol. 2 Pg.181).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "Moderation in the Sunnah is better than exerting oneself in Bid'ah."
sources: Haakim (Vol.1 Pg.103), reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Dhahabi. Abu Nu'aym has reported a similar narration in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.173).

paras: Hadhrat Imraan bin Husayn (RA) said, "The Qur'aan was revealed and Rasulullaah ﷺ demonstrated his way of life (which we emulated). You people must follow us because if you do not, you shall go astray."
sources: Ahmad. Haythami (Vol.1 Pg. 191) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Imraan bin Husayn (RA) once said to someone (who insisted on following only the Qur'aan), "You are a fool! Do you find any verse of the Qur'aan telling you that there are four Rakaahs in Zuhr and that the Qiraa'ah should be silent?" He then proceeded to enumerate the other salaahs, zakaah and other injunctions of Deen, saying, "Are the details of these found in the Qur'aan. While the Book of Allaah only briefly mentions these things, the Sunnah explains the details."
sources: Ibn Abdul Birr in his Jaami (Vol.2 Pg. 191).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "Whoever wishes to follow anyone, should follow the companions of Muhammad ﷺ because from amongst the entire Ummah, their hearts are most righteous, their knowledge is deepest, they are the least pretentious, they are most unswerving in example and their (religious) condition is best. Allaah had selected them to be the companions of His Nabi ﷺ and to establish His Deen. You should therefore acknowledge their worth and follow in their footsteps because they had been fixed on upright guidance."
sources: Ibn Abdul Birr in his Jaami (Vol.2 Pg.97). Abu Nu'aym has reported a similar narration from Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.305), as has been quoted in the chapter describing the qualities of the Sahabah (RA).

paras: Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) used to say, "O assembly of Qurraa! Fear Allaah and follow the path of those before you. I swear by my life that if you follow them, you will go very far ahead and if you forsake their path to go this way and that, you will have gone far astray." '''

Hadhrat Mus'ab bin Sa'd reports that whenever his father (Hadhrat Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas led the salaah (in congregation), he would make it brief together with performing the Ruku and Sajdah properly. However, when performing salaah at home (by himself), he would prolong the Ruku, the Sajdah and the salaah. He would then say, "Dear son! We (the Sahabah (RA)) are the leaders to be followed."
sources: Ibn Abdul Birr in his Jaami (Vol.2 Pg.97). Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Asaakir have reported a similar narration, as quoted in Kanzul Pg.233).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "Follow and do not introduce" and his Statement about Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) and Hadhrat Umar (RA) Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) once said, "Follow and do not introduce (new ways) because everything has been done for you (Rasulullaah ﷺ and the Sahabah (RA) have already blazed the trail)."
sources: Tabraani, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.1 Pg.182). (3), reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.1 Pg.181).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) also said, "An integral part of the Sunnah is to love Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) and Hadhrat Umar (RA) and to acknowledge their worth."

Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "Be careful not to emulate people because while a man can be doing the deeds of the people of Jannah, he can change according to the knowledge of Allaah and then start doing the actions of the people of Jahannam. When he then dies, he becomes an inmate of Jahannam. It may also happen that while a man can be doing the actions of the people of Jahannam, he can change according to the knowledge of Allaah and then start doing the deeds of the people of Jannah. When he then dies, he becomes a worthy dweller of Jannah. However, if it is absolutely necessary for you to follow someone, let it be those who have died (as practising Mu'mineen) and not those who are alive."

Hadhrat Abul Bakhtari says that someone once informed Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood about a group of people who sat in the Masjid after Maghrib when one of them would tell the others to recite "Allaahu Akbar" in a particular manner, to recite "Subhaanallaah" in a particular manner and to recite "Al Hamdu Lillaah" in a particular manner. "Do they then do as he says?" Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood asked. When the person confirmed that they did,, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood told him, "Inform me when you see them gathering again."

(When the person informed him afterwards,) Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood then came to this group, wearing his high hat, and sat with them. When he heard what they were saying, he, being the stern man that he was, stood up and said, "I am Abdullaah bin Mas'ood. By Allaah, besides Whom there is none worthy of worship! Verily you people have certainly perpetrated a terrible wrong by carrying out this act of Bid'ah! Have you then superseded the companions of Muhammad ﷺ in knowledge?"

A person npmed Ma'dad said, "By Allaah! We never intended to perpetrate a wrong with this new act, nor have we superseded the companions of Muhammad in knowledge." Amr bin Utba said, "O Abu Abdur Rahmaan! We seek forgiveness from Allaah."

Thereupon Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) told them, "It is compulsory for you to follow the path (of Rasulullaah ﷺ and the Sahabah (RA)) and to strictly adhere to it. By Allaah! If you will do so, you will have advanced far ahead and if you start swerving to the left and right, you will stray far off." '''

Another narration states: "The news reached Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood that a group of people were sitting in the Masjid between Maghrib and Isha..." The rest of the narration is like the one above. The only difference is in the following words: "Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said to them, "You people have certainly perpetrated a terrible wrong by carrying out this act of Bid'ah, otherwise we the companions of Muhammad ﷺ must have strayed." Amr bin Utba bin Farqad said, bin Mas'ood We seek forgiveness from Allaah and we repent to Him." Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) then ordered them to disperse.
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol. 4 Pg.381). Abu Nu'aym has reported a similar narration from Abu Za'raa, stating that it was Musayyib bin Nujbah that reported the gathering to Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA).

paras: Another narration states that when Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) saw two groups in the Masjid of Kufa, he stood between the two and asked, "Which of you two was before the other?" When the one group said that they were first, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) ordered the other group to join them, thereby combining the two into one.

An authentic abridged narration states that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood approached them covering his face and said, "Whoever recognises me will have recognised me. As for those who do not recognise me, I am Abdullaah bin Mas'ood. Are you people more rightly guided than the companions of Muhammad ﷺ The narrator says that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) also may have added, "You people are definitely clinging to the tail of deviation." Hadhrat Amr Ibn Salamah says that they were sitting at the door of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood's home between Maghrib and Isha when Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari came to the house and said to Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood, "Come with me, O Abu Abdur Rahmaan." When Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood came out from the house, he asked, "O Abu Moosa! What brings you here at this hour?" Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) replied, "By Allaah! The only thing that brings me here is something that I have seen which frightens me, yet it seems so good. There is a group sitting in the Masjid with a person instructing them to recite 'Subhaanallah' in a particular manner and to recite 'Al Hamdu Lillah' in a particular manner." Hadhrat Amr bin Salamah says that they accompanied Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood to the Masjid. When he arrived there, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood told the people, "You have wandered astray so fast! Even while the companions of Muhammad ﷺ are still alive in your midst, when his wives are still young and when his clothing and utensils are still as they were! Count your evil deeds, for I stand surety for Allaah that your good deeds will be counted."
sources: Tabraani.
Tabraani in his Kabeer. Haythami (Vol.1 Pg. 18!) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: that he once came to his father, who asked him, "Where have you been?" The son replied, "I found a group of people better than whom I have not seen. When they engage in Dhikr, one of them trembles and grows ecstatic until he falls unconscious out of fear for Allaah. (I am late because) 1 was sitting with them." Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr (RA) instructed his son saying, "Never sit with them again!" When he detected that this did not make an impression on his son, he added, "I have seen Rasulullaah ﷺ recite the Qur'aan, and I have seen Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) and Hadhrat Umar (RA) also reciting the Qur'aan. Nothing like this ever happened to them. Do you think that these people fear Allaah more than Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) and Hadhrat Umar (RA) The son, Hadhrat Aamir (RA) says, "I then realised that what he said was true, after which I forsook these people."
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol. 3 Pg.167).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Saalih Sa'eed bin Abdur Rahmaan narrates that Anz Nujaybi was once standing and relating stories in the Masjid when a Sahabi by the name of Hadhrat Sila bin Haarith Ghifaari (RA) said to him, "By Allaah! We have scarcely left Rasulullaah (ssss's time and have not even severed ties with our kin, yet you and your kind have already stood up in our midst (to perpetrate such acts of Bid'ah)."
sources: Tabraani in his Kabeer, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.1 Pg.189). Bukhaari, Baghawi, Muhammad bin Rabee and Ibn Sakan have reported a similar narration, as quoted in Isaabah (Vol.2 Pg.193).

paras: Hadhrat Amr bin Zuraarah says, "I was relating stories in the Masjid when Hadhrat Abdullaah (bin Mas'ood) (RA) stood up and said, 'O Amr! You have started a misleading Bid'ah! Are you more rightly guided than the companions of Muhammad ﷺ I then saw everyone dispersing from around me until I was left all alone."
sources: Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.1 Pg.189) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Ibn Shihaab reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) was standing on the pulpit and addressed the people saying, "O people! Accurate opinions came only from Rasulullaah ﷺ because Allaah used to guide him. What comes from us are but assumptions and pretences." Another narration states that Hadhrat Umar then added: ...and assumptions are absolutely useless against the truth." (Surah Najm, verse 28)' ' Hadhrat Sadaqah bin Abu Abdullaah reports that Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab used to say, "Those who wish to exercise their personal opinions are the enemies of the Sunnah. They are too lazy to learn the Sunnah and it escapes their memory even when they do learn it. When questioned, they are too shy to admit that they do not know and therefore use their intellect to challenge the Sunnah. You should beware of such people."
sources: Ibn Abdul Birr in his Jaami (Vol.2 Pg.134).

paras: Hadhrat Umar (RA) also said, "The Sunnah is that which Allaah and His Rasool have determined. You should never make your mistaken opinion a Another narration from Hadhrat Amr bin Dinaar states that when someone asked Hadhrat Umar (RA) whether Allaah guided him in the judgements he passed, he replied, "Do not say that! That was a speciality of Rasulullaah ﷺ
sources: Ibn Abi Haatim and Bayhaqi, as quoted in Kanzul Urnmaal (Vol.5 Pg.241).

paras: Hadhrat Sha'bi narrates that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "Beware of asking, "What is your opinion? What is your opinion?' because those before you were destroyed because they asked, "What is you opinion? What is you opinion?' You should also not judge one thing by another because your feet will then slip after being firm. In addition to this, whenever any of you are asked about something that he does not know, he should say, 'Allaah knows best,' because this constitutes a third of knowledge." '''

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) once said, "Every year is followed by a year that is worse. While no year is essentially worse than another, no nation is essentially worse than another. However, what will happen is that when your Ulema and righteous ones leave the world, such people will come about who will analyse matters using their personal opinions, because of which they will destroy and perforate Islaam."
sources: Tabraani in his Kabeer. Haythami (Vol.1 Pg.180) has commented on the chain of narrators. Ibn Abdul Birr has reported a similar narration in his Jaami (Vol.2 Pg.135).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) said, "The basis (of Islaam and the Shari'ah) is Allaah's Book and the Sunnah of Rasulullaah ﷺ. Whoever says anything else based on his personal opinion, I cannot say whether he will find this amongst his good deeds or his sins."

Hadhrat Ataa narrates from his father that when a Sahabi was questioned about something, he said, "I am too shy before my Rabb to employ my personal opinion in commenting on a matter that affects the Ummah of Muhammad

Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA) narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ sent him to Yemen, Rasulullaah ﷺ asked him, "How will you pass judgement when a case comes beforeyou?" "I shall pass judgement by Allaah's Book," Hadhrat Mu'aadh replied. Rasulullaah ﷺ asked further, "And what if you do not find the solution in the Book of Allaah?" "Then," Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA) said, "I shall judge by the Sunnah of Allaah's Rasool ﷺ Again Rasulullaah ﷺ asked, "And what if you do not find the solution in the Sunnah of Allaah's Rasool ﷺ Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA) replied by saying, "I shall then practise Ijtihaad without compromising on diligence." Rasulullaah ﷺ then placed his hand on Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA)'s chest saying, "All praise belongs to Allaah Who has inspired the envoy of Rasulullaah ﷺ with that which pleases Rasulullaah (l)Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.1 Pg.180) has commented on the chain of narrators.

Hadhrat Muhammad bin Seereen says, "After Rasulullaah ﷺ there was none more concerned about not knowing something than Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) and after Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) there was none more concerned about not knowing something than Hadhrat Umar (RA). When Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) needed to pass a verdict and could not find a verse of the Qur'aan or a narration of Rasulullaah ﷺ that applied directly to the situation, he would say, 'I shall now practise Ijtihaad. Should it be correct, it is from Allaah and if it is wrong, it is my error and I seek Allaah's forgiveness for it."
sources: Abu Dawood, Tirmidhi and Daarmi, as quoted in Mishkaatul Masaabeeh (Pg.316).

paras: Hadhrat Shurayh narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once wrote to him saying, "When a matter presents itself before you, pass your verdict according to the Book of Allaah. If the matter is not mentioned in the Book of Allaah, pass your verdict according to what Rasulullaah ﷺ directed. If such a matter presents itself that is neither in the Book of Allaah, about which Rasulullaah ﷺ has issued no directives, then pass your verdict by that about which the Ulema are unanimous. However, if such a matter presents itself that is neither in the Book of Allaah, about which Rasulullaah ﷺ has issued no directives and about which no scholar has commented, then you have one of two choices. If you prefer to practise Ijtihaad, you may proceed. Otherwise, if you prefer, you may desist from doing so. In my opinion, desisting is the best course for you."

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "When any of you has to pass a verdict, he should pass his verdict according to the Book of Allaah. If the matter is not mentioned in the Book of Allaah, he should pass his verdict as Rasulullaah had done. If such a matter presents itself that is neither in the Book of Allaah, about which Rasulullaah ﷺ has not passed a verdict, then he should pass his verdict as the righteous scholars had done. However, if such a matter presents itself that is neither in the Book of Allaah and about which neither Rasulullaah ﷺ nor the righteous scholars have passed verdicts, he should practise Ijtihaad. He must then be firm on his verdict without being embarrassed about it." Another narration adds that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "He should then practise Ijtihaad and (when stating his verdict, he must) never say 'I think...' or 'I fear that...' because what is Halaal is clear and what is Haraam is also clear. Between the two are doubtful matters and you should forsake that which gives you doubts for that which does

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abu Yazeed reports that when Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas was questioned about anything and the reply was to be found in the Qur'aan, he would state what was in the Qur'aan. If it was not found in the Qur'aan but Rasulullaah ﷺ had spoken about it, he would say what Rasulullaah ﷺ said. If it was not the Qur'aan and Rasulullaah ﷺ had not spoken about it, but Hadhrat Abu (RA) or Hadhrat Umar (RA) had mentioned it, he would say what Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) or Hadhrat Umar said. However, if it was not found in the Qur'aan and if Rasulullaah Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) and Hadhrat Umar (RA) had not spoken about it, he would practise Ijtihaad."
sources: Ibn Abdul Birr in his Jaami (Vol. 2 Pg.57).

paras: Another narration states that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) said, '"When we receive corroboration (to an injunction), we would not equate anything else to it (and would readily practise it)."
sources: Ibn Abdul Birr in his Jaami Bayaanil llm (Vol.2 Pg.57). Ibn Sa'd (Vol. 4 Pg.181) has reported a similar narration.

paras: Hadhrat Masrooq narrates that when he once questioned Hadhrat Ubay bin Ka'b about something, Hadhrat Ubay (RA) asked, "Has it already happened?" When he was informed that it had not happened, he said, 'Then grant us respite until it happens and then when it does, we will be able to practise Ijtihaad."
sources: Ibn Abdul Birr in his Jaami Bayaanil llm (Vol.2 Pg.57).

paras: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Abu Layla says, "I met a hundred and twenty Sahabah (RA) of Rasulullaah ﷺ in the Masjid. When any of them narrated a Hadith, he wished that his brother (another Sahabi) had done it for him and whenever he issued a Fatwaa, he also wished that his brother had done it for him."
sources: Ibn Abdul Birr in his Jaami Bayaanil llm (Vol.2 Pg.58).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "It is only a madman who will immediately issue a Fatwa for everything he is asked." The same statement has been reported from Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) said, "It is only one of three persons who would issue Fataawaa; a man who knows which verses of the'Qur'aan abrogate injunctions of Deen and which have been abrogated, a leader who has no alternative and a pretentious fool."
sources: Ibn Abdul Birr in his Jaami Bayaanil Ilm (Vol. 2 Pg.165). Tabraani has reported a similar narration from Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA), reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol. 1 Pg.183).

paras: Hadhrat Ibn Seereen narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) said to Hadhrat Abu Mas'ood Uqba bin Umar, "I was informed that you issue Fataawaa to people! The person blessed with the privileges (of bear its burden (of issuing Fataawaa)."
sources: Ibn Abdul Birr in his Jaami Bayaanil Ilm (Vol.2 Pg.166).

paras: Another narration staites that Hadhrat Umar also added, "And you are not a governor (so you need not issue Fataawaa). "
sources: Ibn Abdul Birr in his Jaami Bayaanil Ilm (Vol.2 Pg.166).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Minhaal says, "When I questioned Hadhrat Zaid bin Arqam (RA) and Hadhrat Baraa (RA) about selling gold and silver, each one of them told me to ask the other, saying, 'He is better than me and has more knowledge.'" The narration goes on further to discuss trading in gold and silver. Hadhrat Abu Husayn says, "Everyone now issues Fataawaa on matters that had they been posed to Hadhrat Umar (RA), he would have gathered all the veterans of Badr (to consult with before issuing a Fatwaa)."

When Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) was asked who used to issue Fataawaa during the time of Rasulullaah ﷺ, he replied, "Abu Bakr and Umar. I do not know of anyone else." Hadhrat Qaasim bin Muhammad says that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA), Hadhrat Umar, Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) and Hadhrat Ali (RA) used to issue Fataawaa during the time of Rasulullaah ﷺ

Hadhrat Fudhayl bin Abu Abdullaah bin Dinaar narrates from his father that Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA), Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA). Hadhrat Umar and Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) were amongst those who issued Fataawaa during the time of Rasulullaah ﷺ according to what they heard from Rasulullaah ﷺ.
sources: Ibn Sa'd (Vol.4 Pg.157). Ibn Asaakir has reported a similar narration, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaa/ Pg.77).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Attiyya Hamdaani reports that he was once sitting with Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood when a person came to ask him a question. "Have you asked anyone else?" Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) enquired. 'Yes," the man replied, "I have asked Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) The man then informed Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) about Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari's reply. Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) gave a reply that contradicted that of Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) and then left. (When this was brought to the attention of Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) He said, "Do not ask me about anything when this great scholar is in your midst."

Hadhrat Sahl bin Abu Khaythamah reports that during the time of Rasulullaah three Sahabah (RA) from the Muhaajireen and three Sahabah (RA) from the Ansaar were authorised to issue Fataawaa. They were Hadhrat Umar Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA), Hadhrat Ali (RA) (from the Muhaajireen) and Hadhrat Ubay bin Ka'b (RA), Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA) and Hadhrat Zaid bin Thaabit (RA) (from the Ansaar).
sources: Ibn Sa'd (Vol.4 Pg.160). Abu Nu'aym has reported a similar narration in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.129).

paras: Hadhrat Masrooq reports that from amongst the Sahabah (RA) of Rasulullaah those who issued Fataawaa were Hadhrat Umar (RA), Hadhrat Ali Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA), Hadhrat Zaid (bin Thaabit) Hadhrat Ubay bin Ka'b (RA) and Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA).
sources: IbnSa'd(VoI.4Pg.l67).

paras: Hadhrat Qabeesah bin Duayb bin Halhala reports, "During the time of Hadhrat Umar, Hadhrat Zaid bin Thaabit (RA) remained the chief authority of the judiciary of Madinah, as well as the chief authority of issuing Fataawaa, Qiraa'ah and dissolution of estates. He maintained this position during the time of Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) and for as long as Hadhrat Ali (RA) remained in Madinah (as Khalifah before moving the capital to Kufa). Thereafter, he kept the post for a further five years until Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA) became the Khalifah in the year 40 A.H. Even after this, he remained instated in the position until he passed away in the year 45 A.H." '''

Hadhrat Ataa bin Yasaar reports that both Hadhrat Umar (RA) and Hadhrat Uthmaan used to call for Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) (to consult with) and would also consult with the veterans of the Battle of Badr. Until the day he passed away, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) used to issue Fataawaa during the time of Hadhrat Umar (RA) and Hadhrat Uthmaan Hadhrat Ziyaad bin Meenaa narrates that amongst those Sahabah (RA) who issued Fataawaa and narrated Ahadeeth in Madinah were Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA), Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA), Hadhrat Abdullaah Amr bin Al Aas Hadhrat Jaabir bin Abdullaah (RA), Hadhrat Raafi bin Khudayj (RA), Hadhrat Salamah bin Akwa (RA), Hadhrat Abu Waaqid Laythi (RA) and Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Buhaynah (RA). This they continued doing from the time Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) passed away until their deaths. Amongst them, the ones who issued the bulk of the Fataawaa were Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA), Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) and Hadhrat Jaabir bin Abdullaah Hadhrat Qaasim relates, "During the Khilaafah of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA), Hadhrat Umar (RA), Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) and until the time she passed away (may Allaah shower his mercy on her), (my aunt) Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) used to issue Fataawaa by herself. 1 used to stay with her and she showed extreme affection towards me."
sources: IbnSa'd (Vol.4 Pg.l 87).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) said, "Rasulullaah ﷺ left us with so much knowledge that even when a bird fluttered its wings in the sky, it would remind us of something he had taught us."
sources: IbnSa'd(Vol.4Pg.l89).

paras: Another narration adds that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Everything that draws one closer to Jannah and that takes one further from Jahannam has been explained to you (Sahabah (RA)). "
sources: Tabraani. Tabraani has reported a narration similar to that of Ahmad from Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA), which is reported from reliable sources, as confirmed by Haythami (Vol. 8 Pg.264). Ibn Sa'd (Vol.4 Pg.170) has also reported a similar narration.

paras: Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas (RA) says, "I have learnt a thousand similitudes from Rasulullaah ﷺ In a lengthy narration, Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) says, "Whenever they (the Sahabah (RA) disagreed about anything, my father (Hadhrat Abu Bakr would come forth with a Hadith that would satisfy them all and settle the dispute. Therefore, when it was asked where Rasulullaah ﷺ was to be buried, no one could be found who had any relevant knowledge. It was then that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) said, 'I heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say, "Whenever a Nabi passed away, he was buried beneath the place he lay at the time he passed away.' Similarly, when the Sahabah (RA) posed divergent opinions about the inheritance of Rasulullaah ﷺ, they could find none with relevant knowledge. Again it was Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) who said, 'I heard Rasulullaah say, the assembly of Ambiyaa do not leave behind any inheritance. Everything we leave behind is donated as Sadaqah.'"
sources: Ahmad, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.8 Pg.264).
Baghawi, Ibn Asaakir and others, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Utntnaal (Vol.4 Pg.346).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Waa'il narrates that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "If the knowledge of Umar was placed on one pan of a scale and the knowledge of all on earth was placed on the other, the knowledge of Umar would outweigh the rest." Hadhrat A'mash says, "I found it difficult to accept this, so I mentioned it to Ibraheem, who said, 'Why do you find this difficult to accept when I can swear by Allaah that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood said something even more profound than this. He said, 'In my estimation, nine tenths of knowledge left the world with the demise of Umar In a lengthy narration concerning the demise of Hadhrat Umar (RA), Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood stated, "From all of us, it was Umar who possessed the most knowledge about Allaah, who recited the Book of Allaah the most and who had the deepest understanding of Allaah's Deen."
sources: Tabraani, as quoted in Majma'uz Zawaa'id ' (Vol.9 Pg.69).

paras: Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) said, "In comparison to the knowledge of Umar the knowledge of all other people seems like it could be buried in a little hole." A man from Madinah said, "When I was presented before Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab, learned scholars appeared to be little children before him. His understanding and knowledge towered above theirs."
sources: Ibn Sa'd (Vol.4 Pg.153).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Is'haaq narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ got Hadhrat Ali (RA) married to Hadhrat Faatima (RA), she said to Rasulullaah ﷺ, "You have married me to a man whose eyesight is weak and whose stomach is big." Rasulullaah ﷺ responded by saying, "I have married you to him because from all my companions, he was the first to accept Islaam, he has the most knowledge and is the most tolerant."

Another narration states that Rasulullaah ﷺ said to Hadhrat Faatima (RA), "Are you not pleased that 1 have married you to the person who was the first of my Ummah to accept Islaam, is the one with the most knowledge and is the most tolerant?"
sources: Ibn Sa'd (Vol. 4 Pg.153).

paras: Hadhrat Ali (RA) once said, "By Allaah! 1 know precisely about what every verse of the Qur'aan was revealed, where it was revealed and concerning whom it was revealed. My Rabb has blessed me with a perceptive heart and an eloquent tongue."
sources: Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.9 Pg.102) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Musayyib reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) used to seek Allaah's protection against any intricate problem which had to be resolved without the help of Hadhrat Ali (RA).
sources: Tabraani and Ahmad. Haythami (Vol.9 Pg. 101) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Masrooq narrates that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "I know the precise circumstances surrounding the revelation of every chapter of the Qur'aan. If I knew of a person more knowledgeable than myself, I would certainly go to him if a camel or any other conveyance could take me to him." Hadhrat Masrooq says, "I sat in the company of many Sahabah (RA) of Muhammad ﷺ and found them to be like dams. While some dams may quench the thirst of one man, others may quench the thirst of two men, others the thirst often and others will quench the thirst of a hundred men. Then there are oceans that can cater for all the people on earth if they had to settle there. I found Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) to be such an ocean." '" Hadhrat Zaid bin Wahab narrates that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) arrived one day at a place where Hadhrat Umar (RA) was sitting. When he saw Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) approach, Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "He is a coffer filled to the brim with the knowledge and understanding of Deen."

Hadhrat Asad bin Wadaa'ah reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once made mention of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) saying, "He is a coffer filled to the brim with knowledge. I however had to give preference to the people of Qaadisiyyah over myself concerning him (by sending him to teach them rather than keeping him behind with me in Madinah)."
Hadhrat Abul Bakhtari narrates that they once approached Hadhrat Ali (RA) with the request to inform them about the Sahabah (RA) of Rasulullaah ﷺ.

"Which of them would you like to know about?" Hadhrat Ali (RA) asked. "Tell us about Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) they replied. Hadhrat Ali said, "He learnt the Qur'aan and the Sunnah and reached the apex of knowledge. This is sufficient for you to gauge the extent of his knowledge." "Tell us about Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) they asked next. Hadhrat Ali said, "He had been thoroughly dyed in knowledge before coming out of the dye." The men asked further, "Then tell us about Hadhrat Ammaar bin Yaasir Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "He is a Mu'min who remembers well after being reminded about something he had forgotten."
"Now tell us about Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) they asked. Hadhrat Ali (RA)'s reply was-. "Of all the Sahabah (RA), he best knew who the Munaafiqeen were."
When they asked about Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA), Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "He acquired a substantial amount of knowledge but was unable to disseminate it."

The men further asked, "Tell us about Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) Hadhrat Ali said, "He acquired the knowledge of the previous Ambiyaa as well as the knowledge of the final Nabi ﷺ. He is an ocean whose bottom cannot be reached and he is also one of us, the household of Rasulullaah ﷺ "O Ameerul Mu'mineen!" the men then asked, "Now tell us about yourself." Hadhrat Ali said, "It was this that you had intended asking from the outset! Whenever I asked (Rasulullaah ﷺ) anything, I would receive a reply and whenever l remained silent, I would be, informed."
sources: Ibn Sa'd (Vol.4 Pg. 1 65).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "Mu'aadh bin Jabal is certainly an Ummah who was Qaanit and Haneef (one inclined towards the truth and averse to all false creeds). He is (definitely) not from the Mushrikeen." The narrator says, "I thought that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) had perhaps made an error because Allaah says in the Qur'aan.- Ibraheem was certainly an Ummah who was Qaanit and Haneef inclined towards the truth and averse to all false creeds). He was (definitely) not from the Mushrikeen. (Surah Nahl, verse 120-121) However, when Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) repeated his words to me, 1 knew that he meant what he was saying. I therefore remained silent. He then asked, 'Do you know what the meaning of 'Ummah'and 'Qaanit'xsT When I submitted that Allaah knows best, he explained, 'Ummah (in this context) refers to a person who teaches people good things and 'Qaanit' refers to a person who obeys Allaah and His Rasool ﷺ. That is exactly how Mu'aadh bin Jabal was. He taught people everything that was good and was obedient to Allaah and to Allaah's Rasool ﷺ
sources: IbnSa'd(Vol.4Pg.l67).

paras: Hadhrat Masrooq says, "I examined the Sahabah (RA) carefully and found that all their knowledge could be found in six of them; namely Hadhrat Umar (RA), Hadhrat Ali (RA), Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA), Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal, Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) and Hadhrat Zaid bin Thaabit After closely examining these six, I discovered that all their knowledge could be found in Hadhrat Ali (RA) and Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood
sources: Ibn Sa'd (Vol.4 Pg. 176).

paras: Hadhrat Masrooq also said, "When I arrived in Madinah and enquired about the Sahabah (RA), I discovered that amongst those with the most profound knowledge was Hadhrat Zaid bin Thaabit (RA)

Hadhrat Masrooq reports that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) once said, "If Abdullaah bin Abbaas were our age, none of us would be able to equal even a tenth of his knowledge." Another narration adds that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood said, "Abdullaah bin Abbaas is an excellent commentator of the Qur'aan." ''* Hadhrat Mujaahid reports that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) used to be called an ocean because of the great amount of knowledge he possessed.
sources: Ibn Sa'd (Vol.4 Pg. 181).

paras: Hadhrat Layth bin Abu Sulaym says that he once said to Hadhrat Tawoos, "Why have you attached yourself to this youngster (Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas instead of the senior Sahabah (RA) of Rasulullaah ﷺ Hadhrat Tawoos replied, "I have seen seventy Sahabah (RA) who favoured the opinion of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) whenever a difference of opinion arose in any matter."

Hadhrat Aamir the son of Hadhrat Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas (RA) reports that his father said, "I have never seen as quick-witted, as intelligent, as knowledgeable and as tolerant as Abdullaah bin Abbaas. I saw that when an intricate problem arose, Umar bin Khattaab would call for him and say, 'Be prepared! A most complicated problem is coming your way.' Umar would then accept his opinion on the matter even though he would be surrounded by veterans of the Battle of.Badr both from the Muhaajireen and the Ansaar." Hadhrat Abu Zinaad narrates that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) was suffering from high fever when Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab (RA) came to visit him. Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "Your illness has certainly posed a great obstacle to us. Nevertheless it is only from Allaah that we seek help." Hadhrat Talha bin Ubaydullaah (RA) said, "Abdullaah bin Abbaas has been blessed with deep understanding, intelligence and tremendous knowledge. I have not seen Umar bin Khattaab give precedence to any other person's opinion over his." * '

Hadhrat Muhammad the son of Hadhrat Ubay bin Ka'b (RA) says that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas was once present when Hadhrat Ubay bin Ka'b stood up and said, "This youth will soon become the most learned scholar of this Ummah. Together with being blessed with intelligence and deep understanding, Rasulullaah ﷺ also prayed to Allaah to grant him a sound understanding of Deen."
sources: Ibn Sa'd (Vol.4 Pg.181).

paras: Hadhrat Tawoos says, "Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) towered above others in knowledge just as a tall palm tree towers above shorter ones."
sources: IbnSa'd (Vol.4 Pg.185).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Waa'il says, "A friend and I performed Hajj at a time when Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas was the Ameer of Hajj. When he started reciting Surah Noor and commenting on it, my friend remarked, 'Oh Subhaanallaah! What great knowledge is emerging from this man's head! Even the Turks would accept Islaam if they had to hear this.'" Another narration adds that Hadhrat Abu Waa'il himself said, "I have never seen or heard anyone speak as he does! Even the Persians and Romans would accept Islaam if they heard him." Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) relates, "When I went to Umar bin Khattaab one day, he asked me a question that Ya'la bin Umayyah had written to him about from Yemen. After I had given him the answer, Umar remarked, 'I testify that you are certainly most eligible to speak on behalf of Rasulullaah ﷺ's Hadhrat Ataa says, "While some people used to approach Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas to ask about poetry, others went to him to ask about ancestry and there were still others who referred to him to ask about the battles that the Arabs fought and about their history. He was able to give each group of people due attention and gave them detailed replies to their satisfaction."
sources: Haakim (Vol.3 Pg.537).

paras: Hadhrat Ubadullaah bin Abdullaah bin Utba says, "Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas surpassed all other people in his qualities. He excelled others in his knowledge of past events, in the deep understanding with which he gave his opinion to people who consulted with him, in his level of tolerance and in his immense magnanimity. None knew the Ahadeeth of Rasulullaah ﷺ and the verdicts of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA), Hadhrat Umar (RA) and Hadhrat Uthmaan better than he. None gave opinions as deeply thought of as he and there was also none who better knew poetry and Arabic as he did. In addition to all of this, his knowledge was also most profound in the commentary of the Qur'aan, in mathematics and in the laws of inheritance. I have also not seen anyone else as knowledgeable about the past events as he was, nor anyone who gave an opinion more dependable than his when people are most in need of one. Sometimes he would sit all day discussing nothing besides Fiqh, while on other days, he would discuss nothing besides the commentary of the Qur'aan. Then there were days when he sat and discussed only the battles of Rasulullaah while on other days, he discussed only poetry or only the history of the Arabs. 1 have never seen any scholar sit before him without surrendering himself to him. 1 have also seen no one asking him a question without receiving the relevant information from him."

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) says, "I used to remain close to the senior Muhaajireen and Ansaar Sahabah (RA) and ask them about the battles Rasulullaah ﷺ fought and the revelation that pertained to them. Whenever I went to any one of them, they became overjoyed because I am related to Rasulullaah ﷺ. Hadhrat Ubay bin Ka'b (RA) was one of the Sahabah (RA) with the soundest knowledge. When I asked him one day about the Surahs that were revealed in Madinah, he informed me that twenty-seven Surahs were revealed in Madinah and all the rest in Makkah."
sources: Ibn Sa'd (Vol.4 Pg.186).

paras: Hadhrat Ikrama says, "I heard Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas (RA) say, 'From all of us, it is Abdullaah bin Abbaas who has the most knowledge of the previous scriptures and also understands best those matters that the Qur'aan and Ahadeeth are not explicit about.' When I informed Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas about what Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas (RA) had said, he remarked, 'He himself has tremendous knowledge because he used to ask Rasulullaah ﷺ about matters that were Halaal and Haraam.'"
sources: IbnSa'd(Vol.4Pg.l86).

paras: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) was once looking at a group of people gathered around Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) during the days of Hajj, asking him about the rites of Hajj. She remarked, "Of those (Sahabah (RA)) still alive, he knows the rites of Hajj best." When the news of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA)'s death reached Hadhrat Jaabir, he hit his one hand on the other and said, "The most knowledgeable and most tolerant of all people has passed away. By his demise, this Ummah has been afflicted with a calamity that can never be redressed." Upon the demise of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA), Hadhrat Raafi bin Khudayj remarked, "All the people between the East and the West were dependent on the one who has passed away today for their knowledge." Hadhrat Abu Kulthoom narrates that when Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) was buried, Hadhrat Ibn Hanafiyyah said, "Today the sage of this Ummah has passed away." ' '
sources: IbnSa'd(Vol.4Pg,184).

paras: Hadhrat Amr bin Dinaar says, "Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) was regarded as one of the young Fuqahaa."
sources: Ibn Sa'd (Vol.4 Pg. 187).

paras: Hadhrat Khaalid bin Ma'daan says, "From amongst the Sahabah (RA) of Rasulullaah ﷺ, there are none left in Shaam whose knowledge is more dependable, who have a deeper understanding and who are more beloved to the people than Hadhrat Ubaadah bin Saamit (RA) and Hadhrat Shaddaad bin Aws
sources: IbnSa'd (Vol.4 Pg.188).

paras: Hadhrat Handhla bin Sufyaan reports from his teachers that none had a better understanding of the Deen than Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA)
sources: Ibn Sa'd (Vol.4 Pg.188).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Za'eeza'a who was Marwaan bin Hakam's scribe reports, "Marwaan once summoned Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) and, seating me behind his chair, he started questioning Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) as I wrote everything down. After a complete year had passed, Marwaan again sent for Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah and, seating him behind a screen, started asking him the same questions. Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) replied to the questions just as he did the previous year without adding, deleting or even misplacing a single word."
sources: Haakim (Vol. 3 Pg.510), reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Dhahabi.

paras: Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) says, "Whenever the Sahabah (RA) of Rasulullaah ﷺ had doubts about anything, they referred it to Hadhrat Aa'isha and always found the answer with her." ' '
Hadhrat Qabeesah bin Dhuwayb says, "Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) was one of the most knowledgeable personalities and even the senior Sahabah (RA) of Rasulullaah ﷺ consulted with her."
sources: IbnSa'd(Vol.4Pg,189).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Salamah says, "I have not seen anyone with more knowledge of the Sunnah practices of Rasulullaah ﷺ than Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) I have also not seen anyone offer a better opinion when an opinion was sought and seen no one with more knowledge of the circumstances surrounding the revelation of any verse or with more knowledge of the laws of inheritance."

When someone asked Hadhrat Masrooq whether Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) was proficient in the laws of inheritance, he replied, "I swear by the Being Who controls my life that she certainly was! In fact, 1 saw the senior Sahabah (RA) of Rasulullaah ﷺ ask her about inheritance."
sources: Ibn Sa'd (Vol.4Pg.r89).

paras: Hadhrat Mahmood bin Labeed says, "Although all the pure wives of Rasulullaah knew many Ahadeeth, none knew as much as Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) and Hadhrat Ummu Salamah (RA). In fact, Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) used to issue Fataawaa during the period of Hadhrat Umar (RA) and Hadhrat Uthmaan This she continued doing until she passed away. May Allaah shower His mercy on her. Senior Sahabah (RA) of Rasulullaah ﷺ such as Hadhrat Umar arid Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) after him used to send messengers to her to ask about Sunnah practices."
sources: IbnSa'd (Vol.4 Pg. 189).

paras: Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA) said, "I have never seen a speaker as well-spoken, as eloquent and as intelligent as Aa'isha Hadhrat Urwa (RA) says, "I have not seen a woman as knowledgeable in medicine, Fiqh and poetry as Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) Hadhrat Urwa (RA) once said to (his aunt) Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA), "I am more astonished about you the more I think about you! When I find you to be one of those most proficient in Islaamic jurisprudence, I ask myself what was there to prevent you from being such when you were the wife of Rasulullaah ﷺ and the daughter of Abu Bakr Then when I find you to be one of those most knowledgeable about the history of the Arabs and about their lineage and poetry, I ask myself what was there to prevent you from being such when your father knew most about the Quraysh? However, what surprises me is that I also find you to be most proficient in medicine. Where did you learn this from?" Hadhrat Aa'isha held Hadhrat Urwa (RA)'s hand and said, "When Rasulullaah illness worsened, Arab and non-Arab physicians sent (many medicines and prescriptions) for him, from which I learnt medicine." Another narration states that she said, "When I used these to treat Rasulullaah ﷺ, I learnt all about it."
sources: Tabraani, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.9 Pg.243).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) once said to his students, "Be people who are the fountainheads of knowledge, who are beacons of guidance, who spend most of the time at home, who are lanterns of the night, whose hearts remain fresh and young and who wear old clothes. In this manner, you will be known to the inhabitants of the heavens while remaining anonymous to the inhabitants of earth." ^ A similar narration from Hadhrat Ali (RA) states, "In this manner, you will be known to the inhabitants of the heavens while the inhabitants of earth will rave about you."
sources: Tabraani, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.9 Pg.242).

paras: Hadhrat Wahab bin Munabbih narrates that when Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas was informed that some people were debating about predestination at Baab Bani Sahm, he quickly got up and, handing his staff over to Hadhrat Ikrama, he placed one hand on the staff and the other on Hadhrat Tawoos. When he reached the group, they made way for him and welcomed him. Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) however did nor sit down and asked them to inform him of their lineage so that he may recognise who they were. When they did so, he addressed them saying, "Do you not know that Allaah has servants whom fear for Him has driven them to silence even though they are neither handicapped nor dumb? On the contrary, they are people who are Ulema, orators and people of high status. They are well acquainted with the way Allaah deals with sinners but whenever they think of the greatness of Allaah, they lose their minds, their hearts are torn apart and their tongues stop functioning. When they recover from this state, they hasten to perform good deeds that will purify them. While they regard themselves as people who neglect their duties to Allaah, they are really the intelligent ones with the most strength (to do good). Although they regard themselves as wrong-doers and sinners, they are really righteous and innocent. What distinguishes them is they never regard anything as being too much to do for Allaah, they are never satisfied to do only a little for Him and they are never too proud of the deeds they do for Him. Wherever you meet them, they will be filled with concern, in awe of Allaah and ever fearing (that they should not displease) Him." Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) then left and returned to his gathering.
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.325).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "If the men of knowledge would safeguard their knowledge and give it only to those who are worthy, they would lead the people of their times. However, they have handed it over to men of this world only to receive a portion of the world and have therefore fallen in the eyes of these people. I have heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say, 'Whoever narrows all his worries to the one worry for the Aakhirah, Allaah will take care of all his other worries. On the other hand, whoever has been confounded by the worries of this world, Allaah cares not in which valley he destroys himself." Hadhrat Sufyaan bin Uyaynah reports that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) said, "if the bearers of knowledge uphold it as it ought to be upheld and in a befitting manner, Allaah, His angels and the pious ones will love them. In addition to this, people will stand in awe of them. However, they seek the wealth of this world with their knowledge, because of which Allaah detests them and they have no status in the eyes of the people." '
sources: Ibn Abdul Birr in his Jaami (Vol. 1 Pg.188).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "What will happen to you when such a calamity overtakes you because of which your youngsters start to age, your elders grow older and such practices are regarded as being Sunnah that when an attempt is made to change them, people will say (about the act is truly Sunnah), This is something very strange!"' When someone asked Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood when such a time would come, he replied, "When the trustworthy ones amongst you will be few while your leaders will be plenty, when the Fuqahaa amongst you will be few while those reciting the Qur'aan will be plenty, when the knowledge of Deen will be sought for motives other than the benefit of Deen and when worldly gain will be the motivation behind carrying out acts of the Aakhirah."

Another narration states that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "When a fabricated Sunnah becomes such a norm in society, when an effort is made to change it, people will say, 'The Sunnah has been changed!'" The narration also adds that the time will be "when your Fuqahaa will be few and your leaders will hoard wealth."
sources: Abdur Razzaaq, as quoted in Targheeb wat Tarheeb (Vol.1 Pg.82). Ibn Abdul Birr has reported a similar narration in his Jaami (Vol.1 Pg.188).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) said, "You should understand well that these Ahadeeth ought to be learnt solely for the pleasure of Allaah. When a person learns them solely for worldly gain, he will not even smell the fragrance of Jannah. "

Hadhrat Umar (RA) once asked Hadhrat Ka'b (who was learned in the previous scriptures), "What can remove knowledge from the hearts of Ulema after they have studied and memorised it?" Hadhrat Ka'b replied, "It will be greed and asking people for one's needs that will remove it." When Hadhrat Ali (RA) once spoke about certain tribulations that will occur towards the end of time, Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked, "When will this occur, O Ali?" Hadhrat Ali (RA) replied, "When the knowledge of Deen will be sought for motives other than the benefit of Deen, when knowledge will be sought for reasons other than to practise and when worldly gain will be the motivation behind carrying out acts of the Aakhirah."
sources: Ibn Abdul Birr in his Jaami (Vol. 1 Pg. 1 87).
Ibn Abdul Birr in his Jaami (Vol.2 Pg.6).
Abdur Razzaaq, as quoted in Targheeb wat Tarheeb (Vol.1 Pg.82).

paras: Hadhrat Umar (RA) once addressed the people saying, "I fear two people for you, the person who misinterprets the Qur'aan and a person who is vying with his brother for kingdom."
sources: Ibn Abdul Birr in his Jaami (Vol.2 Pg.194). Ibn Abi Shaybah has reported a similar narration, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.5 Pg.233).

paras: Hadhrat Hasan narrates that when a delegation from Basrah that included Hadhrat Ahnaf bin Qais (RA) came to Hadhrat Umar (RA), he granted them all leave, except for Hadhrat Ahnaf (RA), whom he kept back for an entire year.

Thereafter, Hadhrat Umar (RA) said to Hadhrat Ahnaf (RA), "Do you know why I kept you back? Rasulullaah ﷺ warned us against well-spoken hypocrites and I feared that you should not be one. Inshaa Allaah, (I am now confident that) you are not one of them."
sources: Ibn Sa'd and Abu Ya'Ia.

paras: Hadhrat Abu Uthmaan Nahdi reports that he heard Hadhrat Umar (RA) say from the pulpit, "Beware of the hypocritical Aalim." "How will a hypocrite become an Aalim?" the people asked. Hadhrat Umar (RA) replied, "He will be a person who speaks what is right but then does what is wrong."
sources: Bayhaqi and Ibn Najjaar.

paras: Hadhrat Umar (RA) also said, "We always maintained that the one to destroy this Ummah will be a hypocrite with an educated tongue."
sources: Firyaabi, Abu Ya'la, Nasr and Ibn Asaakir, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal ' (Vol.5 Pg.232).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Uthmaan Nahdi reports that he heard Hadhrat Umar (RA) say from the pulpit, "What I fear most for this Ummah is the hypocritical Aalim."
"How will a hypocrite be an Aalim, O Ameerul Mu'mineen?" the people asked.
Hadhrat Umar (RA) replied, "He will be a person whose tongue will be educated but whose heart and actions will be ignorant."
